records.description: The Study in India (SII) programme is a flagship project of the Government of India executed by the Ministry of Education, and the SII Scholarship is the financial-assistance component attached to it. Financial aid takes the form of institute-driven tuition fee waivers or scholarships decided at each partner institute's discretion, ranging from 10% to 100% of tuition depending on the applicant's prior academic scores. Students register on the Study in India portal, submit applications to partner institutes, and the resulting waiver appears on their student dashboard alongside the allotted institute and course. There is no central award amount and no single application deadline; eligibility and concessions vary institute by institute.

official_details.description: Study in India is a Government of India programme executed by the Ministry of Education that helps international students apply to Indian higher education institutions. Its scholarship component is an institute-driven tuition fee waiver of 10% to 100%, awarded at the discretion of each partner institute according to the applicant's prior academic scores. Students register once on the portal, submit applications to multiple institutes, and the resulting 'Partner Institute Scholarship' is shown on their dashboard with the allotted course.
official_details.program_type: Government scholarship / tuition fee waiver administered through the Study in India portal
official_details.coverage: Partial tuition-only coverage of 10% to 100%, awarded per academic year by the partner institute; no living cost, travel or stipend component is published for the SII Scholarship.

Have your passport valid for the full course duration

Compile academic transcripts and mark sheets for upload
Do not apply to undergraduate Medicine or related programmes
Check whether you are an NRI, because NRI status disqualifies you from the SII Scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an NRI, which the FAQ states makes the applicant ineligible for the SII Scholarship
Choosing a partner institute whose individual entry criteria you do not meet, since each institute sets its own conditions
Missing the institute-specific admission window even though the portal registration is open
Applying to undergraduate Medicine or related programmes, which are not offered
Submitting fewer than 3 institute preferences during choice filling
Expecting a full tuition waiver when the institute may award as little as 10%

Student visa fees, quoted by the FAQ as generally USD 14 to USD 118 depending on nationality
Airfare to India
Medical insurance, which the FAQ notes is not included with the student visa

alerts.message: NRIs may join the Study in India programme but the official FAQ states they are not eligible for the SII Scholarship.

records.eligibility_summary: For privately-financed international students enrolled full-time in Japan with excellent academic and character records who are facing financial difficulties. A privately-financed student is one enrolled in a Japanese institution who is not a grantee of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any Foreign Government Scholarship and who holds 'Student' residence status. Candidates must not exceed a monthly allowance of 90,000 yen excluding tuition and enrollment fees, and any financial supporter in Japan must earn under 5 million yen per year.

Enrolled full-time in a preparatory Japanese language program in an undergraduate school or junior college in Japan
Enrolled full-time in a university preparatory course in Japan with the objective of entering university
Enrolled in a Japanese language institute with the objective of advancing to higher education in Japan
Excellent academic and character records and facing financial difficulties
Monthly allowance excluding enrollment fee and tuition must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen

JASSO states there are currently no universities or Japanese language institutes suspended from applying.
records.description: The Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a JASSO programme for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are already enrolled at a Japanese educational institution and are facing financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of 48,000 yen at graduate or undergraduate level and 30,000 yen at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months from April or 6 months from October. Applications are made through the enrolled institution rather than directly to JASSO, so timing and eligibility are institution-specific.

records.description: The POSCO Global Scholarship in Korea is the inbound component of the POSCO Global Scholarship operated by the POSCO TJ Park Foundation, and it is described by the Foundation as 'The Global Future Leaders Scholarship Program'. It funds non-Korean nationals admitted to Master's or doctoral programmes at designated Korean graduate schools, who must be recommended by their admitting institution. Master's students receive full tuition for four semesters plus living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month for 22 months, while doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral students receive full tuition for six semesters plus the same monthly living allowance for 36 months. A one-off KRW 1,000,000 settlement fee, National Health Insurance premiums and Korean language and cultural programmes are also provided.

records.description: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships support researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers. records.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.

records.name: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks
records.deadline: The 2026 call is open. Official indicative timeline: '28 May 2026: launch of the call for proposals (TBC)' and '24 November 2026: deadline for submitting proposals (TBC)'.
records.application_period: The 2026 call runs from 28 May 2026 to 24 November 2026, with results notified in April 2027 and the first EU-funded projects starting in August 2027. Doctoral candidates do not apply to the Commission; they apply to funded Doctoral Network projects through the vacancies those projects advertise, including on EURAXESS.

records.eligibility_summary: Doctoral Networks are applied for by international consortia, not by individual candidates. A consortium must include at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, with at least one established in an EU Member State; organisations from any country in the world may join on top of that minimum, and specific conditions apply to Industrial and Joint Doctorates. Recruited doctoral candidates must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment, may be of any nationality, must be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project, must spend at least 50% of their time outside academia for Industrial Doctorates, and must comply with the mobility rule of no more than 12 months in the recruiting organisation's country in the 36 months before recruitment.

records.notes: This is a doctoral training programme funding salaried research positions, not a tuition scholarship, so there is no tuition component. The 2026 call carries an indicative budget of EUR 593.034 million (TBC) for the whole call, which is not a per-fellowship amount. As from 2022, resubmission restrictions apply to applications scoring below 80% the previous year. Candidates seeking PhD positions are directed to the EURAXESS vacancy list, which is updated daily.
records.description: MSCA Doctoral Networks implement doctoral programmes through international, intersectoral partnerships of universities, research institutions, businesses including SMEs and other socio-economic actors, in order to train highly skilled doctoral candidates. Besides standard Doctoral Networks, the action promotes Industrial Doctorates, which place PhD candidates largely outside academia, and Joint Doctorates, which lead to a joint or multiple doctoral degrees. Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate, who must not already hold a doctoral degree at recruitment, may be of any nationality and is funded through a living allowance, mobility allowance and applicable family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. The 2026 call is currently open, having launched on 28 May 2026 with a deadline of 24 November 2026.

official_details.description: MSCA Doctoral Networks implement doctoral programmes through partnerships of universities, research institutions and infrastructures, businesses including SMEs, and other socio-economic actors from different countries across Europe and beyond, in order to train highly skilled doctoral candidates. Alongside standard networks, the action offers incentives for Industrial Doctorates, where candidates work largely outside academia, and Joint Doctorates leading to joint or multiple doctoral degrees. A consortium must include at least three independent legal entities in different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries, with at least one in an EU Member State. Recruited candidates must not already hold a doctoral degree, may be of any nationality and receive a living allowance, a mobility allowance and applicable family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. The 2026 call opened on 28 May 2026 and closes on 24 November 2026.

records.eligibility_summary: Open to nationals of 26 EU Member States who want to study at Master's level in France. Applicants must be at least 18 at the start of the mobility, must not already hold a master's degree from any country, must be admitted to a Master 1 or Master 2 programme at a French institution, must not hold a French higher education degree or be currently registered in France for a higher education degree, and must not be receiving an Erasmus+, AUF or other French ministry scholarship. Students of French nationality, including bi-nationals, are not eligible.

records.program_type: Government scholarship of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, managed by Campus France
records.best_fit: EU nationals (excluding French nationals) admitted to a French Master 1 or Master 2 programme in one of the seven eligible fields.
records.notes: Eligible fields of study are Culture and Heritage; Education and Pedagogy; French Language and Civilization, Foreign Languages and Civilizations and European Studies; Law and political sciences; Health; Environmental Sciences; and Computer Science and Digital. The scholarship is awarded on academic excellence and in line with the strategic priorities of the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. Applications are pre-selected by the college relations teams at the French embassies and then assessed within the Ministry by collaboration specialists from the eligible fields. The scholarship is maintained only for periods spent in France, except in specified internship or exchange cases, and signing an apprenticeship or professional contract automatically terminates it.
records.description: The France Excellence Europa scholarship programme, developed by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France, lets students from 26 EU Member States study at Master's level at a French higher education institution. It pays a semi-annual maintenance allowance of EUR 6,850 and a one-off installation allowance of EUR 1,700, exempts holders from administrative registration fees for a national degree in public institutions and from the CVEC, and arranges social protection and complementary health insurance. The award lasts up to 12 months for a Master 2 enrolment and up to 24 months for a Master 1 enrolment, and applications are sent electronically to the French Embassy in the applicant's country of nationality.

official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Mixed and narrower than it looks. The memorandum states: 'For students enrolled in public institutions under the Ministry of Higher Education, please recall that the status of French government scholarship recipients exempts them from the payment of administrative registration fees for a national degree. In other situations, course fees are not covered by the France Excellence Europa program.' The programme page likewise states 'The "France Excellence Europa" scholarship does not cover course fees'. So only the administrative registration fee for a national degree at a public institution is exempted; course fees themselves are not covered.

official_details.description: The France Excellence Europa scholarship programme, developed by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and managed by Campus France, funds Master 1 and Master 2 study in France for nationals of 26 EU Member States. Holders receive a semi-annual allowance of EUR 6,850 and an installation allowance of EUR 1,700, are exempted from administrative registration fees for a national degree in public institutions and from the CVEC, and receive social protection cover and complementary health insurance arranged by Campus France. The award runs for up to 12 months at Master 2 and up to 24 months at Master 1, the stay must begin between 1 September and 31 December of the year of award, and applications go to the French Embassy in the applicant's country of nationality.

records.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.

records.description: The Swedish Institute, a Swedish government agency, awards fully funded scholarships for master's studies in Sweden to global professionals from 34 eligible countries. The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals covers full tuition fees, a monthly living-expense allowance of SEK 12,000 and a one-time travel grant, and runs once a year for master's studies starting in the autumn semester. The Swedish Institute also runs the Pioneering Women in STEM scholarship, awarded through the same single application. The 2026/2027 call closed on 25 February 2026 and recipients were announced on 23 April 2026; the next call is expected to be published on si.se in mid-November 2026.
records.deadline: "9-25 February 2026: Application portal for the SI Scholarships is open for two weeks. Please note that the portal closes at 14:59 CET on the final day." For the 2026/2027 academic year; the next cycle's dates are not yet published.
records.application_period: Annual cycle. For academic year 2026/2027: university applications 16 October 2025 - 15 January 2026, SI scholarship portal 9-25 February 2026, results 23 April 2026.
records.english_requirement: The application must be completed in English: "You must complete your application in English."
requirements: Citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries (residency in that country not required)
Liability to pay tuition fees to Swedish universities
Admitted or conditionally admitted to an SI-eligible master's programme on the University Admissions results day
Demonstrated work experience, certified on SI's template
Demonstrated leadership experience from a current or previous employer, or civil society engagement
Not a previous holder of a Swedish Institute scholarship for studies in Sweden
Not a Swedish or EU/EEA citizen, and no Swedish permanent residence or work/family-based permit
application_method: Apply for an eligible master's programme at University Admissions (universityadmissions.se) and pay the application fee
Save the eight-digit University Admissions application number
Submit one SI scholarship application at apply-scholarships.si.se listing up to four eligible programmes
Keep the admissions offer unchanged; reserves and late admissions are not eligible
records.selection_notes: SI scores applications against the aim of the programme and the government strategy it reports to, prioritises work and leadership experience relevant to the chosen field, aims for gender balance and country spread, and states it has no quotas for specific countries, fields of study or universities.
records.program_type: Government scholarship (Swedish Institute public agency), master's level
benefits: Full tuition fee coverage, paid directly by SI to the Swedish university each semester
Monthly allowance of SEK 12,000 to cover living expenses throughout the study period
One-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine)
Membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals (NFGP)
Membership of the Sweden Alumni Network after the scholarship period
coverage: Full tuition fees
Living expenses (SEK 12,000 per month)
One-time travel grant (SEK 15,000; SEK 10,000 for six listed countries)

official_details.description: The Swedish Institute (SI) offers fully funded scholarships for master's studies in Sweden to global professionals from a selection of 34 countries. The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is open for applications once every year for master's studies beginning in the autumn semester and requires citizenship of an eligible country, application to an eligible master's programme, liability to pay tuition fees, work experience and leadership experience. records.name: MOE Taiwan Scholarship Program (Taiwan Scholarship)
records.official_source: Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
records.duration: 4 years for a bachelor's programme, 2 years for a master's programme, 4 years for a doctoral programme; total scholarship period cannot exceed five years
records.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program is administered by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) for outstanding foreign students, and is distinct from the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship and the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship. It pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 each semester and a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 for bachelor's students and NTD 20,000 for master's and doctoral students. Applications go to the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for the applicant's country and a separate application to a Taiwanese university is also required. The 2026 round ran from 1 February to 31 March 2026 and has closed; the next round falls in early 2027.
records.deadline: "In principle, the application period is from February 1 to March 31 each year. The actual application period for each local Taiwan Representative Office will be detailed in its publicly available information." Each university or college also sets its own admission deadline.
records.application_period: Annual cycle, in principle 1 February to 31 March, with the actual window set by each Taiwan Representative Office; the scholarship year runs 1 September to 31 August
records.english_requirement: For a programme not completely taught in English, a TOCFL result or certificate at Level 3 or above is required; for a programme completely taught in English, an official TOEFL or IELTS score report, an English programme graduation diploma, or an official university letter confirming the programme is taught in English.
requirements: Be a foreign national holding at least a secondary school graduation diploma, or post-secondary degree(s)
Show excellent academic performance and be of good moral character
Submit the scholarship application to the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for the applicant's country
Apply separately for admission to a university or college in Taiwan within that institution's own deadline
Sign the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Obtain a health certificate meeting the programme's required items
application_method: Contact the local Taiwan Representative Office for the country-specific application form and deadline
Submit the scholarship application and required documents to that Representative Office
Apply separately for admission to the intended university or college in Taiwan
records.selection_notes: Selection is delegated by the MOE to the local Taiwan Representative Offices, which may work with local government agencies, universities and colleges and cultural institutions. Each Representative Office publishes the number of scholarships, selection criteria, procedure and time schedule in Chinese and the local language by 31 January each year. Recipients must sign the Terms of Agreement; the scholarship may be suspended or revoked.
records.program_type: Government scholarship (Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan))
records.best_fit: Foreign nationals with a strong academic record seeking a degree programme in Taiwan who can also secure university admission within that university's own deadline
coverage: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 each semester; any excess must be paid by the student
Monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 (bachelor's) or NTD 20,000 (master's and doctoral)
Discounts on outstanding tuition and miscellaneous expenses offered by some universities
benefits: Tuition and miscellaneous expense payment of up to NTD 40,000 per semester
Monthly living allowance
University tuition and miscellaneous expense discounts for recipients
Permission to apply for a working permit of up to 20 hours per week, maximum six months per semester
records.eligibility_summary: Foreign nationals with at least a secondary school diploma and excellent academic record and good moral character, excluding Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao students, students already studying at the same level in Taiwan, exchange or dual-degree students, previous holders of a Taiwan Scholarship for five years or more, and anyone whose Taiwan Scholarship or Huayu Enrichment Scholarship was revoked.
eligibility: Foreign national with at least a secondary school graduation diploma, or post-secondary degree(s)
Excellent academic record and good character
Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao students are not eligible
Not already holding student status, or registered to begin studies, at a Taiwanese university or college, unless completing a degree and graduating that year
Not already studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level as the one applied for
Not an exchange or dual/joint degree student admitted under a cooperation agreement
Has not held a Taiwan Scholarship for a total of five years
Has never had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked
Has not received another scholarship or subsidy from a Taiwan government agency or a Taiwanese institution, excluding university discounts that top up the scholarship's tuition payment
required_documents: Taiwan Scholarship Application Form (country-specific, from the Taiwan Representative Office)
Proof of nationality, such as a passport
Photocopy of the highest degree diploma and academic transcripts, translated into Chinese or English and authenticated if not originally in those languages
Proof of having applied to a university or college in Taiwan for the current academic year
TOCFL Level 3 or above, or TOEFL/IELTS score report, or English programme graduation diploma, depending on the language of the programme
Two letters of reference from a principal, college or university president, professors or supervisors
Signed MOE Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Health certificate meeting the programme's required items (Form B)
records.notes: Do not confuse this award with the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship, which is limited to countries with diplomatic relations or friendly relations recognised by MOFA and provides one-way economy-class air tickets, or with the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, which has no tuition component. The MOE Taiwan Scholarship itself provides no air ticket.

official_details.application_cycle: 2026 round ran 1 February to 31 March 2026 and has closed; the 2027 round is expected to open in February 2027 on the same annual pattern
official_details.deadline_central_display: "In principle, the application period is from February 1 to March 31 each year"; each Taiwan Representative Office publishes its own actual application period
official_details.deadline_note: The MOE Scholarship Guidelines set a principle application window of 1 February to 31 March each year and delegate the actual window to the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for the applicant. Each Taiwanese university or college also sets its own admission deadline, which can fall earlier. No exact date for the 2027 round was published on the pages read on 2026-10-04.
official_details.status_note: The 2026 application window has closed. The programme is annual and the next window falls in the first quarter of 2027; the exact dates are published by each Taiwan Representative Office by 31 January each year.
official_details.funding_duration: One scholarship year from 1 September to 31 August; total scholarship period may not exceed five years

If these exceed a total amount of NTD40,000, the remaining amount must be paid to the university/college by the student." Some universities also give recipients a discount on the outstanding amount.
official_details.funding_label: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 each semester plus a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 (bachelor's) or NTD 20,000 (master's and doctoral); tuition is capped, the student pays any excess, and no air ticket is provided
benefits: Tuition and miscellaneous expense payment of up to NTD 40,000 each semester
Monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 for bachelor's and NTD 20,000 for master's and doctoral study

eligibility: Foreign national with at least a secondary school graduation diploma, or post-secondary degree(s)
Excellent academic record and good moral character
Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao students excluded
Not already studying at the same level in Taiwan, nor an exchange or dual/joint degree student

official_details.international_eligibility: Open to foreign nationals with a secondary school diploma or post-secondary degree and an excellent academic record, subject to the exclusions listed by the MOE

official_details.english_requirement: TOCFL at Level 3 or above for programmes not completely taught in English; TOEFL or IELTS official score report, an English programme graduation diploma, or an official university letter for programmes completely taught in English

Good moral character

award_holder_conditions: Sign the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Maintain student status at a Taiwanese university or college

supplements_or_initiatives: University tuition and miscellaneous expense discounts for scholarship recipients
MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship - a separate scholarship for Mandarin study, no tuition component

official_details.description: The MOE Taiwan Scholarship Program, administered by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan), encourages outstanding foreign students to undertake degree studies in Taiwan. It pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 each semester and a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 for bachelor's or NTD 20,000 for master's and doctoral students. The scholarship year runs from 1 September to 31 August, with duration of 4 years for bachelor's, 2 years for master's and 4 years for doctoral programmes, capped at five years in total. Applications must be lodged with the Taiwan Representative Office for the applicant's country, and admission to a university or college in Taiwan must be secured separately.
official_details.program_type: Government scholarship
official_details.coverage: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NTD 40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance; no air ticket and no full tuition guarantee where fees exceed the cap

application_readiness_checklist: Find the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for your country and read its own published deadline
Prepare the country-specific Taiwan Scholarship Application Form
Apply to your Taiwanese university within that university's own deadline, which can be earlier than the scholarship deadline
Get documents not in Chinese or English translated and authenticated
Take the TOCFL at Level 3 or above if your programme is not fully taught in English, or obtain TOEFL/IELTS results for an English-taught programme
Collect two letters of reference from a principal, president, professor or supervisor
Sign the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Terms of Agreement
Complete the health certificate items (Form B)
common_rejection_risks: Missing the Representative Office's deadline, which differs from the 1-31 March principle window
Missing the university's own admission deadline, which the scholarship cannot override
Applying for a programme not on the MOE English-taught list without an official university confirmation letter
Failing to sign the Terms of Agreement
Having received another Taiwan government or institutional scholarship or subsidy
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses above the NTD 40,000 per semester cap, unless a participating university offers a discount
Air travel, which the MOE Taiwan Scholarship does not cover
Any other costs beyond the stated tuition payment and monthly living allowance
document_audit: Translations of non-Chinese/non-English documents must be authenticated
Reference letters must come from a principal, college or university president, professor or supervisor
The language certificate type must match the language of the programme you apply to

records.name: Singapore International Graduate Award (SINGA)
records.official_source: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.description: SINGA was the Singapore International Graduate Award, a PhD research award offered by A*STAR in collaboration with Singapore universities. Its dedicated A*STAR web pages no longer exist: every /talent/for-graduate-studies/... SINGA URL and the stored scholarship URL return HTTP 404 after an A*STAR site rebuild. As of 2026-10-04 the live A*STAR Graduate Academy scholarships hub lists the A*STAR Graduate Scholarship, the National Science Scholarship (BS-PhD and PhD) and the two A*STAR International Fellowships, but no SINGA entry. SINGA funding amounts, intakes and deadlines therefore cannot be confirmed from the awarding body and are left null; a human should decide whether this row is merged into the National Science Scholarship (PhD) or retired.

records.application_period: Not published on the awarding body's live site

That portal states applications are no longer accepted there and directs users to the individual scholarship websites, none of which is SINGA.

records.official_source: OeAD (Agentur für Bildung und Internationalisierung), Austria
records.description: The OeAD, Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation, administers a large set of scholarship and grant programmes for students and researchers coming to Austria, financed mainly by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Women, Science and Research. Funding is not a single award: each programme has its own call, target group, duration, amount and deadline, and the calls are listed in the Austrian Database for Scholarships and Research Grants at www.grants.at. Incoming programmes include the Ernst Mach Grant for researchers worldwide, the Ernst Mach Grant for study at an Austrian University of Applied Sciences, the Ernst Mach Follow-up Grant, the Ernst Mach Grant - ASEA-UNINET, the Franz Werfel Fellowship and the Indonesia-Austria Scholarship Programme. Several calls for the 2027/2028 academic year are still open as of October 2026, with the earliest closing date on 1 December 2026.
records.deadline: Deadlines are set per programme. For the 2027/2028 academic year the OeAD lists: Ernst Mach Grant worldwide - 1 December 2026; Ernst Mach Grant for an Austrian University of Applied Sciences - 1 February 2027; Ernst Mach Follow-up Grant - 1 February 2027; Ernst Mach Grant ASEA-UNINET - 1 March 2027; Franz Werfel Fellowship - 1 March 2027 and 15 September 2027.
records.application_period: Programme-specific. Calls for academic year 2027/2028 are open now, with deadlines from 1 December 2026 to 15 September 2027

records.notes: This row bundles many separate OeAD programmes rather than one award. Applicants must pick a specific call on grants.at. OeAD project support is described by the agency as funding "primarily ... accommodation and travel expenses", so full tuition funding must not be assumed. A separate BMFWF press release stated that the 2026/27 incoming programmes were worth EUR 15 million in total, which is an aggregate programme budget and not a per-scholarship amount.

records.duration: Four years of full-time undergraduate study
records.description: The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students and one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. It covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years and is tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry undergraduate programmes. Around 37 scholars are named each year from a pool representing 188 countries, with more than CAD 12 million of funding in 2024. Candidates must be nominated by their secondary school, which can nominate only one student per year, and must also apply for admission to the University of Toronto through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre. The scholarship is restricted to the applicant's top-choice programme at the time scholarship decisions are made.

records.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State fellowship, administered by the Institute of International Education, for mid-career professionals from eligible countries. It is a non-degree program: fellows may take academic coursework at a U.S. host university but do not earn a degree. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness insurance, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, international and programme-event air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applications go through each applicant's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section, so deadlines vary by country and nominations must reach IIE by mid-September.

official_details.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education. It is a non-degree, ten-month program for mid-career professionals who hold an undergraduate degree, have at least five years of full-time professional experience, and show leadership and public service. Fellows are assigned to one of the host institutions, study without a degree requirement, and complete a six-week Professional Affiliation. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness coverage, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applicants apply through their country's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy, whose internal deadlines are published locally.

official_details.description: The AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship covers all billable American University expenses - full tuition, room and board - for two international students each year who need a non-immigrant (preferably F-1 or J-1) visa to study in the United States. It is renewable for up to four years of undergraduate study based on continued satisfactory academic performance, and all majors offered at AU are eligible. Non-billable expenses such as mandatory health insurance, books, airline tickets, taxes and miscellaneous costs are not covered, leaving approximately US $4,000 per year to the student. The application is two-step and both steps are due January 15, 2027, with late applications not considered; finalists and winners are notified by April 1, 2027.

records.description: The Wien International Scholarship Program, established at Brandeis University in 1958, brings undergraduate students from around the world to campus. It is awarded to exceptional international applicants who show strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement, and it meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient based on a complete review of financial documentation. official_details.description: The Wien International Scholarship Program (WISP), established at Brandeis University in 1958, brings undergraduate students from every corner of the globe to campus and has brought over 894 scholars from 115 countries. It meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient based on a complete review of financial documentation, and is awarded to exceptional international applicants who demonstrate strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement. There is no separate application process: candidates apply directly to Brandeis through the Common Application or Coalition Application, file the CSS Profile by the international aid deadline (Nov. 2 for Early Decision I / Early Action, Jan. 15 for Early Decision II / Regular Decision for Fall 2027), and are informed of a Wien or other Brandeis scholarship with their admission decision. official_details.description: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a full-cost postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge, funded by the Gates Cambridge Trust, which was established in October 2000 by a US$210m donation from the Gates Foundation. Around 70 awards are made each year, roughly two-thirds to PhD students, open to citizens of any country outside the UK applying for a PhD, MLitt or one-year postgraduate course in any subject. The award covers the University Composition Fee, a maintenance allowance of Â£23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate, one economy return airfare and inbound visa costs including the Immigration Health Surcharge, with discretionary top-ups for academic development, dependants, fieldwork, maternity or paternity and hardship.

official_details.description: The Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship is a merit-based award for overseas fee-paying PhD students at the University of Edinburgh. It covers the difference between the tuition fee payable by a UK/EU postgraduate student and the fee chargeable to an overseas postgraduate student, and it does not cover maintenance expenses. The award is tenable for up to three years subject to satisfactory progress and is open to applicants in any subject offered by the University. International applicants for College Postgraduate Studentships must hold this scholarship or otherwise demonstrate the availability of funds to meet the full overseas tuition fee. The scholarship's own webpage is no longer available and the University has published no current deadline or award value.

official_details.description: The Study in Canada Scholarships programme, funded by Global Affairs Canada through the Academic Relations program, lets Canadian post-secondary institutions host international students for short-term study or research exchanges. Individual students cannot apply directly: a Canadian Designated Learning Institution that waives tuition fees selects and nominates them through the My EduCanada portal, and the institution submits a Management and Accountability Framework to the administrator. Awards are CAD 10,200 for four months or one academic term at college, undergraduate or graduate level, and CAD 14,000 for five to six months at graduate level, covering airfare, health insurance, permit fees, living expenses and study supplies. Eligibility is restricted to citizens of 20 named countries and territories who remain full-time, tuition-paying students at home, and all project activity must finish by September 30, 2027.

official_details.description: The Émile Boutmy Scholarship is a tuition-fee exemption created by Sciences Po to welcome high-achieving international students from outside the European Union. It is awarded to first-time applicants admitted to the Undergraduate College or to a two-year Master's programme. At Undergraduate College level it gives either a total exemption or a €9,500 tuition-fee exemption; at Master's level it gives a €18,500 exemption from tuition fees for each of the two years. It cannot be combined with other Sciences Po or partner scholarships.

official_details.description: INSEAD awards merit-based and need-based scholarships to candidates admitted to its Master's and MBA programmes. For the Master in Management, every admitted candidate is automatically reviewed for the Diversity Scholarship and the Achievement Scholarship with no separate form, while a small number of named donor scholarships (Kung Family, L'Oréal for Youth, MIM Women's Merit, Qinqin and Xin Zhang) require a dedicated application and have their own criteria and admission-round restrictions. INSEAD publishes an average MIM scholarship amount of €14,500 against a Class of 2028 tuition fee of €57,870. The stored official page for this record is the MBA International Funding page, which additionally curates third-party loans and scholarships such as Lendwise, Prodigy Finance, MBA for Women, Educations.com and the CFA Institute programme.

Awards take the form of tuition-fee waivers of 25%, 50%, 75% or 100%, plus a limited number of fully-funded scholarships that cover 100% of fees and may add a stipend. official_details.description: The A*STAR Graduate Scholarship offers full funding for a PhD at a Singapore autonomous university, with joint supervision by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member. Successful applicants receive full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment, for up to 4 years. For international students the monthly allowance is $3,600 on the STEM track or $5,000 on the specialised Semiconductor, Quantum and Computing tracks. The scholarship is bond-free for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents; non-Singaporean awardees without Permanent Residency must serve 3 years in a Singapore-based company. Applications run 1 November to 1 February and 1 June to 10 August.

records.description: The NUS Research Scholarship is awarded by the NUS Graduate School to outstanding graduate students for research leading to a higher degree at the National University of Singapore. It is open to PhD and Master's (Research) candidates of all nationalities, including Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and international students, and covers a full waiver of tuition fees plus a monthly stipend. Stipend rates effective from 1 January 2026 are SGD 3,800 (Singapore Citizen PhD), SGD 3,400 (Permanent Resident PhD) and SGD 3,000 (international PhD) per month, and SGD 3,800, SGD 3,000 and SGD 2,900 respectively for Master's (Research) candidates. PhD scholars who pass the PhD Qualifying Examination may receive an additional stipend of up to SGD 500 per month, and international scholars must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirements.

records.description: The President's Graduate Fellowship is awarded by the NUS Graduate School to PhD candidates who show exceptional promise or accomplishment in research, and a number of PhD research students are selected each semester by the University. It is open to Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents and all international students, covers a full waiver of tuition fees at the University and pays a monthly stipend of SGD 3,900 for international students, SGD 4,400 for Permanent Residents and SGD 4,800 for Singapore Citizens, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. International students additionally receive a one-off settling allowance of S$1,000 and a one-off air travel allowance of up to S$750, and from the AY2023/24 intake recipients are eligible for the NUSGS Research Incentive Award. The Fellowship is tenable for one year in the first instance, renewable each semester, with a maximum period of four years, and is awarded by faculty/department nomination only.

records.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme offered by Nanyang Technological University to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying full-time for a PhD at NTU. It is described as the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognising PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. Open to all nationalities, it requires an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level, or official documentation confirming the candidate is on track to achieve it. Monthly stipends revised with effect from January 2026 are S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for international students, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. The award also covers the annual tuition fee and provides an overseas conference allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year, an annual book allowance of S$500, a one-off IT allowance of S$1,500, a one-off thesis allowance of S$600 and priority for campus accommodation. There is no bond attached to the scholarship, though international students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties under the Graduate Assistantship Programme.

records.description: The Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of Singapore Management University's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, made possible by a gift from the Lee Foundation, with up to 60 scholarships funded. It is open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduates of any nationality taking a single or double degree programme, and requires a second major or an equivalent breadth requirement, demonstrated leadership and communications skills, and a substantial record of co-curricular activity or community service. Benefits comprise a waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to four years, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding overseas exchange, community service or competitions, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, and development opportunities from SMU's Student Success Centre. Applicants are considered through the Scholarship section of the standard admission application, with no separate scholarship form. The scholarship is bond-free, but non-Singaporean scholars must sign a Ministry of Education Tuition Grant agreement obliging them to work for Singapore-based companies for three years after graduation.

official_details.description: The India Science and Research Fellowship (ISRF) is funded by the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, and administered and published by the Indian National Science Academy. It enables researchers holding permanent positions in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand to carry out 3 to 6 months of research in India in frontier and advanced areas of science including medicine and agriculture. Up to 80 fellowships are awarded each year, ten per country. The award provides a monthly allowance, contingency grants, return air fare and visa fee reimbursement, but is a research visit rather than a degree programme.

records.eligibility_summary: Students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America. JRF applicants must be 35 (male) or 40 (female) years of age as on 1 July of the year of application and hold at least a high-class master's degree with a second-class bachelor's degree, or a second-class master's degree with a first-class bachelor's degree. RA applicants must be 40 (male) or 45 (female) and hold a doctorate with published and independent research work.

official_details.description: The UGC Junior Research Fellowship and Research Associateship for Foreign Nationals is a Government of India scheme, implemented by the University Grants Commission, that gives students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America the opportunity to undertake advanced study and research in sciences, humanities and social sciences at Indian universities. Twenty JRF slots and seven RA slots are available each year, each with a four-year non-extendable tenure. Applications are circulated to Indian embassies and missions abroad, which screen them locally before forwarding them to UGC. Award is a monthly research stipend plus contingency and departmental assistance to the host institution.
official_details.program_type: Research fellowship for foreign nationals
official_details.coverage: Monthly research stipend, annual contingency grant, departmental assistance to the host institution and hostel accommodation or house rent allowance. No tuition and no travel costs are covered.

application_readiness_checklist: Check that you are a national of a developing country in Asia, Africa or Latin America, since the scheme is not open to Indian citizens
Verify your age against the 1 July cut-off: 35 male or 40 female for JRF, 40 male or 45 female for RA
Confirm you hold the stated minimum qualification, including the bachelor's class requirement for JRF and a doctorate with publications for RA
Approach your Indian embassy or mission early, because it sets the local timetable and must endorse the application
Identify an Indian university willing to host you, since the university must agree to provide facilities
Prepare three copies of the form and all certified enclosures before the mission's local deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing embassy or mission endorsement, which is mandatory
Applying directly to UGC without going through the mission, which is not the official route
Failing the age cut-off measured on 1 July of the year of application
Not meeting the bachelor's-class condition attached to the master's degree for JRF
Not having published and independent research work for an RA application
Incomplete enclosure set, since the form is liable to be rejected if incomplete
Expecting a tuition waiver; this is a stipend scheme
estimated_uncovered_costs: University tuition fees, which the scheme does not state it will pay
International travel to and from India
Mess, electricity and water charges, which are excluded from hostel fee reimbursement
Costs beyond the 30 days annual leave entitlement and beyond the four-year award period
Medical expenses, since no separate or fixed medical assistance is provided

Three typed copies of the statement of not more than 500 words
One certified copy of the birth certificate or evidence of date of birth
Three recent passport size photographs stapled to the forms
Abstract of the proposed research plan of about 500 words in triplicate
Embassy endorsement of the application
Joining report in the Annexure II proforma after joining
Utilisation certificate and statement of expenditure for the previous grant period

Submit six-monthly progress reports by the end of June and December
On completion, submit the audited utilisation certificate to finalise accounts and recover any retained amount

records.name: TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme
records.official_source: UNESCO-TWAS and Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), India
records.duration: Full-time fellowships up to a maximum of 4 years; sandwich fellowships from a minimum of 6 months up to a maximum decided by the host institute but no greater than 3 years
records.deadline: Official wording for the 2026 call: "Closing date of this fellowship: 6 then 20 May 2026 now extended until 3 June 2026". The call is closed and results are expected at the end of 2026 or early 2027, with fellows starting no earlier than 2027.
records.application_period: Annual. The 2026 call opened 6 March 2026 and closed 20 May 2026, extended to 3 June 2026. Applications can only be submitted through the TWAS online portal once the call is open.
records.eligibility_summary: Nationals of a developing country other than India, aged 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, holding a Master's degree in science and technology, regularly employed with a research assignment in their home country, accepted at a CSIR laboratory or institution with an official acceptance letter, and not holding a visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country.

National of a developing country, other than India
Must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Must hold a Master's degree in science and technology
Must be regularly employed in their home country and hold a research assignment there
Sandwich fellowships: must be a registered PhD student in the home country and provide the Registration and No Objection Certificate from the home university
Full-time fellowships: must be willing to register at a university in India within the first year if agreed by CSIR
Must be accepted at a CSIR laboratory or institution and provide an official acceptance letter from the host institution
Must provide evidence of English proficiency if the medium of education was not English
Must provide evidence that they will return to their home country on completion of the fellowship
Must not take up other assignments during the fellowship period
Must be financially responsible for any accompanying family members

Subsidized accommodation
Full-time fellowship tenable for up to 4 years in a CSIR laboratory or institute

Evidence of English proficiency if the medium of education was not English
Evidence of intent to return to the home country on completion of the fellowship
Completed TWAS online application form
records.english_requirement: The official page states "The language of instruction for foreign scholars in CSIR laboratories/institutes is English." Applicants whose medium of education was not English must provide evidence of English proficiency.
requirements: Applications may only be submitted to TWAS through the online portal

Complete the online form and upload the supporting documents listed in the call

records.selection_notes: Results of the fellowship selection are expected at the end of 2026 or early 2027 and selected candidates will be able to start their fellowship no earlier than 2027. Requests for acceptance must be directed to the chosen CSIR host institutions, and without preliminary acceptance the application will not be considered for selection.

official_details.description: The TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme is run jointly by UNESCO-TWAS and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research of India. It allows foreign scholars from developing countries to pursue research toward a PhD in emerging areas of science and technology in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India, across nine named fields including agricultural sciences, chemical sciences, engineering sciences, mathematical sciences and physics. Applicants may either be registered for a PhD in their home country under the sandwich option or enrol in a PhD course at a university in India under the full-time option. CSIR provides a monthly stipend covering living costs, food and health insurance, together with subsidized accommodation. Applications are submitted only through the TWAS online portal.
official_details.program_type: Doctoral research fellowship
official_details.coverage: Monthly stipend for living costs, food and health insurance, plus subsidized accommodation, tenable at a CSIR laboratory or institute in India. No tuition, travel or family support is stated.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a national of a developing country other than India and are 35 or under on 31 December of the application year
Check that you do not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or any developed country
Secure written acceptance from a specific eligible CSIR laboratory or institute before applying, because without it the application is not considered
Make sure the acceptance letter is dated in the same year as the application, since only same-year letters are eligible
For a sandwich application, get the Vice-Chancellor or Registrar to sign the Registration and No Objection Certificate and send copies to both CSIR and TWAS
Prepare evidence of English proficiency if your medium of education was not English
Prepare evidence of your intention to return home on completion and confirm you can support accompanying family members
common_rejection_risks: No preliminary acceptance letter from a CSIR institution, which makes the application ineligible for selection
An acceptance letter dated in a different year from the application
Applying through email or post instead of the TWAS online portal, which is the only accepted route
Holding a visa for temporary or permanent residency in India or a developed country
Being over 35 on 31 December of the application year
Applying to more than one TWAS or OWSD programme in the same calendar year
Selecting a CSIR host that is not on the eligible list
estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel to and from India, which the page does not list as funded
Costs of any accompanying family members, which the applicant is explicitly made financially responsible for
Tuition fees, if enrolment at an Indian university is required, because tuition coverage is not stated
Any expenses beyond the subsidized accommodation offered
Costs of converting or moving the stipend, which is not convertible into foreign currency

Registration and No Objection Certificate signed by the home university Vice-Chancellor or Registrar, for sandwich applicants
Evidence of English proficiency if the medium of education was not English
Evidence of commitment to return to the home country on completion
Completed TWAS online application form
Master's degree evidence as required by the portal

records.official_source: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt. of India
records.duration: Three years
records.deadline: Official wording for the 2026 cycle: "The application should be submitted by September 25, 2026" and "Last date for submission of the application is September 25, 2026." That date has passed. The guidelines state applications are invited annually.
records.application_period: Annual. Applications are invited on an annual basis through announcements published in Indian national newspapers and the notification on the ICAR website, with Indian diplomatic missions informed by email. For 2026 the deadline was 25 September 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Indian as well as overseas nationals holding a Master's degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences who intend to pursue a doctoral degree in agriculture and allied sciences within the priority areas identified by ICAR and notified one year in advance. Overseas candidates study at Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system; Indian candidates study at identified overseas universities or institutions with strong research and teaching capabilities.
eligibility: Indian or overseas national
Must hold a Master's degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences
Must pursue a doctoral degree in agriculture and allied sciences in an identified priority area
Overseas candidates must study at an identified Indian Agricultural University in the ICAR-AU system
Indian candidates must study at an identified overseas university or institution with strong research and teaching capabilities
Must have a clear record of good conduct, certified by the Competent Authority of the university last attended or the present employer
Must provide two referees with contact email addresses who may be contacted directly by the Council
In-service Indian candidates must also furnish deputation approval from the Director of the ICAR institute or Vice-Chancellor of the Agricultural University
coverage: Three-year doctoral fellowship for 30 awardees per year
Support for study at a host institution in India for overseas candidates, or at an identified overseas institution for Indian candidates
required_documents: Completed NS-ICARIF application in the prescribed format
Two references with contact email addresses, one preferably the applicant's supervisor
Letter of acceptance for admission to the PhD degree programme in the identified area of study at the host university
Certificate of good conduct from the Competent Authority of the university last attended or the present employer
Deputation approval from the Director of the ICAR institute or Vice-Chancellor, for in-service Indian candidates
records.english_requirement: The call, guidelines and application proforma are published by ICAR in English.
requirements: The area of study and the line of the proposed research work must fall in an identified priority area relevant to Indian or global agriculture, notified one year in advance
The applicant must obtain acceptance of admission to the PhD programme at their own level, and should preferably enclose the acceptance letter with the application
The applicant should satisfy themselves about the admission and course requirements of the university before naming it as a place of study
Two referees must be provided who may be contacted directly by the Council
Selected candidates must register for the programme within one year of the fellowship award letter, or the offer is terminated automatically
application_method: Complete the prescribed application proforma available on the ICAR website
Email the application to ADG (HRD) at adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the subject line "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number"
Send the complete application with enclosures endorsed as required before the stated last date
records.selection_notes: Candidates are evaluated on a weighted scale taking into account the relevance of the area of study, the proposed research plan, academic records, achievements and past work experience, followed by an interview by a Selection Committee constituted by the Council. The Committee may conduct telephonic or teleconferencing interviews, and overseas candidates may be interviewed by Council-identified experts based in their own country.

official_details.description: The Netaji Subhas-ICAR International Fellowships, administered by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, support doctoral study in agriculture and allied sciences in priority areas identified by ICAR. The programme is open to both Indian and overseas nationals holding a Master's degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences. Thirty fellowships of three years each are awarded annually. Overseas candidates study at identified Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system, while Indian candidates study at identified overseas universities and institutions. Applications are submitted by email to the Assistant Director General of Human Resource Development.
official_details.program_type: International doctoral research fellowship
official_details.coverage: Three-year doctoral fellowship support with placement at an identified host institution. The published call does not itemise tuition, living-cost or travel components, so no specific coverage can be asserted.

Confirm your proposed research sits inside one of ICAR's identified priority areas, which are notified one year in advance

Line up two referees with working email addresses, ideally including your current supervisor
Get a certificate of good conduct from the Competent Authority of your university or employer
If you are an in-service Indian candidate, secure deputation approval from the Director of your ICAR institute or the Vice-Chancellor
Send the application to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the exact subject line "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number"

Research proposal outside the identified priority areas
Missing or undated acceptance letter from the host university
Fewer than two referees, or referees who cannot be contacted at the email addresses given
Missing certificate of good conduct
Missing deputation approval for in-service Indian candidates
Missing the required subject line on the application email
Failure to register within one year of the award letter, which terminates the offer automatically
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any costs the ICAR call does not itemise, since it publishes no coverage breakdown
Travel and relocation costs, which are not mentioned in the published call
Personal expenses beyond the three-year fellowship period

Two referee names with valid contact email addresses
Certificate of good conduct from the Competent Authority
Deputation approval for in-service Indian candidates
Evidence of Master's degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences

official_details.description: FIRST@IITH is IIT Hyderabad's Fellowship for International Research Scholars in Technology. It supports outstanding international scholars pursuing PhDs with full financial support, and is the institute's flagship fully funded doctoral offer for foreign nationals. The award provides a monthly fellowship of INR 60,000 and annual contingency support of INR 1,00,000 across a four-year doctoral programme, with no application fee. Applications are processed entirely by email to the International Relations office, and selection follows shortlisting and an online interview. The scheme runs twice a year with January and July intakes.

official_details.description: KUISP is the KIIT University India Scholarships Programme for foreign national applicants, covering undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study as well as short-term training programmes at KIIT Deemed to be University in Bhubaneswar. It awards a scholarship of between 50% and 100% on tuition fees for the whole course duration, together with free books, examination and registration fees, sports facilities, internet access, airport pickup and student society membership. KIIT publishes 100 international scholarships, with two students per country receiving a full tuition waiver and ten students per country receiving a half waiver. KUISP is explicitly not fully funded: airfare, visa fees, medical insurance, stipends, personal living expenses and laptops are excluded, and students pay accommodation and food charges. Applications are free and are submitted through the KIIT International Admission Portal or directly to the international office, and in some cycles through Indian embassies and missions.

official_details.description: Global UGRAD is a fully funded, one-semester, non-degree undergraduate exchange run by the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs of the U.S. Department of State. It brings outstanding undergraduate students from around the world to the United States for one semester of full-time non-degree study at a U.S. college or university, combined with community service, professional development and cultural enrichment. All participant costs, including international and domestic travel, housing, meals and health coverage for the programme duration, are covered by the Bureau. Two organisations administer the programme on the Bureau's behalf, and public applications are made through the U.S. Embassy's Public Affairs Section or the Fulbright Commission in the applicant's own country, so deadlines vary by programme and region. Participants take at least two courses in their major plus a U.S. Studies course and complete a minimum of twenty hours of community service.

official_details.coverage: All participant costs for the programme duration: international and domestic travel, housing, meals and health coverage, plus pre-academic English training where needed, academic coursework, service learning, professional development and cultural enrichment. No per-participant cash amount is published.

official_details.description: The Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship is the University of Rochester's premier undergraduate scholarship, funded from a permanent endowment created by a $25 million gift in 2007 from Rich and Martha Handler in honour of Alan and Jane Handler. It is awarded to first-year, fall-term domestic and international applicants who have demonstrated academic excellence, have outstanding potential to be future leaders, have shown resilience in the face of complex challenges, and have substantial financial need as demonstrated on the CSS Profile and FAFSA. Recipients receive complete financial support covering tuition, mandatory fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation for the regular four-year academic programme, plus health insurance where applicable, mentoring and an enrichment fund of up to $5,000. A nomination from an unrelated third party is required between 15 September and 30 November, and students are considered automatically if they submit the admission application and financial aid documents by 1 December.

official_details.description: Berea College's Tuition Promise Scholarship guarantees that a student will never pay tuition from personal income. After all federal, state, institutional and private grants and scholarships have been considered, a Berea Tuition Scholarship is awarded to cover the remaining cost of tuition. Berea has not charged tuition for more than 130 years, so the award is conferred on admitted students rather than won in a competition. Eligibility is tied to a unique financial eligibility requirement assessed by the Office of Admissions from the FAFSA using household size and adjusted gross income, and every applicant must file a FAFSA to be considered for admission. Published 2026-27 costs are tuition of $56,900, housing of $5,000 and food of $4,142, giving total direct costs of $66,042 and a total cost of attendance of $69,942, so housing and food remain payable for current cohorts. From Fall 2027 the College's Financial Freedom Pledge will cover 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students until graduation. Domestic first-year deadlines are 1 November, 31 January and 31 March, with 15 October and 15 January for international applicants.

records.description: The Griffin Financial Aid Office at Harvard College provides need-based aid that allows Harvard to bring the best students regardless of their ability to pay. Financial aid is available to foreign students on exactly the same basis as for American students; because international students are not eligible for federal funding, the College applies its own job and scholarship money. For families with income of $100,000 or below and typical assets, aid covers all billed expenses including tuition, fees, food, housing, health insurance if needed, travel between campus and home, and $2,000 start-up and launch grants. Families with income up to $200,000 receive free tuition plus aid for additional costs. Aid is need-blind with respect to admission.

records.description: Yale College operates a need-blind admissions policy paired with need-based financial aid. Every dollar of undergraduate aid is awarded on demonstrated financial need in the form of scholarships rather than loans, and offers meet 100% of demonstrated need regardless of citizenship or immigration status. Families with annual incomes below $100,000 and typical assets qualify for a zero parent share award covering tuition and fees, housing, food and travel, plus hospitalization insurance and a $2,000 first-year start-up grant; families below $200,000 qualify for a scholarship covering at least tuition. International Early Action aid documents are due December 1 and Regular Decision documents February 15.

records.description: Dartmouth College meets 100% of the demonstrated need of all admitted financial aid applicants, regardless of citizenship or entry round, and its financial aid packages never include a required student loan. Need is calculated as cost of attendance minus family contribution, with direct expenses of tuition, fees, food and housing and indirect expenses such as travel, books, supplies and laundry. Families with total annual income below $125,000 with typical assets can expect no parent contribution, while families earning between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets can expect a scholarship or grants covering the full cost of tuition. International applicants file the CSS Profile with school code 3351, or the International Student Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a serious hardship. Financial aid deadlines are November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.

records.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme, established in 1969 by His Highness the Aga Khan IV, supports outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing postgraduate study, and has supported more than 1,500 students. Awards are made through a global, annual competitive process with a limited number of new awards each cycle. Each award is structured as half grant and half loan, and the recipient must repay 50 percent of the award amount with a guarantor co-signing the agreement; repayment, including a service charge, begins six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support for failing academic standards. The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses, but not international travel, clothing, furniture or family living expenses. Master's funding runs for the full degree; PhD funding covers the first two years. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027.

records.notes: Rotary awards up to 170 funded fellowships a year across eight peace centers. Since 2002 the program has trained more than 1,900 fellows who now work in over 140 countries, many in governments, NGOs, education and research institutions, peacekeeping and law enforcement agencies, and organizations such as the United Nations and the World Bank. Master's programmes last 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study. records.description: The #YouAreWelcomeHere Scholarship is a coordinated campaign run by NAFSA: Association of International Educators in which each participating U.S. college or university awards two scholarships to first-year international undergraduates. Each award covers at least 50% of the institution's published annual out-of-state tuition, excluding fees, and is renewable for the length of the degree programme provided the student makes satisfactory academic progress. Students apply directly to each institution by that institution's own deadline, which the campaign states is typically in spring or summer for a fall start. Applicants must submit the campaign's scholarship application form plus a 500-1000 word essay or a two-to-five minute video answering a fixed prompt about leadership skills.

official_details.description: The Faculty of Science of the University of Geneva has established an Excellence Fellowship programme, with the support of external partners, open to outstanding and highly motivated students who wish to pursue a Master of Science in one of the disciplines covered by the Faculty. The Fellowship consists of a grant amounting to CHF 10,000 to CHF 15,000 per year with no teaching duties; it is awarded for one year and extended for the regular duration of the chosen Master's programme provided the applicant is academically successful at the end of the first semester. Candidates are selected on the basis of excellence and must also complete the UNIGE enrolment procedure.
official_details.program_type: Faculty-level excellence grant scheme for incoming Master of Science students
official_details.coverage: Partial: a CHF 10,000-15,000 per year grant with no teaching duties; tuition coverage is not stated and full funding is not claimed.

Prepare the single PDF in the exact order requested, with a CV of no more than two pages
Secure two professors willing to write reference letters attesting your aptitude
Watch for the personal application link e-mail, which only arrives from the beginning of January
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 28 February deadline
Not having completed the UNIGE enrolment procedure, so the fellowship file cannot be considered
Uploading more than one PDF or documents out of the requested order
A CV longer than two pages
Fewer than two reference letters, or letters that do not attest aptitude to the programme
Already having started a Master programme at the Faculty of Science, which disqualifies the applicant

Living costs above the CHF 10,000-15,000 per year grant, and housing in Geneva, which is not among the most affordable
Travel costs to Geneva

records.selection_notes: Around ten excellence scholarships are awarded each year. The SASME checks completeness, the Admissions Office (SII) decides formal eligibility, the faculty decides admission to the chosen master's, and finally the Selection Board for the Master's Scholarship selects the scholarship holders in March, with applicants notified in early April. Decisions may not be appealed.
records.best_fit: Graduates of a foreign university with outstanding academic results seeking a place in a UNIL master's programme in a faculty other than Medicine, and able to supplement the CHF 1,600 per month with their own resources (about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne).
