Around ten awards are made each year. Master programmes in Medicine, Sciences and Practices of Education, most of Law, Physical Education and Sport Didactics, Health Sciences, Sustainable Management & Technology, Human Taphonomy and all MAS programmes are excluded. The page warns the amount does not cover the full cost of living in Switzerland.
records.description: The University of Lausanne awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard. The scholarship is paid for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme at CHF 1,600 per month, and recipients are exempt from the standard course registration fees, with only the CHF 80 semester fees remaining payable. UNIL states explicitly that the amount does not constitute full funding, since about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne. Applications for the 2027/2028 academic year are open until 1 November 2026.

The administrative fee is never refunded, even if you withdraw or are refused. If your scholarship application fails but the faculty still admits you, you do not pay it twice for the same academic year.

There is no age limit, but for applicants from visa-restricted countries a higher age or a completed first master's can make the visa impossible. Check with the Swiss embassy in your country before applying.
Where certified true copies are required, the postmark date counts - 1 November. Late postmarked envelopes are not processed.

records.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.

records.description: IMD Business School offers a portfolio of scholarships and need-based bursaries for candidates applying to and entering its one-year full-time MBA in Lausanne. Six named scholarships were listed as open in October 2026: the MBA5 Scholarship of CHF 50,000, the Hilti STEM Scholars Program of CHF 50,000, the Nestle Scholarship for Women of CHF 40,000, the Forté Scholarship for Women of CHF 30,000, IMD MBA Merit Scholarships of up to CHF 40,000, and the BackPack Scholarship for Women with full funding. Most run throughout 2026 on an available-until-allocated basis, while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Scholarships are applied for through the Program section of the MBA application form and are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer, with selection based on academic and professional excellence, GMAT/GRE scores, career progression, international exposure and Assessment Day performance. Separate need-based bursaries are awarded on proven financial need and confirmed on an ongoing basis.

official_details.description: IMD is committed to fostering growth in diversity through its merit scholarships and need-based bursaries, which are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer to join the IMD MBA programme. Six named scholarships were listed as open: the MBA5 Scholarship of CHF 50K, the Hilti STEM Scholars Program of CHF 50K, the Nestle Scholarship for Women of CHF 40K, the Forté Scholarship for Women of CHF 30K, IMD MBA Merit Scholarships of up to CHF 40K, and the BackPack Scholarship for Women with full funding. Scholarship applications are made in the Program section of the MBA application form, and the main awards carry the deadline 'Throughout 2026 (available until allocated)' while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Bursary applications are made in the admissions application by the admissions deadline, with recipients confirmed on an ongoing basis on the basis of proven financial need, good academic results, a strong reference letter and steady career progression. 48% of students receive a scholarship from IMD and more than 50% of scholarships are awarded to women.

records.notes: This record is a funding information hub rather than a single named scholarship, so no amount, deadline or document list can be attributed to it and those fields are left null. The page explicitly states that the primary responsibility for funding studies lies with the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence, that university scholarships are only supplementary to cantonal education contributions, and that international students should investigate eligibility for scholarships in their home country. That last point is directly relevant to an international-scholarship database and contradicts any reading of this record as a funding route open to international applicants. The page also carries a dedicated Submission Deadlines subpage and a Funding from the University of Basel subpage, neither of which was fetched within this record's fetch budget.
records.description: The University of Basel's scholarship page explains how study funding is structured in Switzerland: essentially, the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence are responsible for funding studies, and scholarships from the university are granted by the scholarship committee of the Senate in addition to any cantonal education contributions. The university additionally awards specific scholarships to students in exchange programmes, advised by the Student Exchange Office, and its Social Services student welfare office offers advice. The page signposts the cantonal scholarship and student loan offices for Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft as well as ausbildungsbeitraege.ch for all cantons, and advises international students to find out what scholarships they are eligible for in their home country.

records.duration: 12 to 36 months; contracts run up to 12 months with the possibility of renewal for a total of up to three years
records.deadline: Fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest published on WIPO's career website, or via WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels. No fixed central deadline is published on the programme page.
records.application_period: Continuous, per vacancy. Positions are announced through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's Taleo career site and on LinkedIn, so there is no single application window.
records.eligibility_summary: At least a first-level university degree such as a bachelor's. Depending on the fellowship category there may be additional requirements, such as a minimum level of professional experience, an advanced degree such as a Master's or PhD, or specific competencies. There is no age limit and no limit on how long ago a candidate graduated. Former interns may apply if they meet the criteria, but Young Experts Program participants may not apply for any WIPO position within one year of completing the programme.

The page states the programme duration as 12 to 36 months while the benefits section describes contracts of up to 12 months renewable to a total of up to three years, which is consistent. A one-year waiting period applies to former Young Experts Program participants, which is a decision-critical rule that is easy to miss.
records.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.

official_details.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program offers hands-on experience, expanded knowledge and network building at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for a duration of 12 to 36 months. To be eligible, candidates must possess at least a first-level university degree such as a bachelor's, with additional requirements such as a minimum level of professional experience, advanced degrees or specific competencies depending on the fellowship category. Fellows fall into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website or via WIPO's LinkedIn and other social media channels. Fellows receive a contract of up to 12 months renewable to a total of up to three years, a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, medical and professional accident insurance largely paid for by WIPO, relocation travel at the start and end of the fellowship, visa assistance, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days annual leave per full month, up to six study leave days a year and funded UN official languages training where job duties require it. There is no age limit, and former Young Experts Program participants may not apply for any WIPO position within one year of completing the programme.

official_details.coverage: Monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 plus insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation travel at the start and end of the fellowship, paid leave and training. Remuneration for work rather than funding of a degree.

records.description: The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) is a University of Amsterdam award for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA who apply for a degree programme at the university. records.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship is a study scholarship for excellent students joining a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September, with the exception of the non-advanced LLM and MSc programmes of Leiden Law School. Applicants must normally hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance. The scholarship is awarded for the duration of the programme at one of five tuition-fee levels between EUR 10,000 and EUR 19,000, and Leiden states it is not a full scholarship, so a significant personal contribution is still required and non-EEA recipients must prove sufficient funds for their residence permit. The application is made inside the master's admission application with a motivation letter of maximum 500 words, and the deadline is 1 December 2026.

official_details.description: The University of Groningen's NL Scholarship is a one-time EUR 5,000 grant co-funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the university, intended to help cover living expenses during the first year of a master's degree. It is awarded for one academic year, can be received only once, and does not cover the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands. Applicants must be non-EEA, hold an admission offer for a listed programme, have obtained their bachelor's degree outside the Netherlands and show excellent undergraduate performance, then submit a motivation letter, transcript and admission letter. The published deadline for 2026-2027 was 1 February 2026 (23:59 CET) and results are aimed at by 15 March.
official_details.program_type: Government and university co-funded one-time grant
official_details.coverage: One-off EUR 5,000 in the first year of study, intended for living costs only; no tuition, travel or insurance coverage.

records.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a very selective scholarship for talented, highly motivated non-EEA students with outstanding study results applying to a complete English-taught Radboud University master's programme. A Radboud Scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 for 2027/2028, against an example normal fee of about EUR 19,000, and covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs, while living and studying costs remain the student's responsibility. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028 across six faculties, the application is made through the OSIRIS master's application with two reference letters and a CV, the OSIRIS submission deadline is 31 January 2027 and the file must be complete by 14 February 2027, and the decision is communicated before mid-April 2027.

records.program_type: University full scholarship (university fund + national NL Scholarship)
records.notes: The programme combines the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund's High Potential Scholarship with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship, so it covers substantially more than the NL Scholarship alone. Handling fees for programmes that charge one are not covered. The application portal is unavailable between 22 and 26 October because of an upgrade. Applicants can submit only one UM scholarship application; multiple applications are disqualified.

records.description: The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship programme awards 18 full scholarships each academic year, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have been admitted to a Maastricht University master's programme. It combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship. For the 2027-2028 intake, scholarship applications run from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), the participating master's application must be complete through Studielink before 10 December 2026, and applicants must be non-EU/EEA (also excluding Switzerland and Surinam), aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and no previous degree-seeking study in the Netherlands. Recipients receive a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 over 13 months or EUR 38,750 over 25 months, tuition fees, visa costs and EUR 700 of health and liability insurance paid at cost, a mandatory UM room until 16 July 2028 and a two-week Pre-Academic Training programme. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.

records.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are master's degrees jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, plus academic and non-academic associated partners. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Catalogue, maintained by EACEA and updated annually, lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU; the stored row corresponds to the catalogue's Sweden country facet. Master's-level students from all over the world may apply, and Erasmus Mundus scholarships are available for outstanding students at participating programmes. Applicants apply directly to the consortium running their chosen programme, not to the European Commission.

records.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship is a merit award for international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Adelaide University, offering a 50% tuition fee reduction over the standard full-time duration of the degree. Places are limited and allocated on merit by a selection panel reviewing applications on a rolling basis through the recruitment cycle. Applicants must be international students applying to a CRICOS-registered bachelor or master degree that is not on the Excluded Programs list, and must have an ATAR of 99 or an overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale as the basis of admission. Recipients must maintain a minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in each compulsory Study Period.

records.description: The Melbourne Research Scholarship is offered to high-achieving domestic and international students enrolling in, or already enrolled in, a graduate research degree at the University of Melbourne. It exists in three forms: a Fee Offset award, a Stipend award, and a combined Stipend and Fee Offset award. The Stipend award combines a full fee offset with a fortnightly stipend of $41,100 per year pro rata (2027 full-time rate), a one-off relocation allowance and OSHC Single Membership for international students who need a student visa. No separate application is required: applicants who apply for a graduate research course by that course's closing date are assessed automatically. Around 350 scholarships are available, and selection is by ranking on academic results for previous study and research potential.

records.description: The ANU University Research Scholarship supports high-achieving higher degree by research (HDR) students whose research aligns with the strategic directions of the Australian National University. It is awarded through ANU's two annual central scholarship rounds alongside the Research Training Program and other centrally managed scholarships, and no separate application is required: prospective candidates are considered automatically on the basis of their admission application. The value is a fortnightly stipend of $40,475 per annum (2027 full-time base rate), paid for 3.5 years for PhD candidates or 1.5 years for MPhil candidates. Each ANU College convenes a selection committee to score and rank all eligible H1 (or equivalent) applicants on academic record, research potential, supervisor support, referee reports and English language competency.

Selection requires each ANU College to convene a selection committee to score and rank all eligible H1 (or equivalent) applicants in a merit-based process.

records.description: The University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS) is a competitively awarded stipend scholarship for international students commencing or already enrolled in a higher degree by research at the University of Sydney. It pays a stipend of $44,293 per annum at the 2027 rate, indexed annually, plus relocation and thesis allowances. Holders are automatically awarded the companion University of Sydney Tuition Fee Scholarship, which covers 100% of tuition fees for up to 14 research periods together with Overseas Student Health Cover, making the combined package a full funding package for international research students. Preference may be given to applicants intending to enrol in, or already enrolled in, a PhD, and to applicants who have not previously completed an HDR course or held an equivalent scholarship at the same level.

records.description: The Deakin Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship recognises international students with consistently high academic performance and the potential to make a leading contribution to Deakin and the communities it serves. The award covers 100% or 50% of tuition fees depending on the scholarship outcome, for the normal duration of the program, and requires participation in the Vice-Chancellor's Professional Excellence Program. Applicants must be new international students enrolling in a Deakin coursework degree with at least an 85% average or equivalent in previous studies, and must submit a 300-word personal statement, two references and their academic transcripts. Scholarships are assessed on a rolling basis in the lead-up to each trimester, and the award is not available to the Doctor of Medicine (H911) program.

official_details.description: The Western Australian Premier's University Scholarship provides successful students with $50,000 towards their course fees and other university costs at one of Western Australia's five universities, with ten recipients selected annually and two awarded per university. Applicants must be new offshore international students who are citizens of one of 22 listed countries, and must apply directly to their chosen university, which assesses applications and selects recipients. The Semester 2, 2026 round closed at 3:00pm AWST on 29 May 2026, and the Semester 1, 2027 round has not yet opened.
official_details.program_type: State government scholarship administered by participating universities
official_details.coverage: Course fees and other university costs only, at $50,000 per year; no living-cost, airfare or relocation component is published.

official_details.description: The La Trobe High Achiever Scholarship gives high-achieving international students a tuition fee discount of up to 25% for the duration of their course. Applicants are automatically considered once they apply for a course on La Trobe's list of eligible courses, and the percentage is set by weighted average mark: 20% for a WAM of 60 to 74.9 and 25% for a WAM of 75 or above. records.description: The SNU President Fellowship Program is one of Seoul National University's most prestigious scholarship programmes, launched to provide opportunities for teaching and instructional staff members of universities in developing countries to pursue PhD degrees at SNU. The application is made at the same time as the online application for admission to SNU, and the deadline falls during the international student admission period each semester.

records.description: The KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship is KAIST's most competitive graduate scholarship tier, covering full tuition and paying a monthly stipend of 1,000,000 KRW for four regular semesters. It is open to international applicants for Master's and Master's-Ph.D. Integrated programmes in all departments except the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track). There is no separate application: applicants select the KAIST scholarship option in their admission application and are automatically considered, but only highly competitive applicants are recommended by their department head. Applications are assessed on the Spring, Fall Early and Fall Regular admission cycles.

records.description: The KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KPS) is one of two named awards inside the KAIST Scholarship scheme for international graduate students, the other being the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KGPS). KAIST's Office of Admissions states that KPS is open to international applicants in Master's-Ph.D. Integrated or Ph.D. programmes in all departments and provides full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend of 300,000 KRW for eight regular semesters. Applicants are considered automatically for KPS by selecting the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the admission application; candidates with outstanding academic and research achievements are recommended by the department head and selected by the college dean.

records.description: The KOICA Scholarship Program (SP) is a Government of Korea scholarship administered by the Korea International Cooperation Agency within its CIAT (Capacity Improvement and Advancement for Tomorrow) fellowship programme. KOICA lists the benefits as full tuition fees, one round-trip airfare, settlement allowance, dormitory accommodation, monthly allowance, national health insurance, private medical insurance and a scholarship completion grant. records.description: The TU Graz High Potentials scholarship programme supports young talent from Austria and abroad with scholarships of up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's students and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's students over a period of up to two years. The programme is funded by partner companies, so individual scholarships carry their own sponsor requirements in addition to TU Graz's general criteria. TU Graz publishes separate application windows for the two degree levels: 15 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 for the Master's scholarships and 5 May 2027 to 7 July 2027 for the Bachelor's scholarships. Recipients also receive personal mentoring and access to a global alumni network, and TU Graz reports that it has supported around 200 students in total, with 13 scholarships awarded at the most recent ceremony in November 2025.

records.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July, online interview, then acceptance or rejection - and the Institute states that applying does not guarantee a scholarship place because positions are very limited. Successful applicants are expected to show financial need, good study progress, interest in development-related issues and a willingness to attend monthly meetings and actively contribute to the programme. Regarding equally qualified individuals, priority is given to female students.

official_details.description: The Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg's One World Scholarship gives EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) to students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who are studying in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme at the University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg or the Mozarteum. The selection is a documented multi-stage process ending in an online interview, and the Institute emphasises that applying does not guarantee a place. Holders are expected to attend monthly meetings, organise an event during the year and contribute to the programme, and priority is given to female applicants among equally qualified candidates.

records.description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,120 for a maximum of 24 months. Funding is granted in six-month blocks confirmed by an interim progress report from the dissertation supervisor, and the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding six months. Applicants must be enrolled as regular students and registered for continuation with a registered dissertation, and must evidence excellent academic success - an excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study - or scientific achievements; a maximum of two resubmissions is possible. The University states that at least 50 per cent of available funding is to be awarded to women in order to promote young female scientists, and that applicants of equal scientific quality are prioritised if they work in the University's main research areas or on project proposals. Payments are made exclusively by SEPA transfer.

official_details.description: ISTA funds its PhD students through employment rather than through a conventional scholarship: PhD students are employed by the Institute, receive a five-year contract and internationally competitive salaries, and get full social security coverage including health insurance plus financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops. Published 2026 gross salaries range from EUR 3,053 to EUR 3,673 per month depending on whether the student holds a Bachelor's or Master's degree at admission, are paid 14 times a year, and increase on passing the Qualifying Exam about 1.5 years into the degree. ISTA charges no tuition and no application fees. The 2027 call opens in late October 2026 with an application deadline of 8 January 2027, and ISTA cannot fund visa or relocation expenses.

records.description: The CeMM doctoral programme in molecular technologies and systems medicine, run with AITHYRA and university partners, recruits fully funded PhD positions in molecular medicine and biomedical AI in Vienna. CeMM states it was established in 2006 and has attracted students from 44 countries, with more than 115 graduates and 84 current doctoral researchers. Eligibility requires a relevant Bachelor's or Master's degree, at least a 2:1 or first-class result, significant research experience for Bachelor's holders, and excellent English, since English is the working language. The previous joint AITHYRA-CeMM call closed on 30 January 2026; AITHYRA has announced that it will open a new call in September 2026 for a programme starting September 2027.

records.description: The Helmut Veith Stipend is an annually awarded grant for women pursuing a Master's programme in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English, created in memory of Professor Helmut Veith (1971-2016). TU Wien states the benefits as "EUR 7000 per year" plus a "Waiver of tuition fees at TU Wien". The fund is set up by TU Wien, the Wolfgang Pauli Institute and the colleagues and friends of the late Prof. Veith. Applications are submitted electronically through the TU Wien job portal and are due by 30 November each year.

records.name: FWF ASTRA Awards
records.description: The FWF ASTRA Awards are a career funding programme launched in July 2024 for advanced postdocs in Austria who already have experience with independent research (R3 level). The FWF awards between EUR 500,000 and EUR 1 million per project over five years, plus an additional EUR 200,000 tenure package for female principal investigators who secure a permanent position within the first three years. The programme is decided by the FWF Scientific Board on the recommendation of an international jury following peer review and a hearing, with about 18 awards per call and half of them awarded to women. Proposals are submitted through the elane portal during a published annual application window, which was closed on the verification date.

records.description: The University of Vienna's SSH Call 2026 is a central recruitment call offering at least 40 fully funded four-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies across nine participating doctoral schools, including the Vienna Doctoral School in Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience (CoBeNe). Positions are 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement §48 VwGr. B1, paid at a monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 paid 14 times per year, and employees are exempt from tuition fees. Applications for the 2026 round ran from 7 January to 2 March 2026 at 14:00 CET through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool, with employment starting between 1 July and 1 October 2026. The University runs a central doctoral call annually, so the next cycle is expected but its dates were not yet published on the verification date.

records.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. The current DAAD announcement sets a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus insurance cover, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly family allowance. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal and are open annually, with deadlines updated in the second quarter of each year; on 2026-10-04 the DAAD stated that applications for the 2027 funding period were closed.

official_details.description: The DAAD research grant offers doctoral candidates and early postdocs the opportunity to realise a research project at a state or state-recognised university or a non-university research institute in Germany, in agreement with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates can be funded for 2 to 12 months and postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the funding cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. Value is a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. German language support and TestDaF or DSH fee reimbursement are also limited to stays over six months. Eligibility requires that the doctorate started no more than 3 years before the deadline (or that a postdoc doctorate was completed no more than 4 years before it), that the doctorate is being done outside Germany, and that the applicant has not been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline. An independent selection committee of specialist scientists assesses academic qualification, the quality of the research project and the applicant's potential, also giving due consideration to equal opportunities. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal, with deadlines updated annually in the second quarter.

records.name: DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates (HSK)
records.description: The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds four-week German language, cultural studies and technical language courses at German universities and affiliated language schools for students and graduates from eligible countries. The scholarship covers the cost of the language course, provides accommodation in a single room through the course provider for the duration of the course, pays a one-time allowance of EUR 475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and personal liability insurance. Applications are accepted each year from 1 September to 30 October at 23:59 Central European Time, and courses run between June and September.
records.notes: The courses run for four weeks between June and September, and the grants are not extendable. The DAAD transfers the one-time allowance and any travel allowance to the course provider, who disburses it in cash to scholarship holders on site, so those amounts are not paid into a bank account abroad. Accepted language certificates are onSET-Deutsch, TestDaF, Goethe Institut Zertifikat, DSD, DSH, telc Deutsch and OSD-Zertifikat; for subject-specific language courses the Abitur is also accepted as proof of German proficiency.

official_details.description: The aim of the DAAD University Summer Courses programme is to deepen knowledge of the German language, both general and technical, and to augment knowledge of regional studies. It funds students and graduates from eligible countries to attend four-week language, cultural studies and technical language courses at state or state-recognised German universities and affiliated language schools, taught exclusively in German and attended in person between June and September. The scholarship covers the cost of the language course, provides single-room accommodation through the course provider for the duration of the course, pays a one-time allowance of EUR 475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and personal liability insurance. Applicants must be enrolled at a university in a programme country other than Germany both at application and throughout the scholarship, be at least 18 at the start of the course, and prove German proficiency with a certificate no older than one year. Applications run from 1 September to 30 October each year, closing at 23:59 CET, and a selection committee reviews previous academic achievements and the letter of motivation.

official_details.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme, also known as Public Policy and Good Governance, is designed to academically qualify future leaders in social and political science, law, economics, public policy and administration according to the principles of Good Governance. Funded by the Federal Foreign Office, it gives very well qualified graduates with a first university degree from developing or emerging countries the chance to obtain a master's degree in disciplines of special relevance for the social, political and economic development of their home country or region, and prepares them for future leadership positions in the Global South. Scholarships are granted for selected English-taught master's courses at seven participating German higher education institutions: Social Protection at Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg; Development and Governance at the University of Duisburg-Essen; Public Policy at the Erfurt School of Public Policy; Peace and Conflict Studies at the University of Magdeburg; Management in Nonprofit Organisations at Osnabrueck University of Applied Sciences; Development Studies and Governance and Public Policy at the University of Passau. Both young graduates and mid-career professionals may apply. Applications are submitted directly to the universities, not to the DAAD, during the 1 June to 31 July window. Scholarship holders study in small groups with special tutoring, take part in networking events and tailor-made workshops, and attend a German language course in Germany for up to six months before the master's studies.

records.description: DAAD study scholarship for graduates in the arts to continue their education in Germany with a postgraduate or complementary course in Fine Art, Design, Visual Communication and Film. Funding covers a Master's/postgraduate degree course or a one-year complementary course without degree at a state or state-recognised German university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend of EUR 992 plus a travel allowance, a one-off study allowance and insurance payments; it does not pay tuition fees. Selection is made by a DAAD specialist committee of professors from German art, design and film schools on the basis of the written application and the artistic portfolio.

records.description: DAAD study scholarship for graduates in the performing arts to continue their education in Germany with a postgraduate or continuing course of study. records.name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship
records.description: Scholarship of the Heinrich Böll Foundation for international students who have completed their first degree abroad and intend to start a Master's degree in Germany, and for international PhD candidates who completed their graduate degree abroad. Applications are accepted in two rounds a year. Master's students funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive a base scholarship of EUR 992 per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to EUR 100 and optional components; PhD candidates funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive EUR 1,500 per month plus health insurance of up to EUR 200 per month. The funds come from the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA).
records.deadline: Two rounds per year. Spring 2027: 15 January 2027 until 1 March 2027 (online portal opens 15 January 2027 and closes 1 March 2027). Fall 2027: 15 July 2027 until 1 September 2027.
records.application_period: 15 January 2027 to 1 March 2027, and 15 July 2027 to 1 September 2027
records.eligibility_summary: International students who have completed their first degree abroad can apply before starting a Master's programme in Germany. International PhD students who completed their graduate degree abroad can apply for a PhD in Germany. Priority is given to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of their application.

records.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation)
records.official_source: MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)
records.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who want to study as undergraduate students at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Applicants first pass a First Screening (documents, written academic examinations and interview) at the diplomatic mission in their country, are recommended to MEXT, and then pass MEXT's Second Screening. The scholarship pays a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on return, back to the grantee's home country. The scholarship period is five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education, or seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and six-year pharmacy courses.
records.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education; seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course; four years for grantees placed directly at a university
records.deadline: No single central date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by the deadline that mission sets, and that date is not published by MEXT. MEXT states applicants are informed of the final selection result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027, and that grantees must in principle arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
records.application_period: Annually; the 2027 cycle guidelines were published by MEXT in April 2026 and applications were made to Japanese diplomatic missions during the first half of the year
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality at the time of application. They must satisfy one of the listed academic-background conditions (normally 12 years of schooling outside Japan, completed by March 2027), must be willing to learn Japanese and to study in Japanese in principle, and must in principle be within MEXT's eligible age limit. Grantees must be able to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible, with a limited exception for dual nationals resident outside Japan who renounce Japanese nationality on arrival
One of the listed academic-background conditions, normally 12 years of schooling completed outside Japan by March 2027
Applicants must be willing to learn Japanese and be interested in Japan
In principle, applicants must be willing to carry out their academic studies in Japan in Japanese
Age limit in principle, as set out in section 5 of the application guidelines
Able in principle to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027, with departure from the home residence on or after 1 April 2027
coverage: Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 117,000
Supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month for study in specially designated regions
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the university
One-way economy-class airline ticket from the grantee's country to Japan
Return economy-class airline ticket from Japan to the grantee's home country on graduation

Direct Placement Preference Form, submitted after the First Screening by eligible applicants
School records or academic transcripts showing grades and the grade scale used
Certificate of graduation from upper secondary school, or certificate of prospective graduation

Recommendation letter

Japanese or English language proficiency certificates, if held (issued no earlier than two years before application)
Passport or other nationality evidence
records.english_requirement: Applicants must in principle be willing to carry out their academic studies in Japan in Japanese. MEXT provides one year of preparatory Japanese language education before university enrolment for grantees who attend a preparatory educational institution. Japanese or English proficiency certificates are optional and must have been issued no earlier than two years before the date of application to the diplomatic mission.

Applicants must sit the First Screening written examinations and interview at the diplomatic mission
application_method: Obtain the FY2027 application guidelines and forms from the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of your nationality
Complete the Application Form and assemble the required supporting documents
Submit both the original set and the copy set to the diplomatic mission by its deadline
Sit the First Screening written examinations and interview at the diplomatic mission
Submit the Direct Placement Preference Form after passing the First Screening, if eligible
Await the final result, notified by the diplomatic mission after February 2027
records.selection_notes: The Japanese diplomatic mission conducts the First Screening through examination of submitted documents, written academic examinations and interviews; MEXT then conducts the Second Screening of the recommended applicants and selects candidates from each course. Written examination subjects depend on the chosen field: Social Sciences and Humanities applicants take Japanese, English and Mathematics; Natural Sciences applicants take Japanese, English, Mathematics and either Chemistry or Physics. Reasons for screening results are not disclosed and objections to the decision on university placement are not accepted.
records.program_type: Undergraduate scholarship (embassy recommendation)
records.best_fit: Students from countries with diplomatic relations with Japan who have completed about 12 years of schooling outside Japan and want an undergraduate place at a Japanese national university.

The grantee is recommended to bring at least about US$2,000 for immediate expenses on arrival, because the first scholarship instalment is paid one to one and a half months after arrival.

legacy_titles: MEXT Scholarship for Research Students (University Recommendation)
mext scholarship for research students (university recommendation)
records.official_source: MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)
records.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who wish to pursue research study at a Japanese university under the university-recommendation route, meaning the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT. The monthly allowance depends on the course enrolled in: JPY 117,000 for regular students in bachelor degree courses, JPY 144,000 for master's or professional degree courses and JPY 145,000 for doctoral courses, with a supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions. Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees must be paid by the accepting university, and MEXT stipulates the travel route and provides an economy-class airline ticket. The scholarship period is the necessary period for completion of the relevant regular course.
records.duration: The necessary period for the completion of the respective regular course; the guidelines note that for adopted five-year doctoral courses the first two years count as a master's course and years three to five as a doctoral course, so students must apply for extension when advancing to the third year
records.deadline: No applicant-facing deadline is published. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT, so the application timetable is set between MEXT and each university and is not announced publicly.
records.application_period: Annual. MEXT publishes the guidelines for the coming year and calls universities for nominations; students apply through their prospective or current Japanese university rather than directly to MEXT
records.eligibility_summary: International students seeking research study at a Japanese university who are nominated by that university under the university-recommendation route. MEXT's aim is to foster human resources who will become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan through study in Japan and who will contribute to the development of both countries and the wider world. Extensions of the scholarship period for advanced study are permitted for doctoral students in five-year doctoral courses and for master's courses progressing to the doctoral phase, but not for bachelor degree courses or for master's courses progressing to a professional degree course.
eligibility: Nominated by a Japanese accepting university under the university-recommendation route
Enrolled in a regular course corresponding to the level for which the scholarship is awarded (master's or professional degree course, or doctoral course)
Meets the nationality, age and academic-background conditions set out in the application guidelines
Able to arrive in Japan within the period designated by MEXT for the intake year

Applications for extension of the scholarship period due to advanced study are not acceptable for bachelor degree courses, preparatory education and bachelor degree courses, master's courses (doctoral course first phase), or professional degree courses
coverage: Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 144,000 for regular students in master's or professional degree courses
Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 145,000 for regular students in doctoral courses
Monthly scholarship allowance of JPY 117,000 for regular students in bachelor degree courses
Supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions
Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees paid by the accepting university
Economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on completion, back to the grantee's home country

records.english_requirement: Not applicable to the MEXT selection at this level: under the university-recommendation route admission is decided by the accepting university, which sets its own language requirements for the course. MEXT's guidelines for this route do not set an MEXT-level English or Japanese test requirement.

records.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Japanese Studies Students, an embassy-recommendation programme for students from abroad who are already enrolled at a university outside Japan, major in Japanese language or Japanese culture, and come to Japan for a one-year non-degree training course at a Japanese university. The scholarship pays JPY 117,000 per month after arrival, does not collect the university's entrance fee, tuition or entrance examination fee, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on completing the course, back to the grantee's home country. The scholarship period runs from October 2026, or from the month the training course starts, for up to one year, and cannot be extended.
records.duration: Up to one year from October 2026, or from the month the training course starts, covering the period needed to complete that university's training course; extension of the scholarship period is not permitted
records.deadline: No central MEXT date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by that mission's designated deadline, and that date is not published by MEXT. For the 2026 cycle the guidelines required the accepting university to confirm placement by 14 August 2026, and the scholarship period began in October 2026.
records.application_period: Annual embassy-recommendation round. For the 2026 cycle MEXT published the guidelines in December 2025, diplomatic missions screened candidates in early 2026, placement was confirmed by 14 August 2026, and the scholarship period began in October 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Students aged 18 to 30 who, at the time of travelling to Japan and of returning home, are enrolled in the faculty of a university outside Japan and major in Japanese language or Japanese culture. They must have completed at least one cumulative year of Japanese language or Japanese culture study as of 1 September 2026, must not be graduating before September 2027, must not already have held a MEXT scholarship, and cannot apply at the same time as any other MEXT scholarship programme.

records.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The scholarship pays JPY 242,000 per month, the tuition is exempted, and round-trip airfare to and from Japan is provided. Unlike the other six MEXT scholarship types, YLP is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended: recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, the initial selection is by document screening, interview and essay writing, and the final selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT.
records.duration: 1 year
records.deadline: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, so the timetable is set country by country and by the recommending organisation. Applicants must check the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country.
records.application_period: Not published centrally. Recruitment runs through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, at timings that differ by country and region.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under 40 years of age in principle, and must be university or college graduates with practical work experience, or young public administrators, who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The programme leads to a master's course at a Japanese graduate school.

records.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution and face financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for 12 months if the student enrols in April, or for 6 months if the student enrols in September or October. Applications are not made to JASSO directly; the applicant must apply through the school they plan to enrol in. There are three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam, and English courses.
records.duration: 12 months for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March); 6 months for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
records.deadline: No JASSO deadline is published. Applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in, so the deadline is the school's own pre-arrival admission and scholarship nomination deadline.
records.application_period: School-by-school, twice a year, matching the Japanese enrolment cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October). JASSO publishes the eligible school and department lists for each cycle; for 2026 the autumn lists were published in June 2026 and the spring lists in January 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Privately-financed international students planning to enrol as full-time students in Japan using pre-arrival admission, either on the graduate level reservation, the EJU exam reservation, or the English courses reservation, and who face financial difficulties. Research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded from the 'full-time student' definition for this programme.

records.description: The MOFCOM Scholarship is an aid programme hosted by the Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China that offers postgraduate study in China to applicants from developing countries. It runs in two tracks: the MOFCOM-40 direct-admission track of 40 MOFCOM-led projects, and the MOFCOM-CSC joint track operated with the China Scholarship Council. Through the Chinese Embassy in Sierra Leone, applicants register on the CSC portal under institution code 00010, select three target universities and majors, and email the full document set to the embassy. The official programme PDF states free on-campus accommodation and annual stipends of RMB 36,000 for master's and RMB 42,000 for PhD students. Admission is decided by the receiving university.

records.selection_notes: Tsinghua states that applying for CGS through Tsinghua is highly competitive and that it usually selects candidates from pre-admitted applicants of remarkable merit. Applicants who cannot be reached or who fail to complete the CGS online application in time are treated as renouncing the candidacy. All CGS holders must pass a strict annual review covering academic performance, learning attitude, attendance, student conduct, rewards and punishments; the scholarship is suspended or terminated if the review is failed.
records.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS) is funded by the Chinese government and administered by the China Scholarship Council, which is entrusted by the Ministry of Education with admission, enrolment and administration of recipients. Tsinghua University hosts the Category Type B route, in which the university nominates candidates under the CGS-Chinese University Program, and the page also explains that Type A programmes are handled by other authorities such as the bilateral, EU and AUN programmes. This record covers the Type B route for graduate study at Tsinghua. Full CGS covers tuition, university accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, for one to three years of master's study or four to five years of doctoral study.

official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The page states 'Full CGS: tuition fees, free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy, stipend, and comprehensive medical insurance'. A Partial CGS variant exists that includes only one or some of those items.

official_details.description: Tsinghua University's official page for the Chinese Government Scholarship explains both Category Type A (handled by other authorities) and Category Type B, which Tsinghua hosts under the CGS-Chinese University Program. Applicants must be pre-admitted to Tsinghua and recommended by the admitting school or department before the CSC online application is filed; applications without that recommendation are not processed. Full CGS covers tuition, dormitory or accommodation subsidy, stipend and comprehensive medical insurance for 1-3 years of master's study or 4-5 years of doctoral study. Holders must pass an annual review to continue receiving the award.

records.description: Entrusted by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences recruits outstanding young graduate students from around the world for master's and doctoral study and provides full scholarships. The award exempts tuition (RMB 40,000 per year for PhD, RMB 30,000 for master's) and the RMB 600 application fee, pays a monthly stipend of RMB 5,000 for PhD and RMB 3,500 for master's students, provides free accommodation on the Beijing campus or an off-campus subsidy, and includes medical insurance of RMB 800 per person. Sponsorship runs for 36 months, with up to 12 months of permitted extension for doctoral students. Applications must be filed in both the CSC system and the UCAS admission system before the published deadline.

records.description: The Silk Road Program is one of Nankai University's Chinese Government Scholarship streams for international students from ten named countries. Applicants apply through Nankai University's online platform by 18 May 2026, are interviewed, and if nominated complete the CSC application under Program Type B with Nankai as agency number 10055.

official_details.description: Global Excellence Postgraduate Scholarships are awarded to exceptional international students who have received a course offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity College Dublin. Scholarships range in value between €2,000 and €5,000 depending on the region and are applied as a one-time reduction to tuition fees. Applicants must have non-EU fee status, and applications are assessed and awarded on a rolling basis against the deadline for their region. Business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt, and students from China are directed to the Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship.

official_details.description: The Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships are offered by the New Zealand Government to eligible citizens from developing countries to study at a New Zealand or Pacific education institution. The tertiary strand is a full scholarship for eligible international students to study full-time, at one of eight universities or three institutes of technology in New Zealand or one of two Pacific universities. Applications are made online through the Manaaki applicant portal and require an academic transcript including the grading scale; shortlisted applicants must supply verified English translations.

records.description: LUT University reduces tuition for fee-paying students of its two-year master's programmes in two automatic steps. In the first academic year every tuition-liable student who accepts the study place and pays the remaining EUR 10,000 of the first-year fee within 21 days of the official admission email receives an early bird discount of EUR 5,000. In the second academic year every tuition-liable student who has completed at least 60 ECTS credits in accordance with their personal study plan, with those credits recorded on the Transcript of Records by 31 July, and who pays the second-year fee on time receives a LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000. Neither award requires a separate application and neither covers living costs.

records.description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: Norwegian PhD candidates are not treated as students and are normally employees of the institution that funds them. Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no. records.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees are integrated international master's programmes jointly delivered by at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or Programme-associated third countries. The European Commission funds the programmes and offers EU scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide at EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, usually between October and January for entry the following academic year.
records.deadline: In most cases you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. Deadlines are set by each individual consortium.
records.application_period: Each consortium sets its own deadlines; the European Commission states that in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in the final year of bachelor's studies, and must graduate before the master's programme starts. Applicants may apply with a demonstrably equivalent level of learning if it is officially recognised in the degree-awarding country. Students from all over the world are eligible, and each master's website lists its own entry requirements.

records.description: The Stipendium Hungaricum is a Hungarian Government scholarship programme, implemented by Tempus Public Foundation, to promote the internationalisation of Hungarian higher education and to attract international students. Applicants must be nominated by the responsible Sending Partner in their own country or region and apply through the Tempus Public Foundation online system, which lists 30 Hungarian universities and colleges and more than 900 study programmes, with a maximum of two programme choices. Holders have their tuition fees covered and receive a monthly stipend plus an accommodation contribution, and must reside in Hungary during the study period. The programme runs a single annual application round, and for 2026/2027 the deadline was 15 January 2026, 2 p.m. CET.

records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be nominated by the responsible Sending Partner (for example the Hungarian Embassy, the relevant ministry or council in their country) and may apply only to study programmes supported by the cooperation agreement between Hungary and their country or region. Selection requires nomination by the sending partner, a successful institutional entrance examination scoring at least 56 out of 100 points, and the agreed minimum credit requirement.

records.description: The Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship Programme, authorised by Government Decree 203/2020 and implemented by Tempus Public Foundation, funds Hungarian citizens and people of Hungarian origin living in the diaspora to study in Hungary. Applicants must live in a diaspora region as a foreign citizen with a foreign address of residence and must be recommended by a Hungarian diplomatic mission or by a Hungarian diaspora organisation in their country. The 2026/2027 call covered 33 Hungarian higher education institutions with nearly 1300 study programmes, and applications were submitted in the DreamApply system by 2 February 2026, 2 p.m. CET. Selection runs through five points from a technical check in February to a Diaspora Scholarship Committee session in May 2026.
records.deadline: The deadline for submitting the complete application: 02 February 2026 - 14:00 (2 p.m., Central European Time).
records.application_period: One application round per year. For 2026/2027: preparation in November 2025, deadline for submitting applications 2 February 2026; technical check February 2026; validation of recommendations 28 February 2026; institutional admissions March-May 2026; evaluation of motivation letters April 2026; Diaspora Scholarship Committee session May 2026; selection results notified June 2026; visa process July-August 2026; arrival in Hungary September 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must have Hungarian roots evidenced in a diaspora motivation letter, live in the diaspora region as a foreign citizen with a foreign address of residence, and hold a recommendation from the Hungarian diplomatic mission accredited to that country or from a Hungarian diaspora organisation there. Applicants must also agree to support the local Hungarian diaspora with community work after obtaining their diploma, and must not previously have held the Diaspora Scholarship or another Hungarian Government scholarship at the same or a higher level.

records.description: Central European University awards need-based financial aid on academic merit to admitted students who indicate their interest in the funding section of the CEU Application Form, and who must begin their studies at the Vienna campus in the fall of the academic year for which the award is made. At bachelor's level the aid is a Partial Tuition Award of up to 50% of the tuition fee, capped at EUR 4,000 per academic year. At master's level candidates receive a Master's Tuition Award covering 50% to 80% of the tuition fee, with a Full Tuition Award only in exceptional cases, plus an optional Master's Stipend Award of EUR 300 to EUR 750 per month. At doctoral level the CEU Doctoral Scholarship covers the full cost of tuition together with a monthly stipend. Candidates from any country may apply. For the 2026/2027 academic year the Round 1 deadline is 15 October 2026 and the Round 2 deadline is 2 February 2027, so the programme is currently open.

official_details.description: Central European University (CEU) is a non-profit private university founded in 1991 and based in Vienna since 2019, with around 1,500 students from more than 100 countries pursuing bachelor's, master's and doctoral programs accredited in both the United States and Austria. CEU grants need-based financial aid on academic merit to admitted students from any country who indicate their interest in the Funding section of the CEU Application Form, and who are able to begin their studies at the Vienna campus in the fall of the academic year for which the award is made. The packages differ by level: a Partial Tuition Award of up to 50% of tuition, capped at EUR 4,000 per academic year, at bachelor's level; a Master's Tuition Award covering 50% to 80% of tuition, with a Full Tuition Award only in exceptional cases, plus an optional Master's Stipend Award of EUR 300 to EUR 750 per month, at master's level; and the CEU Doctoral Scholarship covering the full cost of tuition together with a stipend of EUR 2,002 gross per month awarded for 48 months in total, at doctoral level. Financial aid can be requested in admission Rounds 1 and 2 only.

records.description: The Banach NAWA programme funds full-time second-cycle (master's) studies conducted in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education. It is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland and the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange, delivered as Polish development aid, and is open to citizens of the 36 countries covered by Polish Aid in Eastern Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America. records.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Scholarship Programme supports master's and post-master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe, awarded for a period of 1 or 2 semesters; within the In-Coming scheme, master's applicants can be awarded 1- to 4-semester scholarships. It is open to citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine, and all applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university studies. Because it is a mobility scholarship, the host country varies with the chosen institution rather than being a single destination. The Fund's own site shows the next application round opening on 1 January 2027; no closing date for that round is published yet, and the funding amounts are not stated on the pages read, so funding_type and funding_amount are left unresolved rather than guessed.

official_details.description: The International Visegrad Fund awards Visegrad Scholarships for study or research to master's and post-master's students and researchers from twelve countries: Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine. Applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university studies. The awards are for one or two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe, and within the In-Coming scheme master's scholarships can be awarded for one to four semesters. The Fund's stated purpose is to foster creativity and promote understanding between people across borders, looking for individuals pursuing innovative ideas in science and education who wish to engage in conversation on development and cooperation in the Visegrad region. Applications for the next round open on 1 January 2027.

records.name: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship (stypendium rektora)
legacy_titles: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship for International Students
jagiellonian university rector's scholarship for international students
records.description: Jagiellonian University's Rector's Scholarship is a merit-based cash benefit from the university Scholarship Fund for first-cycle (bachelor), second-cycle (master) and long-cycle master's students, awarded on request for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements. In the first year of first-cycle or long-cycle master's studies it goes to students admitted in the year of the matura exam who won an international olympiad or were laureates/finalists of a central-level olympiad, or who medalled in at least a Polish Championship competition; in higher years it is capped at 10% of students in a given programme. Foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may apply regardless of citizenship. The award runs for nine months (October to June), paid monthly into a Polish zloty (PLN) bank account held at a bank in Poland.
records.deadline: Official wording: "The deadline for submitting the application for the Rector's scholarship is October 20 of the academic year for which the scholarship is to be awarded." The last published schedule (2025/2026) showed applications open from 1 to 20 October.
records.application_period: Annual. Published 2025/2026 schedule: rector's scholarship applications from 1 October to 20 October, submitted electronically in USOSweb.
records.eligibility_summary: Enrolled in first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle master's studies at Jagiellonian University; not available to students who already hold a master's degree (or a bachelor's degree when re-enrolling in first-cycle studies), including degrees obtained abroad; not available to conditionally enrolled students, students who repeated a year without completing the next one, or students resuming after removal from the student list. Foreign students admitted from 2019/2020 onward qualify regardless of citizenship. Total eligibility is 12 semesters, with a maximum of 9 semesters for first-cycle and 7 for second-cycle studies.
eligibility: Enrolled in first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies at Jagiellonian University

First year of first-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies and admitted in the year of the secondary school-leaving exam (matura), and a winner of an international olympiad or winner/finalist of a central-level olympiad, or a medalist in at least the Polish Championship competition in a sport
Higher years: outstanding academic performance, scientific or artistic achievements, or sports achievements at least at national level

First-year second-cycle (master's) students may apply on the basis of the GPA and achievements from the final year of their first-cycle studies, provided they started the master's programme in the year they completed the bachelor's
Foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward, regardless of citizenship or study terms
Must not already hold a master's degree, nor a bachelor's degree when re-enrolling in first-cycle studies, including degrees obtained abroad
coverage: Monthly cash stipend paid October to June (9 months per academic year)
Paid by bank transfer to a Polish zloty (PLN) account at a bank operating in the territory of the Republic of Poland
Tax-exempt in Poland and not declared in the annual Polish tax return
required_documents: Certificates confirming every circumstance cited in the application, attached electronically to the application in USOSweb

For first-year second-cycle students who completed first-cycle studies at another university: a certificate confirming the arithmetic GPA for the last year of first-cycle studies (the bachelor's thesis defence grade is excluded)
requirements: Applications for benefits must be submitted online only via the USOSweb system using the "Sign and submit" function
Applications must be submitted within the deadline; order of submissions does not matter
All achievements must be confirmed with an appropriate certificate attached electronically to the application in USOSweb
Achievements reported after submission of the application are not taken into account
The scholarship holder must provide a bank account denominated in Polish zloty (PLN) with a bank operating in Poland
application_method: Log in to USOSweb
Go to the "For everyone" tab, then "Applications"
Choose the rector's scholarship application and use the "sign and submit electronically" function
records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed with a points-based system awarding points for grade average plus academic, artistic and sports achievements; the scholarship goes to students with the highest number of points and is capped at 10% of students per programme/specialisation. For first-year second-cycle students, two separate ranking lists are used (JU graduates by weighted GPA, graduates of other universities by arithmetic GPA), with 10% awarded from each. Ties are broken by: points for academic/artistic/sports achievements, then ECTS credits obtained, then the grade average over the entire course of studies, then the admission result for first-year second-cycle students.
