records.name: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for Students from Developing Countries
records.official_source: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (MŠMT) / Dům zahraniční spolupráce (DZS)
records.description: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for students from developing countries let nationals of designated partner states study at Czech public universities within the Czech foreign development cooperation programme. DZS states that "the Czech Republic offers scholarships to foreigners for a standard period of study in accredited university study programmes provided at public universities, and for courses in the Czech language and vocational preparation". Awards cover a master's study programme in Czech preceded by a one-year Czech language and professional training course, or study in master's and doctoral study programmes conducted in English. Applications are made through an electronic form, then the file passes through the applicant's Czech embassy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT.
records.deadline: Official wording from DZS: "Each candidate is required to submit an electronic application form no later than 30 September." For the 2027/2028 academic year applications opened on 21 August 2026 and the electronic-form deadline was 30 September 2026, which has already passed as of 2026-10-04.

records.eligibility_summary: Open to foreigners without permanent residence in the Czech Republic who are nationals of one of the states that receive Czech foreign development aid and who meet the conditions in the Guidelines for Granting Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic. Czech citizens, EU citizens and other foreign nationals holding a permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic may not apply, and there is no legal entitlement to the award.

official_details.description: Scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic for students from developing countries are part of Czech foreign development cooperation and are run jointly by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with DZS (the Czech National Agency for International Education and Research) carrying out the tasks. They fund a standard period of study in an accredited programme at a Czech public university: a master's programme in Czech preceded by a one-year Czech language and professional training course, or a master's or doctoral programme taught in English. Eligibility is limited to nationals of the partner states listed in each annual call who do not hold permanent residence in the Czech Republic. Applicants submit an electronic form by 30 September, sit the required online tests, and if selected attend an interview at the Czech embassy responsible for their country before the file proceeds to the ministries.

records.name: Charles University Doctoral Study Income (full-time doctoral students)
records.description: Charles University guarantees every full-time doctoral student a doctoral study income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of the doctorate (four years). The income may take the form of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for creative work directly related to preparing the dissertation, or a combination of both, and is often supplemented by research-project awards and teaching remuneration. For bachelor's and master's students the university publishes no general scholarship: its page routes applicants to Czech Ministry of Education scholarship schemes (developing-country, general international and International Visegrad Fund), the Vaclav Havel Bursary, the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, and faculty-level awards whose amounts are set by each faculty's own regulations.
records.deadline: No application deadline. The official page states the doctoral study income is received "during the standard length of your studies (4 years)" by every full-time doctoral student, so it is a standing entitlement rather than a competitive call.
records.application_period: Continuous for the standard length of the doctorate (4 years) once enrolled as a full-time doctoral student.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to any student enrolled full-time in a doctoral study programme at Charles University. The benefit is described as guaranteed for all full-time doctoral students rather than awarded on merit. Separate, competitive awards (ministry scholarships, the Vaclav Havel Bursary, faculty merit scholarships and tuition fee reductions) have their own eligibility and are set by the awarding party.

Within the standard length of the doctoral study programme (4 years)
coverage: Guaranteed doctoral study income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage
requirements: Enrol full-time in a doctoral study programme at Charles University

For faculty awards: consult the faculty's own scholarship and bursary rules and Admission Office, because amounts are set by faculty regulations
application_method: For the doctoral study income: none - it is paid as a guaranteed entitlement to enrolled full-time doctoral students

records.selection_notes: The doctoral study income is not competitive; it is described as a guaranteed minimum. Merit-based scholarships and tuition fee reductions offered by faculties after the first year of study are competitive and faculty-specific.
records.program_type: Institutional guaranteed doctoral study income (stipend or salary) for full-time doctoral students
records.notes: Charles University's own page also lists the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport schemes (developing countries, general international, International Visegrad Fund), the Vaclav Havel Bursary, the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies scholarships, and faculty awards (Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Faculty of Science STARS, Faculty of Social Sciences FSV UK SCHOLARS). Those are distinct awards and are not part of this row.

The only university-level guaranteed funding it describes is the doctoral study income: as a full-time doctoral student you receive an income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage throughout the standard length of the doctorate (4 years), which may be a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage tied to dissertation preparation, or both. legacy_titles: International Visegrad Fund Scholarships — Czech Republic Host
international visegrad fund scholarships — czech republic host
records.description: The International Visegrad Fund runs regional mobility programmes for Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine. The Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays of 2 to 10 weeks for full-time doctoral students and PhD holders to conduct a research project, give lectures or seminars, or study archival material at an institution in a V4 country other than their country of citizenship and residence; it pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments (80% and 20%). The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe and its next cycle opens on 1 January 2027. Other Fund programmes include the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral researchers, the Western Balkans-Visegrad Fellowships, research grants at the Historical Archives of the EU, and a scholarship at the Open Society Archives in Budapest.

records.application_period: Visegrad Fellowship Program: the current call opened 1 September 2026 and closes 30 November 2026 at 12:00. The Fund also states that applications are accepted through the My Visegrad system continuously in two periods, January through May and September through November, but only while capacities last. The Visegrad Scholarship Program opens 1 January 2027.
records.eligibility_summary: Visegrad Fellowship: applicants must be full-time doctoral students or holders of a doctoral degree, and their country of citizenship and current residence (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia or Ukraine) must differ from the host institution's country within the V4 region. Visegrad Scholarship: supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers. Visegrad-Taiwan: doctoral and post-doctoral researchers from V4 countries.

official_details.description: The International Visegrad Fund's fellowships and scholarships fund short research and study stays across the Visegrad Group. The Visegrad Fellowship Program is open to full-time doctoral students and PhD holders from Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine for an in-person stay of 2 to 10 weeks at a host institution in a different V4 country, covering a concrete research project, lectures or seminars, or archival study. It pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments of 80% and 20%. Applications are made electronically through My Visegrad with an identity document, proof of doctoral status, a signed invitation letter from the host and a recommendation letter, all in English. Applications are assessed on academic credentials, the coherence and justification of the research plan, and the regional relevance of the topic and host. The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters and next opens on 1 January 2027.

records.description: This page is Masaryk University's guidance for students who want to come to Brno under the International Visegrad Fund's scholarship programme. The Fund, not Masaryk University, awards and funds the scholarship; the university acts as host and supplies the letter of acceptance needed for the application. The Fund's scholarships are designed for students at the Master's or post-Master's level and are intended for study or research projects abroad, allowing stays of one to four semesters. Applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university by the time they apply, and Masaryk University states that it has hosted several Visegrad scholarship holders in recent years and is open to receiving more.

Applicants must be at Master's or post-Master's level and must have completed at least four semesters of university at the time of applying.

records.description: The Foundation for Science and Technology runs an annual call for PhD studentships under its Regulation for Studentships and Fellowships (RBI) and Research Fellowship Holder Statute (EBI). The regular line of application covers all scientific areas and funds research carried out in scientific and academic institutions, including public and private higher education institutions, R&D units, Associated Laboratories and other private non-profit R&D bodies, at home or abroad. Selected applicants receive a monthly allowance plus complementary support such as tuition fees, support for additional training, presentation of work at scientific meetings, personal accident insurance and, where applicable, travel and relocation costs. In the 2026 call FCT received 3,628 applications and approved 1,000, a total funding value of 90,625,000 EUR, an approval rate of 28%.
records.deadline: Official wording: "The Call is open from March 2nd to 5:00 pm (Lisbon time) March 31st, 2026." FCT adds that the call "takes place each year in March or, occasionally, between March and April", but no 2027 dates had been published on the page as of 2026-10-04.
records.application_period: Annual. The 2026 cycle ran 2 to 31 March 2026 (closing 17:00 Lisbon time). A separate line of application for research work plans carried out mainly in non-academic institutions exists within the same call.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to applicants enrolled in, or meeting the requirements to enrol in, a PhD programme leading to a doctoral degree. Portuguese citizens, EU member state citizens, third-state citizens, stateless citizens and beneficiaries of political refugee status may all apply. Applicants must not previously have held an FCT-funded PhD studentship or PhD in Industry studentship, must not already hold a doctoral degree, and must live in Portugal permanently and habitually if applying for a studentship based both in Portugal and abroad or entirely abroad.

records.selection_notes: Applications are graded from 0.000 to 5.000 on three criteria: Criterion A, merit of the applicant (30%), Criterion B, merit of the work plan (40%) and Criterion C, merit of the hosting conditions (30%). Applicant merit is split equally between academic career (50%) and personal CV (50%). Ranking is by weighted average, with tie-breaks in the order Criterion B, then Criterion A, then Criterion C. Applications scoring below 3.000 are not eligible for a studentship.

official_details.description: The Foundation for Science and Technology's annual Call for PhD Studentships finances doctoral research in Portugal and abroad under its Regulation for Studentships and Fellowships. The regular line of application covers all scientific areas and is aimed at research in scientific and academic institutions, including public and private higher education institutions, R&D units and Associated Laboratories. Applicants must be enrolled in or eligible to enter a PhD programme, may be of any nationality, must not have held an FCT-funded PhD studentship before, must not already hold a doctorate, and must reside permanently in Portugal if applying for an abroad-based studentship. Applications are submitted exclusively through myFCT, and the Contracting Institution named in the form must validate the application within ten working days or the application is excluded. Selected applicants receive a monthly allowance plus complementary support covering tuition fees, additional training, conference presentation, personal accident insurance and, where applicable, travel and relocation costs. Applications are scored on applicant merit (30%), work plan (40%) and hosting conditions (30%), with a minimum passing classification of 3.000.

records.description: Nova SBE funds its master's students through an institutional portfolio of tuition-fee scholarships and awards. The Nova SBE Merit Scholarship is open to all candidates regardless of country of origin and covers 20% or 50% of the master's tuition fee value. Alongside it sit the Nova SBE Social Mobility Scholarship (20%, 50% or 100% of tuition, for candidates with proven financial need), the Nova SBE Continuity Scholarship (50% or 100%, for Nova SBE bachelor's graduates within a widened income threshold), and a series of partner-funded awards including Accenture (100%), Antonio Serrenho (100%), Banco Primus (100%), Deloitte (100%), Andre Sousa Bessa (100%), Women in Finance (20% or 50%), plus CEMS-specific awards. Scholarships are awarded on a rolling basis, so the available budget can be exhausted before the end of the master's admission cycle, and combined Nova SBE funding is normally capped at 70% of total tuition.
records.deadline: No fixed date is published for the Nova SBE Merit Scholarship. The official wording is "Applications are open for the Fall Intake and cannot be considered after the application to the Master's program has been submitted", and "Scholarships are awarded on a rolling basis to applicants". Partner scholarships with published windows on the same page ran from 13 November 2025 to 23 March 2026 for the Fall Intake.
records.application_period: Rolling award during the master's admission cycle, for the Fall Intake only for the Merit Scholarship. The Social Mobility and Continuity Scholarships are available for both the Fall and Spring intakes. Separate partner scholarships on the same page state explicit windows of 13 November 2025 to 23 March 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: For the Nova SBE Merit Scholarship, all candidates can apply regardless of country of origin; interest must be declared in the master's application form, and the award must be reapplied for against merit criteria at the end of the first year. Individual partner scholarships impose extra conditions such as nationality, household income tiers, a minimum converted bachelor's GPA, enrolment in named master's programmes, or eligibility for a 100% Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarship.

records.description: In support of the Quebec government's science policy, the Merit Scholarship for Foreign Students (PBEEE) supports the internationalization of research activities in Quebec higher education institutions, attracts top foreign researchers and students, and creates cultural links for joint research projects. It is managed by the Fonds de recherche du Quebec - secteur Nature et technologies, which was commissioned by the Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur du Quebec, which provides the funding. The programme has four component types - master's research, doctoral research, postdoctoral and short-term research or professional development - available both to students of all countries and, through five bilateral components, to students from Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia. Recipients must be preselected by a Quebec university or the CCTT network, and scholarship payments begin only after FRQ receives a copy of the study permit (doctoral) or work permit (postdoctoral).

records.program_type: Government exchange scholarship (Indo-Pacific Strategy initiative)
records.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy, funded under that strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia, who conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates, must be Designated Learning Institutions, and must waive tuition fees for recipients. Four award components are offered, from $10,200 to $15,900, with durations of four to eight months.

official_details.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN SEED programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia to conduct short-term study or research in Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates before 11:59 p.m. EDT on March 24, 2026. Four components are offered: college/undergraduate 4 months ($10,200), college/undergraduate 8 months ($15,900), graduate 4 months ($10,200) and graduate 5-6 months ($12,700), covering airfare, health insurance, permit fees, living expenses, ground transport and books, with tuition waived by the host institution.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of one of the 30 eligible countries: an ASEAN Member State, a Pacific Island Country or Mongolia

Find your Canadian host institution early - there is no direct student application, and the institution must want you, waive your tuition, and centralize the application through its international office
Agree the Sustainable Development Goal your proposed study or research will advance, because a letter of intent that does not identify an SDG is 'deemed incomplete and not eligible'

Draft the one-page letter of intent to cover the nature of the work, why Canada and why this institution/programme/supervisor, the career link, the 2030 Agenda link and the SDG, plus the poverty-impact explanation your country requires

Get a one-page letter of support from your instructor, professor or international director on official letterhead dated within the last six months
If you are a graduate student, get a one-page invitation letter from your Canadian supervisor on their institutional letterhead dated within the last six months
Sign the Privacy Notice Statement for non-Canadian participants, dated within the last six months
Prepare a passport or national identity copy and translations of anything not in English or French, and keep each file under 5 MB

Missing the institutional internal deadline - your Canadian host will set one earlier than March 24
A letter of intent that does not identify a Sustainable Development Goal, which makes it incomplete and ineligible

A full-time enrolment letter that does not explicitly confirm full-time status, or submission of a transcript, student card or admission letter instead
Letters dated more than six months before submission

Already holding or having applied for Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
Arriving in Canada outside the permitted window of August 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027, which can cancel the scholarship

Any tuition shortfall if the host institution fails to formally waive tuition in writing
Costs outside the eligible-expense list, such as personal expenses, gifts and non-essential travel
Costs of your own travel to Canada before the scholarship period begins

records.description: Schulich Leader Scholarships are Canada's largest undergraduate STEM scholarship programme, launched in 2012 from a CAD 200 million fund. Every high school or cegep in Canada may nominate one graduating student per year, who then submits a separate scholarship application with two referees.

records.description: The UCAS Scholarship for International Students is a University of Chinese Academy of Sciences award for non-Chinese-citizen students pursuing a Master's or doctoral degree, or attending courses, conducting research or making academic visits at UCAS colleges and CAS institutes. It has two tiers: a full scholarship covering tuition waiver, application fee waiver, monthly stipend, basic accommodation and medical insurance, and a partial scholarship covering only the tuition waiver, insurance and application fee. Awards run for no longer than 36 months, and the full tier publishes RMB 40,000/year (PhD) or RMB 30,000/year (Master's) tuition waived plus a monthly stipend of RMB 2,500 (PhD) or RMB 2,000 (Master's), with a combined total of at least RMB 3,500 or RMB 3,000 once the host assistantship is added.

official_details.description: The Václav Havel Bursary is Charles University's own financial support for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes. Students from countries where humanitarian organisations report violated human rights and freedoms, and where discriminatory measures restrict access to education, may apply once they have been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure. The student submits the Application Form and all documents required under Rector's Directive (Article 2, point 3) to the faculty's Student Affairs Office, and the faculty forwards the complete file digitally via the Dean or an authorised Vice-Dean to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board. Applications are submitted twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October, with the next round closing on 31 October 2026. Proof-of-persecution documents may be submitted in English, and students preparing for Czech-language study may also apply for a contribution towards living expenses. The bursary is governed by Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, effective from 22 December 2025.

records.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It is funded by the International Visegrad Fund, founded by the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and it does not cover tuition. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and their country of citizenship or residence must differ from the host institution's country.

official_details.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program of the International Visegrad Fund supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It operates in two directions: nationals of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia may study in another Visegrad country or in Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia or Ukraine, and citizens of those Eastern Partnership and Western Balkan countries may study in the Visegrad states. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and the country of their citizenship must differ from the host institution's country; previous levels of university studies must have been completed in a third country, and the host institution must be more than 150 km from the applicant's current employer, university or permanent residence. Support is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and tuition is not covered. Applications are submitted online through My Visegrad. For the 2027 cycle the call opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM, the final deadline is 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM, and results are announced on 31 May 2027 at 12:00 PM.

records.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral award covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund, and are awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities, section 91(3)(b). The award is a living-cost contribution and does not cover tuition fees.

official_details.description: The Czech Technical University in Prague awards a scholarship to foreign students under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities, section 91(3)(b), in two tracks. The Master's track is a contribution towards covering the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month, normally awarded for one to two semesters and extendable on excellent study results up to the standard length of the Master programme. The doctoral track is for foreign doctoral students capable of scientific work who study on an English-language doctoral programme at CTU in Prague; it covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months, extendable on excellent work outcomes, and requires a publication in an internationally reviewed journal or an international grant application as an outcome of the stay. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund. Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus and Exchange students, government scholarship holders and other scholarship holders are not eligible. Applicants first obtain their faculty's agreement and then apply through the faculty International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate, and the vice-rector decides on the recommendation of the commission of vice-deans for international relations. The scholarship covers costs of stay and living costs only; tuition fees are not mentioned.

official_details.description: The MARIHE Erasmus Mundus scholarship funds a place on the Master's programme in Research and Innovation in Higher Education, an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by the University for Continuing Education Krems in Austria. It covers the EUR 18,000 participation costs and pays a monthly allowance of EUR 1,400 towards travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, up to EUR 33,600 for the full programme, together with health and accident insurance. Students may be required to fund travel, visa, legalisation and housing costs incurred before the programme starts.

records.description: The Embassy of France in South Africa invites citizens of South Africa, Lesotho and Malawi to apply for Master's or PhD study at French higher education institutions in 2027/28 under the France Excellence scheme. Beneficiaries receive a monthly living allowance, one return economy-class airfare, social security and health insurance, priority student accommodation and exemptions from the visa fee and the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC). Tuition fees are not covered. Because of the opposing hemispheres' academic calendars, laureates follow online French-language courses through the Alliances Francaises network in South Africa from February to July 2027 before departing for France in September 2027.

records.name: Pasteur-Paris University (PPU) International Doctoral Program 2027
records.duration: Three years, starting in October 2027
records.description: The Institut Pasteur runs the Pasteur-Paris University international doctoral programme with Universite Paris Cite, Sorbonne Universite and Universite Paris Saclay for candidates holding a Master's degree or equivalent in life or medical sciences. Selected students are employees of the Institut Pasteur on a three-year working contract and receive a monthly salary of EUR 2,000 including social benefits, a EUR 4,000 welcome bonus, annual round-trip travel reimbursement and EUR 750 per year for conferences. The 2027 call for October 2027 enrolment is open from 1 October to 16 November 2026, with around 15 places offered each year through a three-stage selection ending in an interview week at Institut Pasteur.
records.deadline: The call for enrollment of students in October 2027 will be open from October 1st to November 16th, 2026
records.application_period: Host-laboratory applications 1 October to 16 November 2026; shortlisted candidates submit the joint application by 14 December 2026; interviews at Institut Pasteur in February 2027 with decisions shortly after.
records.eligibility_summary: Master's degree or equivalent in science, medicine or related fields from a university outside France, obtainable by the start of the programme. Holders of a B.A. or B.S. after four years may be considered with at least six months of laboratory experience. Candidates must not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years before the deadline. No age or nationality restriction.
eligibility: Master's degree or an equivalent university degree in science, medicine or related fields from a university located outside France, by the time the programme begins
Students holding a B.A. or B.S. acquired after four years of academic education may be considered with at least 6 months of laboratory experience and a written final report or publication
Students who have already begun doctoral training elsewhere, and students with a Master's degree obtained in France, are not eligible for PPU-Classic, PPU-OXFORD, PPU-EID and PPU-Imagine
Students should not have resided in France for more than 12 months in the three years immediately prior to the application deadline
Candidates must be selected by a host laboratory as part of the application
Host thesis advisors must hold an HDR diploma and the host laboratory must be affiliated with Institut Pasteur Paris and a doctoral school of a partner university

One-off welcome bonus of EUR 4,000 gross
Reimbursement of one round-trip eco-class ticket per year
EUR 750 per year per student for international conferences or summer courses
Assistance with accommodation in the first year
Reduced-fee access to campus amenities, subsidised cafeteria lunches and free WiFi

Select up to four host-laboratory projects during the call
Upload a detailed CV and a motivation letter in PDF format
Complete the joint application with the host laboratory in November, choosing one single project and programme
No application by email is accepted
Candidates who apply to several laboratories may apply to a maximum of four

Upload a detailed CV and a motivation letter in PDF format

Present the Master's degree research and the PhD project at the interview week

Around 15 openings are available each year and admission is highly competitive.

records.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po is the first such programme in continental Europe and supports students from the African continent who wish to pursue a two-year Master's degree at Sciences Po, covering the full financial needs of selected Scholars. Applicants must first be declared eligible and receive an application fee waiver, then apply and be admitted through the International Graduate Admissions Procedure, and finally be selected by the Programme's Selection Committee. For the 2027 intake the fee-waiver window runs from October to mid-December 2026, while the scholarship application timeline itself had not been published on the page as of 4 October 2026. Shortlisted admitted candidates are invited to a roughly 25-minute online interview conducted by Zoom.

Applicants currently enrolled at Sciences Po, or currently enrolled in or graduated from a French higher education institution, are not eligible.

records.name: Hungarian Bilateral State Scholarships
records.description: Hungarian bilateral state scholarships are awarded under scientific and educational cooperation agreements signed by the governments of two countries, with the Hungarian side offering places to foreign students, researchers or lecturers in Hungarian higher education institutions and in scientific or art institutions. Tempus Public Foundation, a background organisation of the Hungarian Ministry of Culture and Innovation, is Hungary's national scholarship office. Applicants can apply either through nomination by their home country's national scholarship office or by submitting an individual application, and in both cases they must also submit into Tempus Public Foundation's online system. Applications undergo a formal eligibility check and are then scored by Tempus Public Foundation's external experts against several professional criteria.
records.deadline: No application deadline is published on the Tempus Public Foundation pages for bilateral state scholarships; applications are submitted into the Foundation's online system and assessed on a rolling basis per bilateral partner.
records.application_period: No fixed dates published. Deadlines are set by each bilateral partner's national scholarship office for nominated applicants.

records.description: The Momentum MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme is a Hungarian Academy of Sciences initiative to attract up to 35 postdoctoral researchers from around the world into Lendulet (Momentum) research groups in Hungary. It is co-funded by the European Commission and the MTA Secretariat under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions, under grant agreement number 101179854 (HORIZON-MSCA-2023-COFUND-01), and runs from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029. Fellows join a Lendulet research group, receive expert supervision, coaching, specialised training, interdisciplinary workshops and networking, and may take secondments at leading Hungarian and international research centres, academic and industrial partners. The amount depends on the faculty, with the highest amounts for the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry and for the Andras Peto Faculty and the lowest for Health Sciences, and it is paid in 12 equal monthly instalments. records.duration: Five years, not extendable
records.description: The Ramanujan Fellowship, operated by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, is a reverse brain drain scheme that brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers from abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. It is scientist-specific and highly selective, restricted to candidates below 40 years of age who hold a higher degree such as a PhD in science or engineering, a master's in engineering or technology, or an MD, with adequate professional experience and a proven track record evidenced by publications and recognition. Fellows must not already hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in an Indian institution or university, and must be working abroad at the time of nomination. The fellowship pays Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA, plus a research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh per annum and Rs 60,000 per annum in overhead charges to the host institute.

Research Ireland runs the programme, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science. The award is worth up to €34,000 per annum for 1-4 years, made up of a €25,000 stipend, a fee contribution of up to €5,750 and €3,250 of eligible direct costs. Applications are assessed by international independent expert peer review.

records.description: The Ireland Fellows Programme offers people from around the world the opportunity to spend one year studying at Master's level in Ireland. It is fully funded by the Irish Government and offered under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and is managed by the Embassy of Ireland responsible for each applicant's eligible country. The award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs for a one-year Master's placement running 10 to 16 months. Roughly 224 Fellowships were awarded for 2025/26 across 48 countries, with applications organised in three annual stages.

Irish and UK candidates are assessed together through the normal Royal Society peer review process. Historical success rates are 7% (2022/23), 6.4% (2023/24), 6.8% (2024/25) and 6.3% (2025/26). Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society.

Funding covers a contribution to salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants. The 2027 round closed on 9 September 2026 with decisions due by 31 May 2027.

official_details.description: The University Research Fellowship (URF) is an eight-year fellowship for outstanding early career scientists with the potential to become leaders in their field, designed to build an independent research career in the UK or the Republic of Ireland. Awards based in the UK are funded by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, while awards based in the Republic of Ireland are funded by Research Ireland and must be hosted within a Research Ireland Eligible Research Body. Applicants can request up to £1,907,400 over eight years to cover a contribution to salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation and visa costs. Shortlisted applicants attend an in-person interview at the Royal Society, and years six to eight of funding are subject to a mid-fellowship review.

official_details.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship is funded by the Erasmus Trustfonds, a fund founded to support research and education projects organised by Erasmus University Rotterdam, and it contributes to the growth and flourishing of the university. It pays EUR 17,500 towards the statutory tuition fee, housing and living costs for one academic year to high-achieving incoming Master's students who cannot finance their own study. The award is administered by the university's participating schools - ESL, ESSB, ESHCC, ESHPM, RSM, ESE, ESPhil and EMC - each of which sets its own eligibility, documentation and deadlines.

official_details.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship / TSH Changemaker Scholarship supports underrepresented students to pursue a Master's programme at Erasmus University Rotterdam. The Erasmus Trustfonds component covers the statutory tuition fee and includes a monthly living allowance of EUR 600, totalling EUR 9,895 for costs of living and the statutory fee for one year, while the TSH Changemaker Scholarship provides one year of housing in a Social Hub Residence. At Erasmus MC the award is limited to applicants to the Health Sciences, Neuroscience and Molecular Medicine Research Master's programmes who have a bachelor average equivalent to Dutch 8.0 and who belong to a disadvantaged or underrepresented group. Applications are submitted through the OSIRIS Cases portal, with the 2026-2027 deadline set at 1 April 2026, 23:59 CET.
official_details.program_type: Combined need- and merit-based Master's scholarship pairing an Erasmus Trustfonds grant with the TSH Changemaker Scholarship
official_details.coverage: Statutory tuition fee, EUR 600 monthly living allowance within a EUR 9,895 living-and-fee award, one year of Social Hub housing, and a partial tuition fee waiver where applicable

records.selection_notes: The fund was established through a partnership between the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund in 2018. It provides one scholarship annually to a Master's student from an Arab country to attend a Master's programme at Leiden University, on the basis of exceptional academic excellence and motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. A separate variant fund, the LUF - Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund: Extra Gaza Scholarship, exists for Gazan students and should not be confused with this award.

official_details.description: The LUF - Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund is intended for students who have demonstrated exceptional academic excellence and a strong motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. Funded through a partnership between the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund established in 2018, it awards EUR 30,000 for one academic year, covering the Leiden University tuition fee and housing fee with the small remainder paid in monthly installments. Eligibility is limited to nationals of nineteen listed Arab countries who hold an admission letter for a one-year Leiden Master's programme or are entering the second year of a two-year Leiden Master's. Leiden University states explicitly that this is not a full scholarship and does not cover all of a recipient's expenses in the Netherlands.

records.selection_notes: The scholarship is based on invitation. The WU Scholarship Selection Committee coordinates selection, and around March-April 2027 a number of applicants are informed by email that they have reached the final stage, at which point a lottery determines the recipients. On 7 April 2027 the scholarship is offered to the selected students and the remaining candidates are placed on a waiting list. Receiving the scholarship is conditional on fulfilling all admission criteria.

Students who are offered and accept the scholarship receive a revised first-year invoice which still includes the living allowance, health and liability insurance, and the residence permit fee; based on the current fee structure that invoice is approximately EUR 16,500 and must be paid before 1 July 2027. WUR's scholarship programmes are for prospective students only, are for the MSc September start only, and WUR does not offer scholarship programmes to students currently enrolled at Wageningen University.

Louise Thijssen-Schoute Foundation in collaboration with the Knowledge and Art Practices research group at the Huygens Institute in Amsterdam. The foundation encourages research into the history of ideas, with a special focus on the seventeenth century and the Dutch Republic, and awards the fellowship to a young researcher at an advanced stage of a PhD or within three years of a PhD defence. The award is a stipend of EUR 2,000 per month for three months, with the research carried out during 2027 and a place of work at the Huygens Institute requiring presence at least three days a week. Applications are submitted as a single PDF by email and were due on 15 May 2026.

official_details.coverage: Monthly stipend of EUR 2,000 for three months plus a place of work at the Huygens Institute. No travel, accommodation or tuition provision is stated.

records.selection_notes: NIAS first checks all applications for eligibility. A ranking committee appointed by the KB then ranks eligible candidates, giving preference to proposals that bring new questions or unexpected dimensions to the KB research agenda. The KB returns its ranking to NIAS, where the Fellowship Advisory Committee assesses it with a view to a cohort balanced in discipline, location, career stage and gender, and advises the NIAS Director, who makes the final decision.

records.notes: NIAS and the KB, the National Library of the Netherlands, established the current fellowship in 2025, continuing an earlier KB Fellowship that ran from 2004 to 2018. It is open to researchers in all scholarly and artistic disciplines whose project relates to the KB research agenda or extends its scope, and proposals with an international or comparative perspective are especially welcome. The funding route depends on affiliation: a personal stipend for the fellow, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the institution for scholars affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute. NIAS does not provide studios, materials or tools for artistic work, although artists may propose artistic production as a research strategy or research ahead of production. Any resulting publications must be published under CC BY 4.0.

official_details.description: The KB Fellowship at NIAS offers researchers and creative practitioners five months to work on the future of the (public) library, on the library as a public institution, or on the library as a pillar of liberal democracy. NIAS and the KB, the National Library of the Netherlands, established the current fellowship in 2025, continuing an earlier KB Fellowship that ran from 2004 to 2018, and one fellowship is awarded each academic year from September to January. Applicants must be scholars at least three years past their PhD or creative practitioners with at least three years of independent practice, with or without institutional affiliation, and submit a project proposal of no more than 1,500 words, a CV of no more than four pages and a statement of no more than 300 words. The fellow receives a personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant paid to the institution for scholars at a Dutch university or research institute, plus an office, research facilities and, where eligible, subsidised Amsterdam accommodation or local transport reimbursement. The call for 2027-2028 opens on 15 January 2027 and closes on 15 March 2027 at 12.00 noon CET.

official_details.coverage: Personal stipend or a Dutch University Grant, an office and research facilities at NIAS, and subsidised Amsterdam accommodation or local public transport reimbursement where eligible. No euro amount is published and travel to the Netherlands is not mentioned.

official_details.description: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship at NIAS offers researchers and policymakers the opportunity to work on topics in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy and public finance. The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation, established in 2007 in honour of Willem F. Duisenberg and supported by De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch Ministry of Finance, ING Group, Rabobank Nederland, ABN AMRO and AEGON, offers one five-month and one ten-month fellowship per academic year. Applicants need a minimum of three years of post-PhD academic experience; the fellowship targets prominent mid- to late-career researchers while encouraging exceptionally talented early-career candidates. Fellows receive a personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant paid to their institution if affiliated with a Dutch university, plus an office, research facilities and subsidised accommodation where eligible. The 2027-2028 call ran from 15 January to 13 April 2026 and is now closed.

records.name: Eric Bleumink Fellowship
records.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of a listed group of countries who hold provisional or unconditional admission to a one or two year master's programme starting in September. The grant covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. It is nomination-based: the University of Groningen's Admission Office decides which admitted applicants are nominated, so there is no direct scholarship application. The University of Groningen states that a considerable number of students apply each year while it can issue only a limited number of grants.
records.duration: 1 or 2 year master's degree programme, starting in September only
records.deadline: There is no scholarship application deadline: "It is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship Scholarship. Suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination." Applicants must hold a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February, and their master's application "should be completed by the applicant before 1st of December".

records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country in Appendix 1 of the fellowship, have received provisional or unconditional admission to a University of Groningen master's programme before February, have excellent academic performance and excellent undergraduate grades, have excellent English matching the chosen programme's admission requirements, be available for the whole programme, be in good health so Dutch health insurance can be arranged, and have no other means of financing the study.

records.name: KITLV Visiting Fellowship
records.official_source: Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV)
records.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.
records.duration: 3 months
records.deadline: The stored 2026 (2nd) call closed at "21 March 2026, midnight (CET)". The next still-applicable deadline published by KITLV is: "If you are interested and eligible, please apply at the latest on 14 October 2026." Selection for the annual programme takes place twice a year via an Open Call.
records.application_period: Open Call, selection twice a year. Eight three-month fellowships are available each year across four periods: March-May, June-August, September-November and December-February. The next call is published in September 2026 and closes 14 October 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities, carry out research in Southeast Asian and/or Caribbean Studies, wish to conduct that research in the Netherlands, be prepared to be based at KITLV for the entire fellowship period, and not be a (tax) resident of the Netherlands. No university or research institute affiliation is required, but fellows must have a steady income during the fellowship.

records.name: Tilburg University Waiver
records.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.

records.deadline: Both the Master's programme application and the waiver webform must be completed by the same date: "Submit your application for a Tilburg University Master's program by April 1, 2027" and "Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form before April 1, 2027". Outcomes are notified by June 1, 2027.
records.application_period: Annual for the September intake. The current cycle is the 2027-2028 academic year (21 waivers), applications open now and close 1 April 2027, with outcomes by 1 June 2027. Waivers are not available for the February intake.

records.name: Radboud Scholarship Programme
records.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a highly selective Radboud University scheme for talented, highly motivated non-EU/non-EEA students with outstanding study results, covering English-taught Master's programmes. A scholarship reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 (the university notes the amount is to be confirmed) instead of an illustrative EUR 19,000, and additionally covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs. Costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028, allocated across six faculties, and selection is based on academic excellence, ambition and the quality of two reference letters.

records.deadline: Two official deadlines: "You must have submitted your application in the online OSIRIS Application system on 31 January 2027 23:59 CET at the latest", after which the application must be complete "by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET at the latest" and "incomplete applications will not be considered for the scholarship selection". Final decisions are notified before mid-April 2027.
records.application_period: Annual cycle for the September 2027 intake. OSIRIS submission by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET, complete application by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, decision before mid-April 2027.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport, not qualify for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons, hold a Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands with no Dutch degrees and no prior education in the Netherlands, meet the English proficiency requirement of the chosen Master's programme, be fully admitted to an English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027, be able to comply with Dutch visa conditions, and enrol as a full-time Radboud student.

records.name: University of Amsterdam Scholarships
records.description: The University of Amsterdam runs several scholarship programmes for talented and motivated international students, published from one official Fees and funding hub. The flagship is the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship for outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA planning a Master's programme at the UvA. Each faculty also runs its own scholarships for international Master's students, covering Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Science and Social and Behavioural Sciences, and a separate set of Bachelor's scholarships exists. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship equals the tuition fee but the UvA states it cannot be used as a partial tuition waiver, so the recipient still pays the full tuition, payable in monthly instalments. Amounts are set annually and are published by each faculty.
records.deadline: The umbrella hub page publishes no single deadline. Deadlines are set per scheme and per faculty: faculty scholarship pages for the Amsterdam Merit Scholarship give an application deadline of 15 January, with results announced at the end of April, while some faculties run a later round with a 2 February deadline. Amounts are determined each year and published in late autumn.
records.application_period: Annual. The main Amsterdam Merit Scholarship round opens at the beginning of October with a 15 January deadline and results at the end of April; individual faculties publish their own rounds, amounts and deadlines, and amounts are published in late autumn.
records.eligibility_summary: The umbrella covers several schemes, so eligibility is scheme-specific. The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship requires outstanding academic results and is open to students from outside the EU/EEA who plan a Master's at the UvA. Individual faculty schemes add their own criteria, and the UvA directs applicants to the relevant faculty page for details.

records.name: Tulī Takes Flight Scholarships
records.description: Tulī Takes Flight scholarships are funded by the New Zealand Ministry of Education and administered by the Pacific Education Foundation to reduce financial barriers to tertiary study and vocational training for Pacific people. They form part of the government's gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific communities following its 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids. Awards can be made for either vocational or academic study and can run for one, two or three years. For the 2027 round the Ministry states applications are closed and outcomes will be notified by 18 March 2027; a new annual round is expected to open in the same late-summer window each year.

records.deadline: Applications for the 2027 round are closed. The Ministry's official page states "Applications for the 2027 round are now closed" and "You will be notified of the outcome of your application by 18 March 2027". The round closes annually on 30 September at 11.59pm; no date for the next still-applicable round is published on the page as at 2026-10-04.
records.application_period: Annual round for study in the following year. The 2027 round closed at 11.59pm on Wednesday 30 September 2026, with outcomes notified by 18 March 2027. The next round is expected to follow the same pattern but no date is published yet.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be enrolled or in the process of enrolling in full-time study or training with a New Zealand tertiary provider, be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, have lived in New Zealand for the last three years, be of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage, and have completed NCEA 3 or equivalent and be 16 or over when the course starts (or 18 or over if already out of secondary school). New-to-study applicants must have done no more than 0.5 equivalent full-time student load of tertiary education; continuing-study applicants must have completed at least one year of study or be entering a second or subsequent year.

For a continuing study award: have successfully completed at least 1 year of study, or be expecting to enter a second or subsequent year of training or study

The remaining scholarships continue to support the full breadth of study including social services, construction, Pacific languages, and Pacific customs and culture. The Tulī programme is distinct from the separate Pacific Education Foundation scholarships and from the Tulī career changer strand.

records.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

records.deadline: The Ministry states "Applications for the 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship open on 1 October 2026" but publishes no closing date for the 2027 round on this page.
records.application_period: The 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and is open now. The internship itself runs July to September 2027. No closing date is published on the official page.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be New Zealand citizens (a NASA requirement), aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, hold a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale with New Zealand grades converted to the US scale, and be proficient in written and spoken English. They must be available in person from July to September 2027, willing to undergo any required health and security checks for US travel and entry to US federal facilities, eligible for a J1 or F1 visa, and able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance. Applicants who hold or have held citizenship of a country on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible.

records.description: The Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is the early-career scheme within the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. It funds employed researchers within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral to build the foundations of an independent research career. Around 20 fellowships are awarded each year, each worth NZ$820,000 over four years, made up of salary contribution, institutional overheads and research expenses. The scheme replaced the previous Rutherford Discovery, Rutherford Foundation and James Cook Research Fellowships.

records.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a partnership between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation, administered in New Zealand by Universities New Zealand – Te Pōkai Tara. It supports outstanding all-round students to undertake postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year, and the Scholarship covers fees, accommodation and living costs for up to three years. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens or hold a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa and must meet an age and undergraduate GPA requirement.
records.duration: Up to three years of postgraduate study at the University of Oxford

records.description: The Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarships are annual awards funded by the Ngarimu VC and 28th (Māori) Battalion Memorial Scholarship Fund Board, established in 1945, and administered through the Ministry of Education. They are awarded to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values aligned with those of the 28th (Māori) Battalion. Following a $100,000 per year increase from the 2026-27 Budget, 14 scholarships are awarded each year across five schemes: 5 VET, 4 undergraduate, 3 master's, 1 Master of Education research and 1 doctoral. Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi and be enrolling in or continuing full-time tertiary study.
records.deadline: Applications to support study in 2027 closed on Sunday 19 July 2026, and the Ministry expects to notify all applicants of outcomes by late November 2026. Applications to support study in 2028 will open mid-2027; no exact 2028 closing date is published.

records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of Māori descent or whakapapa to a recognised Māori iwi, and must be enrolling in or already enrolled to continue full-time tertiary study for the relevant academic year. The selection panel gives preference to applicants whose studies aim to improve the social, economic and cultural wellbeing of Māori. VET applicants need a certificate or diploma at NZQA levels 4 to 7 (minimum 120 credits, full time) and cannot be studying a bachelor's degree.

records.official_source: Ministry of Education — Education Workforce (TeachNZ Scholarships)
records.description: The Kupe Scholarship is one of the Ministry of Education's TeachNZ scholarships, awarded to 20 high-achieving Māori and Pacific students each year who can see themselves as outstanding education role models. It pays the course fees for an approved teaching qualification and provides an allowance of NZD$15,000 over the period of study, limited to three years, plus a Kupe Keepsake. All TeachNZ scholarship recipients must complete a bonding period teaching in a New Zealand state or state-integrated school, kura or early learning centre.
records.deadline: Application period 3 August to 31 August 2026. The Ministry states 'Applications are now closed. Applicants will find out if they are shortlisted in early October 2026. Final notifications will be sent by the end of November 2026.' The next round's dates are not published.
records.application_period: Annual. 2027 round: 3 August to 31 August 2026; shortlisted applicants notified early October 2026 and final notifications by end of November 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of New Zealand Māori or Pacific descent with Māori or Pacific cultural knowledge, demonstrate integrity, leadership and vision, have support from their iwi or Pacific community and Māori or Pacific leaders, be a New Zealand citizen, permanent resident or resident, and either have completed at least one full year of an approved teaching course or hold academic excellence and be enrolled in an approved Graduate Diploma of Teaching or Master of Teaching. Undergraduate applicants need a B+ grade average or above.

official_details.description: The Kupe Scholarship is a TeachNZ scholarship awarded by the Ministry of Education to 20 high-achieving Māori and Pacific students each year. It pays course fees for an approved teaching qualification, provides an allowance of NZD$15,000 over the period of study (limited to three years) and includes a Kupe Keepsake. Recipients must complete a bonding period teaching in a New Zealand state or state-integrated school, kura or early learning centre.
official_details.program_type: TeachNZ scholarship (pre-service teacher training)
official_details.coverage: Approved teaching qualification course fees plus a NZD$15,000 study allowance over the period of study, limited to 3 years.

Get every required document certified by an authorised person

Undergraduate GPA below B+
Enrolling in a qualification that is not on the Teaching Council's approved ITE list

Any study costs not covered by the paid course fees, such as materials or travel to placement

Evidence of Māori or Pacific cultural knowledge

alerts.message: Every TeachNZ scholarship carries a return-of-service obligation: 1-3 years of teaching in a New Zealand state or state-integrated school, kura or early learning centre after you complete study, scaled to the length of your scholarship.
All required documents must be certified by an authorised person, resident visa holders are now eligible, and a video upload is required.

records.description: The University of Otago International Master's Research Scholarship provides funding to support international Master's students studying at the University of Otago. It pays a stipend of NZ$18,204 per annum plus a tuition fee waiver for one year capped at NZ$35,000 for Master's study, excluding the student services fee and insurance. Four awards are offered, normally one per Academic Division. Applicants must be international students undertaking a thesis-based Master's as their first Master's qualification, and selection is based predominantly on academic merit and research potential.

records.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program is a nine-month non-degree professional development scholarship for graduates from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan who already have at least two years of professional experience. Grantees attend two semesters of classes at one of about fifteen affiliated Polish universities, take part in an introductory course, trainings and grantees' conventions, and complete at least two weeks of professional internship. The programme provides support valued at PLN 6,000 per month, free access to university classes, accommodation, health insurance and a return ticket to Poland. It was founded by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and is financially supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA).

records.description: Poland My First Choice NAWA is a Polish government scholarship that funds the statutory period of full-time second-cycle (master's) studies at academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education. Beneficiaries receive the NAWA Director's scholarship of PLN 1,800 per month, an exemption from tuition fees at public universities and a one-time travel lump sum. Applicants choose the university and field of study themselves and must apply for university admission independently of the NAWA application. records.name: UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering
legacy_titles: UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships Programme in Engineering
unesco/poland co-sponsored fellowships programme in engineering
records.duration: 6 months of individual research, 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 in the 2025 edition
records.deadline: 2025 edition: 'National Commissions of invited Member States will select qualified candidates and transmit ... by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time at the latest.' Individual applications are not accepted by UNESCO; only candidates endorsed by their National Commission are considered. That edition is closed and no 2026/27 deadline is published.
records.application_period: Annual edition. For 2025 the National Commissions had to forward nominations by 26 May 2025 for a fellowship running 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Nationals of the invited Member States listed in Annex II (57 states in the 2025 edition) who hold a bachelor's, master's or PhD degree and are nominated by their own National Commission for UNESCO. Because UNESCO is intergovernmental, individual applications are not accepted: the National Commission selects and transmits the application to UNESCO Paris. Specific qualifications per field of research are set in Annex III, and some fields are restricted to particular regions.
eligibility: National of one of the invited Member States listed in Annex II
Holds a bachelor's, master's or PhD degree (certified copies in English, apostilled or legalised)
Endorsed and nominated by the National Commission for UNESCO of their country
Meets the field-specific qualifications in Annex III for the chosen project
Some projects are restricted to candidates from particular regions - check Annex III and Annex IV
coverage: Free tuition for six months and access to university facilities
Monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc candidates) or PLN 2,200 (MSc candidates)
One-time special allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival in Poland
International travel to and from Poland by the most direct, economical route (UNESCO)
Health insurance for fellows declared medically fit (UNESCO)
One-time pocket allowance of USD 120 (UNESCO)
required_documents: UNESCO fellowships application form, all 4 pages, completed in English in capital letters
Copy of the applicant's passport
Copy of the applicant's identity photo
Certified copies in English of bachelor's, master's or PhD degree, apostilled or authorised (legalised where apostille is not recognised)
UNESCO certificate of language knowledge, if the mother tongue is not English
Two letters of recommendation dated 2025 for the 2025 edition
Completed online information sheet once endorsed by the National Commission
records.english_requirement: The UNESCO application form must be completed in English using capital letters; illegible documents are eliminated from evaluation and handwritten forms must be in capitals. Degree certificates must be certified copies in English.
requirements: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your own country first - UNESCO will not accept a direct application
Choose a maximum of three of the 28 proposed projects and give a priority number for each
Submit to your National Commission early enough for it to transmit to UNESCO by the official deadline
Once endorsed, submit the application by e-mail to agh.poland@unesco.org and complete the online information sheet
Pay for your own passport and visa expenses
application_method: National Commission for UNESCO of the candidate's country selects and transmits the application to UNESCO Paris by e-mail
Endorsed candidates then e-mail agh.poland@unesco.org (copy uniune25@agh.edu.pl and Fellowships.Engineering@unesco.pl) and complete an online information sheet
records.selection_notes: Individual applications are not accepted by UNESCO; only applications endorsed by National Commissions are considered, and incomplete or late applications are discarded. The selection of fellowship recipients is made and decided by the concerned Polish authorities, taking into account gender equality and diversity.
records.program_type: Research fellowship
records.best_fit: BSc, MSc and PhD holders from the 57 invited Member States who need their National Commission for UNESCO to nominate them for a six-month engineering research stay at AGH University in Krakow.
benefits: Free tuition for six months plus university facilities
Monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc)
One-time special allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival
International travel to and from Poland covered by UNESCO
Health insurance taken out and paid for by UNESCO
One-time pocket allowance of USD 120
records.notes: There is a sibling award, the Programme of Fellowships under the Polish National Commission for UNESCO, which is a different scheme and must not be merged into this row.
records.description: The UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering place 28 six-month research fellowships at the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology and Engineering at AGH University of Science and Technology in Krakow at the disposal of UNESCO, for candidates from 57 invited developing Member States. The Polish authorities provide free tuition, a monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 or 2,200 and a one-time arrival allowance; UNESCO covers international travel, health insurance and a USD 120 pocket allowance. Applications must be endorsed and transmitted by the candidate's National Commission for UNESCO. The 2025 edition is closed.

official_details.application_cycle: 2025 edition closed; fellowship ran 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026. A new edition is expected but no 2026/27 announcement is published on the UNESCO page as of 2026-10-04.
official_details.deadline_central_display: National Commissions must transmit applications 'by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time at the latest' (2025 edition)
official_details.deadline_note: The only exact deadline published is the 2025 edition's transmission deadline of 26 May 2025, which has passed. No 2026/27 date is published, so deadline_date is null for the next cycle and deadline_precision is 'recurring'.
official_details.status_note: UNESCO states plainly: 'The 2025 edition of this Programme is closed for applications.' The programme is annual, so the next edition is treated as upcoming.
official_details.funding_duration: 6 months
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Official: 'Free tuition for six (6) months and access to the university facilities based on the local regulations.'

Passport and visa costs are not covered.
benefits: Free tuition for six months and access to university facilities
Monthly allowance PLN 1,800 (BSc) / PLN 2,200 (MSc), intended to cover all living expenses and accommodation
One-time special allowance PLN 1,800 (BSc) / PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival, covering the obligatory medical check-up, cultural/historical visits, conferences, workshops and seminars
International travel expenses by the most direct, economical route, paid by UNESCO
Health insurance paid by UNESCO for fellows declared medically fit
One-time pocket allowance of USD 120
eligibility: National of an invited Member State listed in Annex II (57 states in the 2025 edition)
Holds a bachelor's, master's or PhD degree with certified English copies
Endorsed by the National Commission for UNESCO of their country
Meets Annex III qualifications for the selected field of research
Declared medically fit for the health insurance cover

official_details.application_method: Application must be endorsed by the National Commission for UNESCO, which transmits it to UNESCO Paris by e-mail; the endorsed candidate then e-mails agh.poland@unesco.org and completes an online information sheet

requirements: Individual applications are not accepted by UNESCO; only National Commission endorsements are considered

official_details.description: UNESCO and the Polish National Commission for UNESCO place 28 six-month engineering research fellowships at the UNESCO Chair at AGH University of Science and Technology in Krakow at the disposal of developing Member States. official_details.coverage: Full tuition for six months, living allowance, arrival allowance, international travel, health insurance and a USD 120 pocket allowance; passport and visa costs excluded.
