records.name: Erasmus+ Programme
records.duration: Not specified on the official pages read; mobility periods are agreed bilaterally between the sending and receiving institutions
records.deadline: No central deadline is published on study.gov.pl or on the Polish National Agency's site. Erasmus+ calls are announced nationally by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System and by each sending or receiving university, so the deadline varies by institution and call.
records.application_period: Continuous programme with institution-level calls announced each academic year; no single national window is published
records.eligibility_summary: Erasmus+ is open to students and staff of institutions in Programme Countries, and mobility is arranged between a sending and a receiving institution that hold an inter-institutional agreement. Students take part of their studies in another country at no additional cost of tuition, registration or examination, and the time spent abroad plus the courses completed must be recognised by the home institution.
eligibility: Enrolled student or employed staff member at a participating higher education institution
Sending and receiving institutions must hold an inter-institutional Erasmus+ agreement
Mobility must be within the Erasmus+ Programme Countries or an eligible Partner Country
The home institution must recognise the study period and the courses completed abroad
coverage: Study abroad without additional costs of tuition, registration or examination
Scholarship covering costs of living abroad (amount set nationally, not published on the pages read)
Support for work placements in companies abroad and academic staff mobility
New option of graduate mobility for practical training or work placement
required_documents: Application to the sending institution's Erasmus+ office
Learning Agreement / Transcript of Records agreed with the sending and receiving institutions
Proof of enrolment or employment at the sending institution
Grant agreement signed with the sending institution or National Agency
requirements: Applications are made through the sending university, not directly to the National Agency
The Learning Agreement must be completed for the period before mobility starts
The home institution must accept the period abroad and credit the courses completed
application_method: Application through the sending higher education institution's international/Erasmus+ office
Selection and grant award by the sending institution or, in some cases, the National Agency
records.selection_notes: Not published on the official pages read: Erasmus+ selection is run at institutional level, so criteria and weighting vary by university. The official page confirms only that mobility must be agreed between the institutions and recognised by the home institution.
records.program_type: EU-funded academic mobility programme
records.best_fit: Students and staff at a Polish higher education institution with an Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreement who want a study, placement or staff mobility period abroad.
benefits: No additional tuition, registration or examination costs at the receiving institution
Scholarship covering living costs abroad
Academic staff mobility
Work placements in companies abroad
Graduate mobility for practical training or work placement
records.notes: This row is a programme-level umbrella, not a single call. The stored study.gov.pl page still describes the 2014-2020 funding period and points to http://www.erasmusplus.org.pl/in-poland/, which now returns HTTP 404; the live national agency site is https://erasmusplus.org.pl/. The Polish National Agency is the Foundation for the Development of the Education System (FRSE), not NAWA.
records.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. Its higher education strand is mainly a student exchange programme that also covers placements in companies abroad and academic staff mobility. Students can spend part of their studies in another country without additional tuition, registration or examination costs and receive a scholarship covering living costs, with the period and courses recognised by their home institution. In Poland the programme is implemented by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System, appointed as the Polish National Agency.

official_details.application_cycle: Continuous programme; calls announced annually by the Polish National Agency (Foundation for the Development of the Education System) and by each participating university for each academic year
official_details.deadline_central_display: No central deadline published; Erasmus+ deadlines are set per call and per institution
official_details.deadline_note: Neither the official study.gov.pl Erasmus+ page nor the Polish National Agency site read publishes a single application deadline or any cycle dates. deadline_precision is 'varies' and deadline_date is null rather than guessed.
official_details.status_note: The programme is continuously operating with annual institutional calls; no central open/closed state is published.

official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Official: 'Erasmus+ Higher Education allows students to undertake a part of their studies in another country without additional costs of tuition, registration or examination.'
official_details.funding_label: Study abroad with no additional tuition, registration or examination costs, plus a scholarship covering costs of living abroad. The official pages read publish no monthly or per-travel amounts, and travel support is not quantified, so this is not claimed as a full-funding award.
benefits: Study abroad without additional tuition, registration or examination costs
Scholarship covering the costs of living abroad
Academic staff mobility
Work placements in companies abroad
Graduate mobility for practical training or work placement
Recognition of the period abroad and of courses completed by the home institution
eligibility: Enrolled student or employed staff member at a participating institution
Inter-institutional Erasmus+ agreement between sending and receiving institutions
Mobility within Programme Countries or an eligible Partner Country
Recognition of the study period by the home institution

official_details.international_eligibility: Open to students and staff of institutions in Programme Countries, with mobility possible to eligible Partner Countries throughout the world.

official_details.application_route: Sending institution's Erasmus+/international office, with the Foundation for the Development of the Education System as Polish National Agency

Home institution must recognise the period and credit the courses completed
documents: Application to the sending institution's Erasmus+ office
Learning Agreement / Transcript of Records
Proof of enrolment or employment
Signed grant agreement

selection_criteria: Institutional eligibility under the inter-institutional agreement
Academic nomination by the sending institution
Recognition commitment by the home institution

official_details.description: The EU Erasmus+ programme, whose higher education strand funds study periods, placements and staff mobility. Students study abroad without additional tuition, registration or examination costs and receive a scholarship for living costs, with recognition by the home institution. In Poland it is implemented by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System.
official_details.program_type: EU-funded academic mobility programme
official_details.coverage: No additional tuition, registration or examination costs at the receiving institution, plus a scholarship covering living costs abroad; amounts are not published on the official pages read.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your university has an Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreement with a specific receiving institution and in your field - this, not your nationality, is the gate
Go to your sending institution's Erasmus+ office, not to the National Agency, to apply
Agree and sign the Learning Agreement before the mobility begins
Check that your home institution will credit the courses and the period abroad
Ask your Erasmus+ office for the current monthly rates and travel support, which the national pages do not publish
Time your application to your university's internal call, not to a national deadline
common_rejection_risks: No inter-institutional agreement with the chosen host, or the agreement does not cover your field
Applying directly to the National Agency instead of through the sending university
Missing the university's internal selection or nomination round
Leaving the Learning Agreement unsigned before departure
Host outside Programme/Partner Country eligibility
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition, registration or examination fees the receiving institution charges outside the agreed waiver
Living costs above the scholarship rate set for your nationality and destination group
Travel and insurance costs above whatever travel support your institution's call provides
Costs outside the agreed mobility period
document_audit: Learning Agreement signed by the applicant, sending and receiving institutions
Transcript of Records or learning outcomes agreed for the period abroad
Proof of enrolment or employment
Signed grant or scholarship agreement with the sending institution
Bank details for payment, in the format the sending institution requires

records.description: The Fulbright Program is a merit-based US government grant programme for international educational exchange, founded by Senator J. William Fulbright in 1946 and operating in over 155 countries. In Poland, where it has run since 1959, it is administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission with financial contributions from both governments and supports studies, research and instruction for American and Polish students, scholars, teachers and institutions. Award categories, benefits and deadlines are set separately by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission and by the US Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs.

records.degree_levels: Varies by network (undergraduate, master's or doctoral level, following the sending institution's programme)

The grant is paid by the host country and its amount varies, so no single figure can be quoted for the whole programme.
records.description: CEEPUS is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe, organised as a transnational university network of subject-specific networks, each containing at least three higher education institutions from at least two different CEEPUS contractual countries. Exchanges last 3 to 10 months. Within a network, incoming students are exempted from paying tuition fees and receive a comprehensive grant from the host country sized according to local living costs. Eligibility requires CEEPUS-country nationality and participation through a member institution.

records.name: SAF Merit Scholarship
records.description: The SAF Merit Scholarship is a top-tier military scholarship offered by MINDEF/SAF to Singapore citizens and permanent residents intending to take up citizenship. It pays full tuition fees and other approved academic charges, a monthly salary for the duration of studies, maintenance and other allowances, return airfare and a one-time sponsorship for summer exchange programmes, and can sponsor up to six years of studies inclusive of a Master's degree. Recipients must qualify for and excel in Officer Cadet School and serve a six-year bond in MINDEF/SAF after graduation.

Open to both genders.

Applicants may apply before beginning their degree or as mid-term applicants up to the penultimate year, and must be Singapore Citizens who demonstrate strong leadership qualities and potential with good academic and non-academic records. It was set up in 1991 by the Tanjong Pagar Citizens' Consultative Committee with public funding to commemorate Lee Kuan Yew's contributions to Singapore. Recipients receive full tuition fee coverage and an annual allowance of S$50,000 for up to two years of Master's study or up to five years of PhD study, may study at local or overseas universities with no restriction on course of study, and carry no bond.

records.description: The MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term) sponsors Singaporean school leavers through a full-time undergraduate degree so that they can enter the Education Service as teachers. Applicants may be offered either an Education Merit Scholarship or Teaching Scholarship administered by the Public Service Commission, or a Teaching Award administered by MOE, and are considered for the full range. records.description: SgIS is described by MOE as the only multi-industry scholarship in partnership with the Singapore Government, offering Singapore Citizens scholarships at different stages of university education, locally and overseas. Organisations across various industries sponsor scholars, who are groomed through the SgIS Scholars' Development and Engagement Programme and take at least one internship with their sponsoring organisation. The award covers full tuition fees and approved academic charges plus an allowance for living expenses, hostel and overseas exchange, against a bond of four years for most autonomous universities or three years for SIT and LAS.

records.name: A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF)
records.description: The A*STAR International Fellowship funds up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral research training through a Research track at overseas universities or laboratories and an Innovation track at deep-tech startups. A*STAR publishes a monthly allowance of $5,000 for Singapore Citizens alongside an overseas living allowance, a CPF-inclusive sustenance allowance, annual return airfare, personal insurance and settling-in, computer and conference allowances. Holders must return to Singapore and contribute to A*STAR's research institutes or relevant organisations for 3 years after the training.

records.eligibility_summary: Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents who completed a PhD within the last 4 years and hold no existing bond to any institution. Research track applicants need excellent publication records and a postdoctoral position at, or application to, a top overseas university or laboratory; Innovation track applicants must show aptitude and aspiration for innovation and entrepreneurship roles. Non-Singaporeans may apply only if they obtain Singapore citizenship before the fellowship starts.

A*STAR publishes a monthly allowance of $5,000 for Singapore Citizens alongside an overseas living allowance, a CPF-inclusive sustenance allowance, annual return airfare, personal insurance and settling-in, computer and conference allowances. records.name: National Science Scholarship (PhD)
records.description: The National Science Scholarship (PhD) funds up to 5 years of PhD study at a top overseas institution for Singapore citizens and prospective citizens. It covers full tuition fees plus a monthly allowance of $4,500 for Singapore Citizens and $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents, together with living, airfare, conference, thesis, computer and settling-in allowances. Awardees must first complete a compulsory 1-year research attachment at an A*STAR research institute, then serve 4 years at an A*STAR research institute or relevant organisation, or 3 years if the PhD was completed in a non-anglophone country.
records.official_source: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), A*STAR Graduate Academy
records.program_type: PhD Scholarship
records.duration: Up to 5 years of PhD funding
records.deadline: First application cycle opens on 1 January and closes on 1 April; second application cycle opens on 14 July and closes on 1 October.
records.application_period: Two application cycles a year. The Scholarship Facts box states "Application period: 1 January to 1 April & 1 July to 1 October", while the Application Timeline table states the second cycle opens on 14 July and closes on 1 October. A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis.
records.eligibility_summary: Singaporeans, or other nationals intending to take up Singapore citizenship, who hold a good class of Honours degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline, are in the last semester of their final undergraduate year, and have applied or are applying to a PhD programme at a top overseas institution. Non-Singaporeans must hold at least Singapore Permanent Resident status before the studies start and convert to Singapore citizenship during the PhD. Full-term candidates must complete a compulsory 1-year research attachment at an A*STAR research institute before starting the PhD.

The process typically takes about five months from a complete submission to notification of results, and candidates are advised to submit early. Applicants may also request consideration for the A*STAR Graduate Scholarship in the same application form.

Scholars who complete the PhD in a non-anglophone country serve a 3-year service commitment instead of 4 years. All rates and allowances vary by country and university and are subject to A*STAR adjustment.

records.description: The NUS Undergraduate Scholarship is one of three tiers of NUS Scholarships for Singapore Citizen freshmen, awarded on academic excellence, co-curricular record and leadership potential. For the tier read in full, the benefits are subsidised tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, a guaranteed one-semester exchange placement at an NUS overseas partner university, priority for on-campus accommodation over the first two years and bond-free status. One common online application from 1 February to 19 March 2027 covers the tiers, and the award is tenable for the normal candidature period subject to semesterly renewal on a GPA of at least 3.50.

Transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible, and the tiers exclude Dentistry, Medicine and Music.

records.description: The Nanyang Merit Scholarship is awarded by Nanyang Technological University to outstanding freshmen in full-time undergraduate programmes on the basis of academic achievement, co-curricular record and leadership. It provides full coverage of subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant, a living allowance of S$5,000 per academic year and a one-off $4,000 travel grant, for up to the normal programme duration. The scholarship carries no NTU bond, although Singapore Permanent Residents and international students remain bound by the three-year MOE Tuition Grant Scheme bond.

Write the compulsory Personal Essay of no more than 250 words
Upload a recent passport-size digital photograph
Assemble family identification documents and income documents with the Document Checklist and upload them as a single file
Ask a school teacher who is not a family member or relative to file the online referee's appraisal within 7 days, giving them your NTU application number and date of birth
Keep March to May free for the selection interview and monitor email from mid-May
common_rejection_risks: Missing the admission closing date that governs the scholarship window
A referee appraisal submitted after the 7-day window, or a second appraisal
Uploading the family ID and income documents as separate files instead of one file with the Document Checklist
A CGPA below 3.5 at a semesterly review
Holding a concurrent award not approved by NTU
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, which are not listed among the standard benefits and are only covered via bursaries for applicants who demonstrate further financial need and meet extra conditions
Living costs beyond the subsidised hostel place
Living costs beyond Year 4 if the degree runs longer than the four-year hostel guarantee
document_audit: NTU admission application submitted and application number issued
Scholarship application form completed with the compulsory 250-word essay
Passport-size photo uploaded
Family identification and income documents uploaded as one file with the Document Checklist

alerts.trigger: Tuition is not a standard benefit
alerts.message: Do not assume this award pays tuition. Tuition coverage via bursaries is conditional additional support for applicants who require further financial aid.
The $10,000 overseas travel allowance and $10,000 annual study allowance are only granted if you require further financial aid and satisfy further terms and conditions.
Terminating the award early triggers repayment, and NTU may withdraw it if progress or behaviour is unsatisfactory.
There is no NTU bond, but the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme bond applies to holders who are not Singapore Citizens.

records.name: SMU Global Impact Scholarship Award
records.description: The SMU Global Impact Scholarship Award is Singapore Management University's premier flagship undergraduate scholarship, open to Singapore Citizens entering a full-time degree programme and awarded on academic excellence, leadership and co-curricular or community record. The published benefits, applying from Academic Year 2028-29, are a waiver of subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to 4 years, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$14,000 GLOW grant for overseas exposure and community service, a S$1,800 computer allowance, a S$9,000 Enhanced Flexibility Grant and up to S$40,000 for an optional concurrent or sequential SMU Master's programme. The scholarship is bond-free and is applied for through the Scholarship section of the SMU admission application.

records.name: Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship
records.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who show academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement and a strong passion for STEM, to study a STEM undergraduate degree at an overseas university, with Medicine and Dentistry excluded. Temasek lists tuition and other compulsory fees for the whole course, a monthly living allowance, one-time relocation and pre-studies allowances, reimbursed application fees for up to five universities and visa fees, plus exchange programmes, internships and mentoring. Eligibility is capped by a Gross Monthly Household Income of S$15,000 or less at the point of admission, and graduates must serve a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company.

official_details.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who show academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement and a strong passion for STEM, to study a STEM undergraduate degree at a top overseas university, with Medicine and Dentistry excluded. Temasek lists tuition and other compulsory fees for the whole course, a monthly living allowance, one-time relocation and pre-studies allowances, reimbursed application fees for up to five universities and visa fees, plus exchange programmes, internships and mentoring. Eligibility is capped by a Gross Monthly Household Income of S$15,000 or less at the point of admission, and graduates must serve a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company.

records.name: Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship
records.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship is a merit-based award for talented students pursuing a full-time STEM undergraduate degree programme at the Singapore Institute of Technology, offered to polytechnic graduates. Each scholarship is valued at up to S$18,030 per annum, including an annual stipend of S$7,200, with a one-time S$2,000 laptop allowance in the first year of study and a possible one-time S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant for an eligible global exposure programme. It forms part of Temasek's S$150 million T-Spring community gift, made to mark the company's 50th anniversary in 2024, and is administered by Singapore Institute of Technology under its published Terms and Conditions.

records.official_source: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
records.duration: Up to four years (the normal duration of the relevant SUTD bachelor degree programme)
records.deadline: There is no separate scholarship deadline. SUTD states 'Application for the scholarships is made at the same time as application for admission to SUTD', and the published 2026 admissions application window ran 2 January to 2 March 2026 for most qualifications, and from the release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026 for Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level qualification.

records.eligibility_summary: Open to Singapore Citizens applying for admission to an SUTD undergraduate degree programme with outstanding GCE A-Level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications and a passion for technology and design. As a special concession it may also be awarded to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students with exceptional achievements.
eligibility: Singapore Citizen applying for admission to an SUTD undergraduate degree programme
Outstanding Singapore-Cambridge GCE A Level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications
Have a passion for technology and design
As a special concession, may be awarded to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students who have demonstrated exceptional and outstanding achievements
coverage: Subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant, for up to four years
benefits: Subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant) for the normal duration, up to four years, of the relevant bachelor degree programme
application_method: Apply for admission to SUTD and indicate interest in applying for the SUTD scholarships in the admission application
records.selection_notes: Scholarships are awarded on the basis of competition among eligible applicants. SUTD reserves the right not to award the scholarship if there are no candidates of sufficient merit, and the decision of the selection committee is final.
records.program_type: Merit-based tuition scholarship for new undergraduate admission applicants
records.description: The SUTD Undergraduate Merit Scholarship is an academic merit award for applicants to SUTD bachelor's degree programmes. It pays the subsidised tuition fees, after the Tuition Grant, for the normal duration of the programme, up to four years. It carries no bond, but the recipient must take up the Singapore Government's Tuition Grant Scheme to enjoy subsidised fees. Recipients must maintain good academic standing, reviewed every term, and complete at least 20 hours of service to the University. Applications are made as part of the SUTD admission application.
records.best_fit: Singapore Citizen high school leavers with top A-Level, Polytechnic Diploma or IB results seeking a design-and-technology undergraduate degree at SUTD.
records.notes: For awards made to Singapore Permanent Residents or International Students, tuition fees coverage is capped at the fees payable by a Singapore Citizen.

Applicants must possess at least one academic degree (earned in the U.S. or abroad) that is equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree.
Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned.
Applicants may apply for only one degree type and in a single specific field.
Applicants must pursue their study in the U.S. on a full-time basis at an institution accredited by the U.S. Department of Education.
Applicants must reside in the U.S. or country of their study for the duration of the fellowship period.

records.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program funds citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience to pursue a master's degree in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, it offers scholarships for 44 participating master's programs in 24 universities across the United States, Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan, in areas including economic policy management, tax policy and infrastructure management. Applicants must already be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to one of those participating programs. Awards cover tuition, basic medical insurance, a monthly subsistence allowance, two-way economy class air travel and a US $600 travel allowance per trip, for the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.

official_details.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program is open to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts who are applying to a master's degree program in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, JJ/WBGSP offers scholarships for 44 Participating Master's Programs in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan in key areas of development, including economic policy management, tax policy, and infrastructure management. Applicants who are not admitted to one of these 44 programmes are not eligible to apply in 2027. The application process is organized in two rounds: Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027 and Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The scholarship provides tuition, a monthly living stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance and a travel allowance.
official_details.program_type: Master's scholarship
official_details.coverage: Tuition, basic medical insurance through the university, a monthly subsistence allowance for living expenses, two-way economy class air travel and a US $600 travel allowance per trip. Not covered: visa costs, family expenses, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, expenses related to research, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee.

Time your submission for at least a week before the deadline, as the Secretariat recommends, because the process is lengthy.

Holding dual citizenship of a developed country.

Having previously declined a JJ/WBGSP scholarship or received one without graduating.
Submitting an incomplete application; the scholarship must also not duplicate other funding.

Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. official_details.description: The U.S. Department of State's Benjamin A. records.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
records.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, fully integrated master's programmes designed and delivered jointly by at least three higher education institutions in at least three different countries, and they award either a joint degree or multiple degrees. The European Commission funds both the programmes and competitive scholarships for the best students worldwide. Applicants apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, and each master's own website sets its own entry requirements and deadlines. Individual scholarships are worth EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months.

Applicants who demonstrate a bachelor's-equivalent level of learning may also apply, provided this is officially recognised in the degree-awarding country.

records.name: Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme (ICCR)
records.official_source: Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Government of India
records.description: The Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme is scheme code A1218 in ICCR's scholarship schemes list. ICCR states that the scholarship to Bangladesh nationals is offered under this single scheme, which subsumes the schemes previously used for that purpose. The Government of India, through ICCR, funds undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study at Indian universities for nationals of Bangladesh. Applications are made through ICCR's A2A scholarship portal, and registration for the academic year 2026-27 is now closed, with the next cycle to be announced by ICCR.

records.name: DAAD Scholarships (Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst Scholarship Database)
records.description: DAAD administers a family of scholarship programmes for international students and researchers funded largely by the German Federal Foreign Office, listed in its official Scholarship Database at www2.daad.de. The flagship Study Scholarship for postgraduate study states scholarship payments of 992 euros a month, payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance, and an annual study allowance of EUR 460. Funding is awarded for the standard period of study of the chosen programme, up to a maximum of 24 months, and must begin in 2027. Each individual programme in the database sets its own eligibility, deadline and award value, and application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter.

official_details.description: DAAD's Scholarship Database lists the German Academic Exchange Service's scholarship programmes for international students and researchers, funded largely by the German Federal Foreign Office. The flagship Study Scholarship for postgraduate study funds a whole Master's programme at a state or state-recognised German university, or one study year in Germany as part of a second or Master's degree completed at the home university. It pays 992 euros a month, contributes to health, accident and personal liability insurance, provides a travel allowance on application and an annual study allowance of EUR 460, and can support rent, accompanying family members, disability-related costs and climate-friendly travel. Funding is awarded for the standard period of study up to 24 months and must begin in 2027. Applications are made through the DAAD portal, which is only accessible during each programme's application period.

records.description: The Global Korea Scholarship is South Korea's representative government scholarship programme, designed to attract talented international students by supporting them in pursuing degrees and broader study in Korea. NIIED publishes a selection quota of approximately 280 undergraduate students including associate degree students, plus 1,600 graduate students. Awarded scholarship comprises one year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years), a bachelor's degree (4-6 years), a master's degree (2 years) or a doctoral degree (3 years). Benefits include airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition fees and a monthly stipend. Applications are made either through a Korean embassy or consulate (Embassy Track) or directly to a designated university (University Track).

records.name: Japanese Government (MEXT / Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
records.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
records.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship is offered in seven types: Research students, Teacher training students, Undergraduate students, Japanese studies students, College of technology students, Specialized training college students, and the Young Leaders Program. Applicants apply either through embassy recommendation or, for most types, university recommendation. The published benefits are a monthly scholarship, tuition exemption, and round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Each type has its own age limit, academic qualification, field of study and duration, and MEXT directs applicants to the latest edition of the application guidelines because detailed requirements are established separately.
records.duration: Varies by type: research students up to 2 years for the irregular course or the standard school year for the regular course; teacher training within 1 year and 6 months including Japanese language education; undergraduate students 5 years including Japanese language training (7 years for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary science); Japanese studies students 4 years including Japanese language training (4 years and 6 months for merchant marine studies); college of technology students 3 years including Japanese language training; specialized training college students 1 year. Under university recommendation the duration depends on each school's quota, up to a standard school year
records.deadline: With regard to application qualifications and procedures, in addition to the actual contents, there are also cases when detailed requirements are established. Because of this, be sure to confirm the latest edition of the application guidelines. If the application qualifications differ from the application guidelines, the contents of the guidelines should be followed.
records.application_period: Embassy recommendation and university recommendation cycles are set per scholarship type and published in the MEXT application guidelines; the official page publishes no single central date
records.eligibility_summary: Each type has its own eligibility. Research students must be under 35 and eligible for admission to a master's or doctoral programme at a Japanese graduate school. Teacher training students must be under 35, be graduates of a college or teacher training college, and have at least five years of active teaching experience in a primary, secondary or teacher training college in their home country. Undergraduate students must be under 25 and have completed 12 years of schooling or comparable study. Japanese studies students must be between 18 and 29 and be enrolled in a Japanese-language or Japanese-culture faculty at a university outside Japan. College of technology students must be under 25 with 11 or more years of education. Specialized training college students must be under 25 with 12 years of schooling.

records.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
records.official_source: Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS / ESKAS), State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SBFI), Swiss Confederation
records.description: Each year the Swiss Confederation awards Government Excellence Scholarships to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and over 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students, also known as ESKAS. The scholarships are mainly intended for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and the programme is currently open to applicants from 183 countries. Funding is CHF 2450 per month for a maximum period of 12 or 36 months for research scholarships and 21 months for art scholarships, with a maximum age of 35. Applications are open from 20 August 2026 and must be prepared in the GO ESKAS application platform using a Switch edu-ID.
records.duration: Research PhD scholarship: 12 months or 36 months. Art scholarship: 21 months.
records.deadline: Applications are open starting August 20, 2026. Information on application deadlines and scholarship availability by country of origin will be published in August 2026.
records.application_period: Applications open from 20 August 2026 for the 2027-2028 academic year; deadlines and availability differ by country of origin and are published by country. Awards are announced by the end of May at the latest, and scholarships for the 2028-2029 academic year will be advertised online from August 2027.
records.eligibility_summary: The scholarships are mainly intended for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree. Research scholarship applicants must have a Master's degree and be backed by an academic supervisor in Switzerland willing to direct and guide the proposed research. Art scholarship applicants must hold a Bachelor's degree and hold an admission or proof of application, and are eligible from a limited number of countries only. The maximum age is 35.

records.name: France Excellence Charpak Scholarship Program
records.official_source: Campus France India / Embassy of France in India (Government of France)
records.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India, divided into four sub-programmes that allow Indian students to study at undergraduate or postgraduate level in public and private institutions in France. The Master track is designed for one to two years of study at Master's level across all streams and fields, and awardees receive the status of Boursier du Government Français. The Master track pays a monthly living allowance of EUR 860 and covers visa and Campus France procedure fee exemption, student social security and complementary health insurance, accommodation assistance through Campus France in France, and reduced university restaurant meals at EUR 1. The scholarship does not cover travel expenses from India to France or within France, or any other expenses related to the awardee's stay.
records.duration: Master track: designed for one to two years of study in France at Master's level. The Master scholarship is renewable once, upon request and based on the results obtained in the first year.
records.deadline: Applications are submitted on the online scholarship portal for the French Institute in India; Campus France India directs applicants to their nearest Campus France office in India or the institution's website for admission procedure information
records.application_period: Four separate sub-programmes with different cycles: the Summer Training track runs during the academic break in May-July, and the Exchange track runs twice a year with an autumn session in September-December and a spring session in January-May/June
records.eligibility_summary: For the Master track, applicants must be an Indian citizen or hold an OCI card, be 30 years old or younger at the time of application, be currently enrolled in or have completed studies at an Indian institution of higher education, and ensure the course takes place in France. Knowledge of French is an asset but not mandatory, the scholarship is for full-time master's degree programmes only, and the applicant must already have applied for admission to a French institution.

official_details.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India. It is divided into four sub-programmes allowing Indian students to study at undergraduate or postgraduate level in public and private institutions in France: the Bachelor track, the Master track, a Summer Training track for internships or research projects in May-July, and an Exchange track offered twice a year for a semester in France. The Master track is designed for one to two years of study across all streams and fields, and awardees receive the status of Boursier du Government Français, entitling them to a monthly living allowance of EUR 860, visa exemption when applying from India, exemption of Campus France procedure fees, student social security and additional health insurance, assistance finding student accommodation through Campus France in France with priority access to CROUS residencies subject to availability, and meals at EUR 1 in university restaurants. The scholarship does not cover travel expenses from India to France or within France, or any other expenses related to the awardee's stay in France. Applicants must be Indian citizens or OCI card holders aged 30 or under, already enrolled at or graduated from an Indian institution, and must have applied for admission to a French institution before applying for the scholarship.

records.official_source: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE), France, implemented by Campus France in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space (MESRE)
records.description: Since 2018 the Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) initiative has been a flagship programme for postdoctoral mobility in France and one of the leading fellowship programmes of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The 2027 call is the tenth edition, funded by MEAE in partnership with MESRE and implemented by Campus France, and enables young international researchers to carry out a research project in France. Each fellowship runs for 12 months and provides a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health coverage including health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance. Successful applicants receive the status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF) and the fellowship is paid directly by Campus France.

records.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is Germany's public-private scholarship programme, supporting talented and committed students at public and state-recognised universities in Germany. First- and higher-semester students of all nationalities can apply directly to their university. Private donors, which may be businesses, foundations or private individuals, pledge EUR 150 per month and the Federal Government matches that with another EUR 150, giving EUR 300 per month. Many universities and private sponsors add non-financial support such as mentoring, networking events and internships. The scholarship is awarded without consideration of personal or parent income, nationality is not material to the award, the funds do not count towards grants under the Federal Training Assistance Act, and there are no social insurance contributions payable.
records.duration: Funding is normally granted for at least two semesters but may be provided for a maximum time covering the standard period of study. The university reviews at intervals of two semesters whether the scholarship holder still meets the award criteria and whether private funding will continue to be available.
records.deadline: The Deutschlandstipendium is awarded by the universities and applicants must meet the requirements of the individual institutions; for the procedure and deadlines you should enquire directly at your university.

official_details.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is Germany's public-private scholarship programme, supporting talented, high-achieving and committed students at public and state-recognised universities in Germany. First- and higher-semester students of all nationalities can apply directly to their university. Private sponsors, which may be businesses, foundations or private individuals, pledge EUR 150 per month, and the Federal Government matches this with another EUR 150, giving EUR 300 per month. Many universities and private sponsors also provide non-financial support such as mentoring programmes, networking events and internships. The scholarship is awarded without consideration of personal or parent income, nationality is not material to the award, the funds do not count towards grants under the Federal Training Assistance Act, and there are no social insurance contributions payable. The universities award the scholarship, select the holders and pay the funds; in addition to academic achievement, the selection criteria include social commitment and personal achievements such as overcoming challenges in a social or family background. Funding is normally granted for at least two semesters, up to a maximum covering the standard period of study, with a review every two semesters.

official_details.coverage: EUR 300 per month stipend plus optional non-financial support; no tuition or travel coverage statement published

official_details.description: The Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship is offered by the University of Melbourne to international students enrolling in a bachelor's degree who are citizens of countries where international educational opportunities are limited by financial disadvantage, defined on the official page as countries with a GDP per capita of US$10,000 or less. official_details.description: The Global Excellence Scholarship is an annual tuition fee discount awarded automatically by the University of Western Australia to high-achieving international students from any country who take an eligible 2027 undergraduate or postgraduate course. The discount is 10 or 20 per cent of tuition fees for the normal full-time duration of the course, and its value is set by the applicant's equivalent ATAR for undergraduate study or UWA weighted average mark for postgraduate study. records.description: The McCall MacBain Scholarships at McGill University is a full graduate scholarship for candidates entering a full-time master's or second-entry professional undergraduate program at McGill. For the 2027 cohort the programme awards up to 30 full scholarships and up to 100 finalist and regional awards. The scholarship covers tuition and fees for the full normal duration of the programme, a living stipend of $2,300 per month during academic terms, and a one-time relocation grant, with up to $5,000 available for summer initiatives. Applications for Summer/Fall 2027 closed on August 19 or September 23, 2026 depending on applicant group, and the programme runs annually.

records.description: The Invest Your Talent in Italy programme, run by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation together with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia, awards scholarships to international students from 23 listed countries to attend a Master's degree or postgraduate programme at an Italian university participating in the programme. The scholarship is worth EUR 10,800 for nine months starting 1 October 2026 and includes exemption from tuition fees. Recipients must complete a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association consistent with their field of study. Only courses in Engineering and Advanced Technologies, Management and Economics, and Design and Architecture listed in the programme catalogue are eligible, and candidates must first obtain pre-admission from the university.

records.name: International Talents @unibo — Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in Second Cycle Degree Programmes
records.official_source: Alma Mater Studiorum – Università di Bologna
records.program_type: University merit and needs-based study grant for international students matriculating in a Second Cycle (Master's) degree programme
records.description: The University of Bologna awards 30 International Talents @unibo study grants each year to international students who matriculate for the first time in the first year of a Second Cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree programme. Each grant is worth EUR 6,500 gross per academic year and is awarded for two academic years, and successful applicants also receive a full tuition fee waiver, paying only EUR 157.04 in regional taxes, stamp duty and insurance premium. Selection is based on GRE General Test scores, with minimum scores of 290 in the combined Verbal and Quantitative Reasoning sections and 3.0 in Analytical Writing, together with a family economic situation within an ISEE band of EUR 16,000 to EUR 35,000. Applicants must be under 30 years old at the deadline and must not already be a student of the University of Bologna.
records.duration: Two academic years (a standard Second Cycle degree programme)
records.deadline: Applications for the 2025/26 edition closed at 12:00 CEST on 30 May 2025 ("scadenza: 30 maggio 2025, 12:00"); the call is published annually and no open window was visible on bandi.unibo.it on 4 October 2026.
records.application_period: Annual call, opening in mid-January and closing at 12:00 CEST in late May (17 January 2025 12:00 CET to 30 May 2025 12:00 CEST for the 2025/26 edition); results published in July
records.eligibility_summary: Holds a qualification obtained outside the Italian education system that gives access to a Second Cycle degree programme at the University of Bologna; is not a current or former student of a Bologna degree programme; has an ISEE between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000 or equivalent economic documentation; has not held an Unibo Action 2 grant; and is under 30 years old at the deadline.

Is less than 30 years old at the application deadline
Matriculates for the first time in the first year of the degree programme; later enrolments, course changes and transfers do not count
Is not enrolling in a multiple or joint degree programme where fees are paid to a partner university other than Bologna
coverage: Study grant of EUR 6,500 gross per academic year, paid over two academic years
Full exemption from university tuition fees
Only EUR 157.04 payable by the holder, covering regional tax, stamp duty and insurance premium

requirements: Applications are submitted exclusively through Studenti Online (studenti.unibo.it); paper, fax and email applications are not accepted

Submit the ISEE or equivalent economic situation documentation
records.selection_notes: Grants are ranked on the summed GRE General Test score, with equal weight to each section; applicants below the minimum scores are excluded. Ties are resolved in favour of the younger candidate. Results are published by a managerial decree on studenti.unibo.it. Winners must send an unconditional acceptance declaration to internationaldesk@unibo.it within 10 days of the award notification.

records.name: Merit-Based International Scholarships — Politecnico di Milano (Academic Year 2027/2028)

politecnico di milano — merit based international scholarships
records.program_type: University merit-based scholarship scheme for international Master of Science applicants, with Platinum, Gold, Bronze and Silver tiers plus partner-funded awards
records.description: Politecnico di Milano runs an annual merit-based scholarship scheme for international candidates applying to the first year of an English-taught Master of Science programme. The 2027/2028 call offers 64 awards: 10 Platinum (Milan), 18 Gold (Milan), 16 Gold Piacenza Campus, 10 Bronze Piacenza Campus and 10 Silver scholarships for the Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza campuses. Every award includes a full tuition-fee waiver for the academic year, and the cash tiers add a gross allowance of EUR 10,000 (Platinum), EUR 8,000 (Gold), EUR 5,000 (Gold Piacenza) or EUR 2,500 (Bronze); the Silver tier is a waiver only. Recipients must pay a non-refundable administrative fee of about EUR 170 on acceptance, and the awards can be renewed for a second year on academic points.
records.duration: One academic year, renewable for a second year on academic points
records.deadline: The application form must be submitted from 1 October 2026 until 12:00 noon (Italian time) on 15 December 2026 through Politecnico di Milano Online Services; a valid English language proficiency certificate must be submitted by 4 March 2027 to remain eligible for the scholarship.
records.application_period: Applications open 1 October 2026 and close at 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026, for admission application and scholarship for academic year 2027/2028. Eligibility is restricted to candidates who paid the admission application fee during the Early Bird period from 1 October to 1 December 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: International students who have already submitted an admission application to the first year of an English-taught Master of Science programme at Politecnico di Milano and paid the application fee between 1 October and 1 December 2026. Applicants must be admitted to the programme and accept the positive admission outcome, and must provide a valid English language certificate by 4 March 2027.

Silver tier: tuition-fee exemption only, excluding the administrative fee and insurance

records.selection_notes: Scholarships are assigned by a Commission nominated through an Executive Decree of the Head of the Campus Life Area, including the Vice Rector for International Relations and the Heads of Schools or their delegates. To be considered, students must be admitted to the programme and accept the outcome. The Commission takes into account gender equality, country of origin and age, prioritising the youngest candidates where requirements are equivalent. The published assignment criteria on the scholarships page state that selection is based on the evaluation of previous education and its match with the programme requirements, the documents provided at application and the scholarship form, with GPA and academic achievements (including the portfolio where requested) of utmost importance.

records.name: Padua International Excellence Scholarship — Università degli Studi di Padova
legacy_titles: University of Padua — Padua International Excellence Scholarship
university of padua — padua international excellence scholarship
records.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in a completely English-taught degree programme: 2 years for master's degree programmes, 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes
records.description: The University of Padua awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships each year to the most deserving international candidate on each degree programme delivered entirely in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional right-to-education tax and the revenue stamp payable. There is no separate scholarship application: applying to an eligible English-taught degree programme by its admission deadline makes the candidate eligible automatically. Selection is made by the Teaching Committee of each degree programme on academic excellence and the quality of the candidate's prior academic record, with the youngest candidate preferred in a tie.
records.duration: 2 years for master's degree programmes; 3 years for bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes
records.deadline: There is no separate scholarship deadline: the application for the degree programme automatically makes the candidate eligible, so the deadline is the admission deadline of the chosen degree programme, published in its Admission Notice. The call for the 2027/2028 edition had not yet been published on the verification date and the University states it will appear in November 2026.
records.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission call. For the 2026/2027 cycle the official call set first application periods of 2 November 2025 to 2 February 2026 for unlimited-access programmes and 7 January to 7 March 2026 for limited-access programmes, with scholarship results published from 11 March 2026 and 10 April 2026 respectively. The 2027/2028 call is due in November 2026.
records.eligibility_summary: Candidates must not hold Italian citizenship (dual citizenship is allowed), must hold a non-Italian secondary school diploma for bachelor's and single-cycle programmes or a foreign degree for master's programmes, must not be resident in Italy at the time of application, and must apply to an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua within that programme's deadline.

Is not resident in Italy at the time of application
Applies for admission to an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua within the deadline set by that programme
Does not receive other scholarships or grants, which is a condition of receiving and keeping this award
Completes enrolment at the University of Padua
coverage: EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year, paid in two instalments of EUR 4,000.00
Exemption from student fees (contributi studenteschi) for each academic year of the award
required_documents: Only the documents required to apply for the chosen degree programme; no additional documentation is needed for the scholarship
Online bank account or prepaid card with an IBAN at an Italian bank or any other bank in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), of which the student is the holder or joint holder
Signed Declaration of acceptance of the scholarship terms and confirmation of no incompatibility
For non-EU candidates residing abroad, an Italian student visa (D) for enrolment
records.english_requirement: The degree programme must be taught completely in English. No separate English language test score is required by the scholarship itself; admission to the programme governs the language requirement.

application_method: Choose an English-taught degree programme at the University of Padua and apply for admission within its application period
No separate scholarship application is needed; the degree application makes the candidate eligible for the competition
If shortlisted, receive a specific scholarship offer from the Admissions and Welcome Unit of the Global Engagement Office
Accept the admission and scholarship offers and pay the admission fee by the stated deadline
Complete enrolment and open or use an IBAN in an Italian or SEPA bank account
Sign and submit the Declaration of acceptance
records.selection_notes: The Teaching Committee of each degree programme shortlists eligible applicants and awards the scholarship to the most deserving candidates on the basis of academic excellence in their field of study and the quality and results of their prior academic career. In case of equal scores the youngest candidate is given priority. Scholarships are mainly reserved for candidates applying in the first application period and may be awarded to second-period candidates only on an exceptional basis. Results are published on the University website on the dates set out in the Admission Notice.

official_details.application_cycle: Annual call tied to the degree programme admission rounds. The 2026/2027 call is published and closed; the University states that calls for application for the Padua International Excellence Scholarships "will be published in November 2026" for the 2027/2028 edition.
official_details.deadline_central_display: No single central deadline exists. The application for the degree programme automatically makes the candidate eligible, and the scholarship results are published according to the deadlines specified in each programme's Admission Notice. For the 2026/2027 cycle the official call set first application periods of 2 November 2025 to 2 February 2026 (unlimited access) and 7 January to 7 March 2026 (limited access).

official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The official page states the scholarship includes "exemption from student fees for each academic year" and that "Beneficiaries are only required to pay the regional fee and the revenue stamp per academic year".
official_details.funding_label: EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, with only the regional right-to-education tax and revenue stamp payable. Travel, insurance and other expenses are expressly not reimbursed, and the scholarship is revoked with repayment if the credit milestones are missed or the student transfers or withdraws.

official_details.description: The Padua International Excellence Scholarship is a merit award from the University of Padua for international students enrolling in a degree programme taught entirely in English. Up to 76 scholarships are awarded each year, one to the most deserving candidate on each programme, worth EUR 8,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from student fees. Candidates become eligible simply by applying to an eligible English-taught programme within its admission deadline. Awards run for two years on master's programmes and three years on bachelor's and single-cycle programmes, and are paid in two instalments subject to credit milestones.
official_details.program_type: University merit scholarship with fee waiver (international students)
official_details.coverage: EUR 8,000 gross per academic year for up to three years plus exemption from student fees. The recipient still pays the regional right-to-education tax and revenue stamp. Travel, insurance and other expenses are expressly not reimbursed, and accommodation is not included.

alerts.message: There is no scholarship form. The University states that applying to the degree programme "automatically makes you eligible to compete for the award of the scholarship". Missing the programme's admission deadline is the same as missing the scholarship deadline.

The University states calls for application "will be published in November 2026". Start checking the Padua International Excellence Scholarship page and the programme Admission Notices from November 2026.

The scholarship may be revoked if you do not earn at least 20 CFU by 30 November of the following year, or if you transfer or withdraw, and in that event "you will be required to return the installments you may have already received".

Arrive in Padua before the applicable instalment deadline

records.program_type: University merit scholarship awarded through the degree programme admission ranking, with a tuition-fee exemption; renewable on credit milestones
records.description: The University of Trento awards a limited number of merit scholarships to citizens of countries outside the European Union who live outside Italy and enrol in a degree programme, based on their admission score and programme of study. The scholarship is worth EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes, and scholarship holders are also exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on earning at least half of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions. The award lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.
records.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme; up to 3 years for an undergraduate programme
records.deadline: There is no separate scholarship call: scholarships are assigned through each degree programme's admission ranking, so the deadline is that programme's admission application deadline. The University of Trento's 2026/2027 admission calls for non-European candidates closed in March 2026, and the 2027/2028 calls had not been published on 4 October 2026.

For the 2026/2027 cycle published deadlines included 4 March 2026 at 12:00 CET on several English-taught master's programmes and 23 March 2026 on others, each with a EUR 30.00 application fee.

records.selection_notes: The selection is competitive: the University states scholarships are limited in number and based on the admission score obtained, and candidates do not need to apply separately for the scholarship. Ranking lists with admitted candidates and scholarship assignation are published by each degree programme. In September the University checks the credits earned by 10 August and confirms or does not confirm the scholarship for the following academic year; candidates who fall short must return part of the scholarship and pay tuition fees for the following year according to the published credit table.

records.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in English-taught degree programmes, awarded automatically through the admission ranking
records.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is a merit award from the University of Milano-Bicocca for international students who hold a foreign qualification, are not resident in Italy and are admitted to one of the University's English-taught degree programmes. Around 100 scholarships are awarded each year, with five dedicated to each eligible English-taught course, mainly at Master's level. Each scholarship is worth EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees, and is renewable for a maximum of three years on Bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes and two years on Master's degree programmes. No separate application is needed: applying to an eligible programme makes the candidate automatically part of the selection, and applicants are not required to submit any further form.
records.duration: Up to 3 years for Bachelor's and single-cycle degree programmes; up to 2 years for Master's degree programmes
records.deadline: There is no separate scholarship application form: the deadline is the admission deadline of the chosen degree programme. For the 2026/2027 call, candidates on free entrance courses had to be admitted and confirm their admission offer by 15 March 2026, and results were published by mid-April 2026 for free-access programmes and after the admission ranking list for limited-access programmes. The 2026/2027 cycle is complete, with ranking decrees issued on 28 April 2026 and 15 July 2026.
records.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission calls, referred to on the apply.unimib.it website. For 2026/2027 the key milestone was confirmation of admission by 15 March 2026 for free entrance courses, with a second session reflected in a further ranking decree on 15 July 2026.

If a candidate withdraws, the Commission proceeds down the ranking and the next eligible candidate is notified through the Dream Apply messaging section. Priority is given to candidates who applied in the first Call for Admission.

official_details.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is a merit award from the University of Milano-Bicocca for international students resident abroad who hold a foreign qualification and are admitted to an English-taught degree programme. Around 100 awards are made each year, five for each eligible course, each worth EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees, with the administrative fee and regional tax still payable. Applicants submit no separate form; admission to a programme places them automatically in the selection, which follows the programme's admission ranking. Awards are renewable for up to two years on a Master's programme or three years on a Bachelor's or single-cycle programme, subject to published ECTS milestones.
official_details.program_type: University merit scholarship with tuition-fee exemption (international students)
official_details.coverage: EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees. The administrative fee and regional tax are not covered, and accommodation, travel and visa costs are not part of the award. Renewal and instalment payment depend on published ECTS milestones and on arrival in Milan by 31 October.

records.program_type: Need-based Right to University Education scholarship (cash stipend plus services and supplements), administered by the University and funded by the Lombardy Region and the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research
records.description: The ISU Bocconi Scholarship is Bocconi University's implementation of the Italian Right to University Education Scholarship for students entering the first year of a Bachelor of Science, Integrated Master of Arts in Law or Master of Science programme in academic year 2027-2028. It combines a cash stipend with services and supplements, including a free daily meal valued at EUR 829.00 for a.y. 2026-27, access to preferential-rate canteen services and a 200-hour work-study programme. Eligibility depends on three separate tests: enrolment for the absolute first year, an economic test set annually by the Lombardy Region (ISEE/ISEEU Parificato not above EUR 26,887.93 and ISPE/ISPEEU Parificato not above EUR 58,452.06 for a.y. 2026-27), and a merit test verified after the fact through credit thresholds. International candidates apply under this call, while Bocconi and Italian applicants are directed to the separate Bocconi4Access to Education call.
records.duration: One academic year per application; the benefit is not automatic and must be reapplied for each year of enrolment
records.deadline: Applications are only accepted within the published windows and cannot be submitted outside them. For first-year Master of Science international candidates the windows are 28 January to 8 February 2027, 4 to 18 March 2027, 13 to 27 April 2027 and 10 to 18 June 2027.

records.name: Talents 4 UniTo — Two-Year Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in English-Taught Master's Degrees (University of Turin)
records.program_type: University merit scholarship for international students enrolling in the first year of a postgraduate degree (Laurea Magistrale) without restricted access taught in English
records.description: Talents 4 UniTo is the University of Turin's programme of 40 two-year scholarships for talented international students enrolling for the first time in a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places taught in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 20,000 gross in total (EUR 10,000 per academic year) and holders are exempt from university tuition fees, except for the first instalment due for enrolment in each academic year. Candidates are international students who hold a qualification obtained outside the Italian system valid for admission to a postgraduate degree, do not hold Italian citizenship and are not resident in Italy. There is no separate application form: applicants are included automatically if they apply on apply.unito.it for up to two eligible programmes during the published window. Selection is carried out per programme by an Evaluation Teaching Committee on a 50-point scale with a 36-point eligibility threshold, and two scholarships are awarded per programme.
records.duration: 2 years (two academic years), paid in four instalments of EUR 5,000 gross
records.deadline: Applications had to be submitted on apply.unito.it between 25 November 2025 and 29 January 2026 for the a.y. 2026-2027 cycle, and that call is now closed. Rankings were published from 14 May 2026, and ranking scroll was not possible after 30 November 2026. The next edition's window had not been published on 4 October 2026.
records.application_period: Annual call with a fixed window. For a.y. 2026-2027 the Apply@Unito application window opened on 25 November 2025 and closed on 29 January 2026; rankings followed from 14 May 2026. The previous edition funded 38 scholarships, and the 2027-2028 call was not published at the verification date.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants who hold a qualification obtained at an institution outside the Italian education system that is valid for admission to a postgraduate degree, do not hold Italian citizenship, are not resident in Italy, apply to an English-taught postgraduate degree without restricted access at the University of Turin, and demonstrate English proficiency of at least B2 on the CEFR scale.

official_details.description: Talents 4 UniTo is the University of Turin's annual programme of 40 two-year scholarships for international students enrolling for the first time in an English-taught postgraduate degree without restricted access. Each award is EUR 20,000 gross over two years (EUR 10,000 per academic year, paid in four instalments of EUR 5,000) plus exemption from university tuition fees, except the first enrolment instalment. Applicants qualify automatically through the apply.unito.it admission application, with no extra form, and are scored out of 50 points by each programme's Evaluation Teaching Committee with a 36-point eligibility threshold. Two scholarships are awarded per programme, with ties going to the younger candidate, and the award is incompatible with any other scholarship including EDISU.

records.description: UNICORE 8.0 (University Corridors for Refugees) is a project promoted by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees that creates educational corridors from selected countries in Africa and Asia to Italy, in partnership with MAECI, Caritas Italiana, Diaconia Valdese and a group of Italian universities. For the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 academic years the University of Turin awards three two-year cash-and-services scholarships for refugee students to access its open-access, English-taught Master's degree programmes. Each scholarship provides a cash benefit of EUR 7,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from all amounts due for university enrolment, except the first instalment of the student contribution. The award is paid in four instalments by bank transfer to an Italian bank account, with each payment conditional on enrolment and credit milestones.

records.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.

official_details.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program, together with one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan. application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and are not an overseas compatriot student.
Confirm you are not from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau - the programme does not apply to those applicants.
Confirm you have never studied in Taiwan at the level you are applying for.

Decide between a degree place and the one-year pre-degree Mandarin LEP, noting the different stipends (NT$33,000 vs NT$28,000 per month).
Prepare to demonstrate an excellent academic record, good moral character and no criminal record.

Arrange a direct-flight itinerary, since MOFA funds one-way economy-class tickets only.

Applying from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau.
Having previously studied in Taiwan at the same degree or LEP level.
Missing the 1 February to 31 March window - it is the only application period and no extension is published.
Assuming the stipend pays tuition: MOFA explicitly provides no other subsidies and recipients cover all remaining expenses.
Assuming the university must give a tuition reduction - the guidelines only say universities 'may' offer one.
Previously having had a Scholarship revoked.
