records.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.

official_details.application_cycle: Annual cycle with a per-office deadline, which MOE states is 'usually in January or February each year'. records.notes: TIGP is not free tuition. Academia Sinica subsidises the international fee differential for five consecutive years, so students still pay domestic tuition, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter. Budgeted living costs given on the official site are approximately NT$5,000-14,000 per month for accommodation, NT$6,000-10,000 for food and NT$1,000-3,000 for study and personal requirements, so the NT$40,000 stipend is broadly adequate but not surplus. After the stipend period, support depends on the thesis advisor. TIGP also runs a separate Taiwan International Internship Program (TIIP), which is not part of this award.
records.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.

official_details.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program, administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes. Admitted students receive a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year, extended for one further year for good performers, and Academia Sinica subsidises the international tuition surcharge for five consecutive years, after which students still pay domestic tuition of roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 thereafter. Applications are submitted online with no application fee between 1 November and 1 February GMT+8, and results are usually announced in late June or early July for the following fall enrolment.
official_details.program_type: Research-based doctoral scholarship programme administered by a research institute (Academia Sinica) with partner universities
official_details.coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable one further year; full subsidy of the international tuition differential for five consecutive years, leaving the student at the domestic tuition rate; optional separate fellowships and travel grants. Accommodation, food, insurance and tuition itself remain the student's own cost.

application_readiness_checklist: Choose one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes and read that programme's own admissions requirements before applying.
Prepare your application for the 1 November to 1 February GMT+8 window; the site posts a cycle-specific announcement each November.
Submit through the TIGP online application system at https://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php - no application fee is charged.
Have academic records ready for the qualification you declare; add any programme-specific documents.

Budget for domestic-rate tuition: roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter. The international surcharge is subsidised, tuition itself is not.
Plan how you will select a thesis advisor before the end of your first year, because post-stipend support depends on that advisor.
Treat the stipend as a two-year maximum core award (first year, plus one extension for good performance) and build a funding plan for year three.
Check whether you are also eligible for the Presidential, Research Performance or Rising Star Fellowships, or for travel grants.
Contact the programme secretary directly for the tuition figure that applies to your specific programme.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 February GMT+8 deadline - TIGP's window is only three months and there is no stated grace period.
Applying to a programme whose own admission requirements you have not met.
Assuming TIGP pays full tuition: it subsidises the international differential only, and domestic tuition remains payable.
Assuming the stipend lasts the full three years: it is first year plus one extension for good performers, then advisor-dependent.
Not contacting the programme secretary, which is TIGP's stated route for programme-specific tuition costs.
Overlooking academic integrity expectations; TIGP states violations can affect grades, stipend and academic standing.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic-rate tuition: approximately NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder until graduation.
Accommodation: approximately NT$5,000-14,000 per month (on-campus dormitory around NT$5,500; Taipei off-campus single room NT$5,000-14,000).
Food: approximately NT$6,000-10,000 per month.
Books, National Health Insurance, transport and recreation: approximately NT$1,000-3,000 per month.
Airfare to Taiwan, and all costs after the stipend allowance period if the thesis advisor does not provide support.

records.notes: This is a multi-university national programme, so benefits and deadlines are not uniform. Published packages differ by university: one partner advertises full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket, initial administrative expense support and an NT$10,000 monthly industry-sponsored stipend, while another caps tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester for up to two years and lists partner-company stipends between NT$10,000 and NT$15,000 depending on the job and Chinese-proficiency requirement. The scheme carries an employment obligation: the stipend duration matches the work-obligation duration and repayment may be requested if the contract is violated. The stored official_source_url and application_link both point to NTU's Overseas Compatriot and Mainland Chinese Students Advising Division, which does not host this programme.
records.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.

official_details.application_cycle: Two intakes a year (Spring and Fall), each with two application rounds: first round from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June. Published 2027 Spring windows include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; published 2027 Fall milestones include an NTUT student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027, results announced June 2027 and semester start September 2027.

application_readiness_checklist: Identify which participating university and which specific INTENSE programme you want, because funding, language and nationality rules differ between them.
Check the programme's eligibility window for its Spring or Fall intake - partner universities publish different dates and they do not align.
Confirm you satisfy the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan.

Get CEFR B1 English evidence for an English-taught programme, or TOCFL B1 for a Chinese-taught one.
Have official transcripts of your highest completed degree ready in Chinese or English, or with a certified translation.
Prepare a future career plan, two letters of recommendation, a passport-size photo and the eligibility self-check declaration.
Read the signed internship and employment contract carefully: the stipend duration equals your work-obligation duration and repayment may be requested on breach.
Apply through the participating university's own online portal, not through any central INTENSE site.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the participating university's own deadline, which differs from every other INTENSE programme.
Applying to the wrong intake - Spring and Fall rounds are roughly six months apart and do not coincide.
Not holding the required language level: CEFR B1 for English-taught, TOCFL B1 for Chinese-taught.
Being outside the programme's nationality restriction when it is limited to specific Southeast Asian countries.
Falling outside the top 50% of the class or scoring below 80 on conduct.
Underestimating the employment obligation - it is attached to the stipend and is contractually enforceable.
Assuming the funding package is identical across universities: at least one caps tuition subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above any per-semester cap, where a participating university caps the subsidy (one published cap is NT$50,000 per semester).
The return airfare: only a one-way ticket to Taiwan is covered.
Living costs beyond the monthly stipend of at least NT$10,000, particularly in Taipei.
Any cost of the mandatory internship beyond the published minimum-wage allowance.

records.official_source: National Taiwan University (NTU), Office of International Affairs
records.deadline: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.

records.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
records.program_type: University merit scholarship with a matching-fund structure (university tuition waiver plus a thesis supervisor's research-assistant salary)
records.eligibility_summary: Current international (non-overseas-Chinese, non-Mainland-Chinese) graduate students already enrolled at NTU. Because the award is a matching fund, a graduate student also needs a thesis or dissertation supervisor who is willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form; scholars must pass an annual review to keep the award.

records.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.

Assuming the tuition waiver covers everything: NYCU states dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees are still payable.
Confusing this with the general NYCU International Student Scholarship, which is student-applied and has a flexibly adjusted stipend.

records.name: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries
legacy_titles: MOE Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia
moe elite scholarship for university lecturers from south & southeast asia
records.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan)
records.deadline: There is no single ministry deadline. Applicants apply through the participating university's admission application, and the published application windows have been mid-December to mid-March for Fall entry (National Cheng Kung University's AY2026/27 window was mid-December 2025 to mid-March 2026). After admission results, the university emails the MOE-Elite guidelines, forms and upload links, and applicants must submit by the deadline stated in that email. MOE then announces recipients, around late October for Fall intake and late April for the African Spring intake.
records.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.
records.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
records.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens and current university lecturers (or assistant professors and professors) at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible South or Southeast Asian country, or lecturers meeting the African route, whose teaching position is on hold because of their studies. Applicants must hold an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English and must not already be enrolled in, or hold a retained place at, a Taiwanese university, have studied in Taiwan at the same level, hold another government scholarship, or be an exchange or dual-degree student.
eligibility: Must be a university lecturer, assistant professor or professor currently employed at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible country.

Eligible Southeast and South Asian countries: Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bhutan.

African route: applicants from any African country who are either current university lecturers or professors with an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English, or have at least three years of university researcher experience in an African country with research publications or papers.
Must be a citizen of the country where they hold the teaching position.
The teaching position must be on hold because of the studies.
Must provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English; the African researcher route requires an employment certificate in English plus research publications.
Must not hold Taiwan (R.O.C.) nationality or overseas Chinese student status.

Must not be enrolled in, or hold a retained admission at, a university in Taiwan. This restriction does not apply to a student on course to graduate who is pursuing a next degree, provided they are still a lecturer from a South or Southeast Asian country.
Must not previously have studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level.
Must not be an exchange or dual-degree student under a partnership agreement with an overseas institution.
Must not have received stipends through this programme for more than three years.
Must not be a recipient of any other scholarship or financial assistance from a Taiwan government agency or a foreign government.
Must satisfy the participating university's own admission and English-taught programme requirements.
coverage: Total monthly award of NT$25,000 from MOE.
Tuition and credit fees are paid out of that total award, after which the remaining balance is paid to the student as a monthly stipend.
Stipends may be used for tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodation, internet use and living allowance.
Remaining stipends may not be retained or deferred.
benefits: NT$25,000 per month total award from MOE, of which tuition and credit fees are deducted first.
Full tuition fee subsidy out of the award; Taipei Tech states tuition and fees are subsidised for up to 4 years.

Post-tuition monthly stipend. At Taipei Tech this works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4, because the full tuition is deducted from the total MOE award.
Annual review, with enrolment procedures to be completed every semester to keep the scholarship continuous.
required_documents: Up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English (mandatory for lecturers)
For the African researcher route: Employment Certificate in English plus research publications
The MOE-Elite online application form, completed via the link emailed by the university's Office of International Affairs
Regular university registration and tuition payment documents
application_method: Apply for admission to the participating university, choosing a full English-taught programme where required, and indicate the scholarship track in the admission application where the university provides one.
After admission results are announced, the university's Office of International Affairs emails the MOE-Elite guidelines, forms and upload links to eligible admitted students.
Complete the online application form via the emailed link and upload the Lecturer Certificate and all other required documents before the deadline stated in the email.
Complete regular university registration and tuition payment during the tuition payment period.
MOE reviews all applications and announces recipients; the university notifies selected students and shares the stipend plan.
Confirm the six-month stipend plan by email, after which the stipend is disbursed monthly.
records.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.
records.english_requirement: Not an English-language test requirement. The scholarship supports study in full English-taught programmes, and participating universities require applicants to choose a full English-taught programme where applicable, with courses taught in English rather than merely enough English courses to meet credit requirements.
requirements: Hold a current university lecturer, assistant professor or professor post at an institution in an eligible country.
Provide an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English.
Have the teaching position on hold because of the studies.
Apply to a participating university and, where required, choose a full English-taught programme.
Submit the MOE-Elite form and documents by the deadline stated in the university's post-admission email.
Complete enrolment procedures every semester to keep the two or three-year scholarship continuous.
Apply for renewal each year, subject to review.
records.best_fit: University lecturers, assistant professors and professors from South and Southeast Asian or African countries who have secured an offer from a participating Taiwanese university, whose institution can place their post on hold, and who hold an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate.
records.notes: Critical money nuance: NT$25,000 per month is the TOTAL award, not the amount in the student's pocket. Participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total first and split only the remainder into a monthly stipend. Taipei Tech publishes the resulting figures as around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4. Applicants should not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income. Duration also varies by university: the standard MOE terms are 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate with annual review, while Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years and restricts it to newly admitted PhD students. The scheme is quota-limited at 100 places per academic year, and waitlisted candidates approved by MOE must repay any previously disbursed stipends. Do not confuse this with MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program, which pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NT$40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 or NT$20,000.
records.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.

official_details.application_cycle: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle. Published Fall application windows run from around mid-December to mid-March (National Cheng Kung University's AY2026/27 window was mid-December 2025 to mid-March 2026). After admission, the university emails MOE-Elite guidelines and upload links around early August for Fall intake and late January for the African Spring intake, with a separate post-admission document deadline. MOE announces recipients around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 cycle has closed and the next Fall window is expected to open around mid-December 2026.
official_details.deadline_note: The Ministry of Education publishes no standalone application deadline for this programme. Deadlines are set by each participating university: the admission application window has run from around mid-December to mid-March for Fall entry, and a second, post-admission document deadline is stated in the university's own email to admitted students, as published by Taipei Tech: 'Eligible students must submit an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate (English version) and other required documents by the deadline specified in the email'. MOE's recipient announcement also falls on a university-dependent schedule (late October for Fall, late April for the African Spring intake). deadline_date is therefore null and the precision is 'varies'.
official_details.status_note: The AY2026/27 Fall application window closed in mid-March 2026 and MOE had announced its Fall recipients by late October 2026, so that cycle is complete. The next Fall intake window is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry, so the award is upcoming.
official_details.funding_duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually; Taipei Tech's implementation runs the award for up to 4 years with the fourth year at NT$12,000 per month. Enrolment procedures must be completed every semester to keep the scholarship continuous.
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition and credit fees are covered out of the award rather than in addition to it. Taipei Tech states the full tuition amount is deducted from the total MOE-Elite scholarship and the remainder is divided into a six-month stipend plan; it publishes a full tuition fee subsidy of up to 4 years. Note that at least one participating university states students still pay tuition at the local-student rate, so the exact treatment should be confirmed with the admitting university.
official_details.funding_label: Fully funded, but the NT$25,000 per month is the total award: participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from it first and pay the remainder as the student's monthly stipend (published example at Taipei Tech: around NT$14,000 per month in years 1-3 and NT$12,000 in year 4). Stipends may be applied to tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodation, internet and living allowance. Unspent stipend may not be retained or deferred.

Stipend usable for tuition and miscellaneous fees, thesis supervision, insurance, accommodation, internet and living allowance.

Eligible Southeast and South Asian countries: Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan.

African route: current lecturer or professor in any African country with an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, or at least three years of university researcher experience in an African country with research publications.
Must be a citizen of the country where the teaching position is held.
The teaching position must be on hold because of the studies.

MOE reviews and announces recipients, after which the student confirms the six-month stipend plan.

official_details.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program, created by Taiwan's Ministry of Education under the New Southbound Policy, funds university lecturers from South, Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must hold a current lecturer or more senior post in an eligible country with the position on hold, supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through a participating university, which submits the case for MOE review under a quota of about 100 places per academic year.
official_details.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)
official_details.coverage: NT$25,000 per month total award from MOE, from which tuition and credit fees are deducted before the remainder is paid as the student's monthly stipend (published example: around NT$14,000 per month for years 1-3 and NT$12,000 in year 4 at Taipei Tech). Standard term is 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate, reviewed annually; some universities extend this. No airfare or separate insurance funding is stated.

Confirm you hold no other scholarship or financial assistance from a Taiwan government agency or a foreign government.
Confirm you have not studied in Taiwan at the same level and are not an exchange or dual-degree student.
Choose a participating university with a full English-taught graduate programme, and note that priority goes to doctoral study.
Apply within the university's admission window, published as roughly mid-December to mid-March for Fall entry.
Watch for the university's post-admission email with the MOE-Elite guidelines, form and upload links, and submit everything by the deadline stated in that email.
Complete normal university registration and tuition payment during the payment period.
Review and confirm the six-month stipend plan by email once MOE announces the recipient list.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the Lecturer Certificate, or supplying an out-of-date one.
Holding another government scholarship, which is an outright exclusion.
Being unable to place the teaching post on hold, which the programme requires.
Confusing the NT$25,000 total award with take-home pay - tuition is deducted from it first.
Missing the post-admission document deadline, which is separate from the admission deadline and only appears in the university's email.
Already having studied in Taiwan at the same degree level.
Counting on a fourth year, since the standard MOE term is 3 years for a doctorate and only some universities extend it.
Applying to a participating university that does not run this scholarship or that restricts it to particular intakes.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to Taiwan, which is not part of the award.
Anything above the post-deduction monthly stipend, which is significantly lower than the headline NT$25,000 at universities with higher tuition.
Costs for a fourth year of doctoral study at universities that do not extend the award beyond three years.
Costs arising from a waitlist outcome, since previously disbursed stipends may have to be repaid if MOE later approves the candidate.

alerts.trigger: NT$25,000 is the total award, not your stipend
alerts.message: Participating universities deduct full tuition and credit fees from the NT$25,000 total before paying the student. Taipei Tech publishes the outcome as around NT$14,000 per month for years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 in year 4. Do not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income.

There is the university's admission application window (roughly mid-December to mid-March) and then a separate post-admission document deadline stated only in the university's email. Missing the second one forfeits the award even after admission.

Around 100 places are awarded per academic year over a three-year cycle, so entry is quota-limited, priority goes to doctoral study, and waitlisted candidates who are later approved may have to repay stipends already received.

Do not confuse this with MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program, which pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NT$40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 or NT$20,000 and is open to a different applicant pool.

Apply for admission during the university's published window, indicating the scholarship track if the university offers one.
After admission results, receive the OIA email with MOE-Elite guidelines, the form and upload links.
Complete the online form, upload the Lecturer Certificate and other documents, and finish registration and tuition payment by the stated deadlines.
Await MOE's recipient announcement around late October (Fall) or late April (African Spring).
Review and confirm the six-month stipend plan by email, then receive monthly disbursements.
Apply for annual renewal in the announced period with your transcript and publication evidence.

records.notes: Programme statistics published by KI: 1,002 applicants and 12 awardees in 2026; 687 applicants and 10 awardees in 2025. KI notes that scholarship applications are submitted before admission results are published, so applicant numbers are higher than the number of admitted students and should not be read as the number of eligible candidates. In 2026 a total of 484 fee-paying students were admitted to KI's master's programmes.
records.description: The KI Global Master's Scholarship is awarded by Karolinska Institutet to tuition fee-paying students admitted to one of its global master's programmes, with the award distributed across all global master's programmes and decided on the merit rating from the KI CV form, where the highest-rated applicant in each programme wins and ties are resolved by lottery. The scholarship covers tuition fees only - living expenses, accommodation and travel must be funded by the student. Applicants must rank a KI programme as their first choice, remain eligible even if admitted to a lower-ranked KI option, and be admitted, since only admitted students enter the final selection. The joint programmes in Molecular Techniques in Life Science and Biostatistics and Data Science are excluded. The published application window for the 2027 cycle is 8 to 24 February 2027, with results on 26 April 2027 and an acceptance deadline of 30 April 2027.

records.description: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is a Swedish Institute programme for master's studies at Swedish universities, aimed at citizens of 34 eligible countries outside the EU/EEA and Sweden who are liable to pay tuition fees. It is fully funded: SI pays the full tuition fee directly to the university each semester, pays a monthly allowance of SEK 12,000, and makes a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000 (SEK 10,000 for applicants from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Ukraine). Applicants must first secure a place on an eligible English-taught master's programme through University Admissions and then submit a separate SI application in a two-week February window. Scholars join the SI Network for Global Professionals during their studies and the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards.

official_details.description: The SI Scholarship for Global Professionals is the Swedish Institute's fully funded master's scholarship for global professionals from 34 eligible countries. It covers the full tuition fee of an eligible English-taught Swedish master's programme, a SEK 12,000 monthly living allowance and a one-time travel grant of SEK 15,000, and includes membership of the SI Network for Global Professionals during the study period and the Sweden Alumni Network afterwards. Applicants must first be admitted to an eligible programme through University Admissions, then submit a separate SI application in a two-week window each February. The scholarship does not cover insurance, grants for family members or the University Admissions application fee, and it does not permit programme changes or extensions.

records.description: The University of Auckland International Student Excellence Scholarship is a tuition fee credit of up to 25% of one year of tuition fees for new international master's students at Waipapa Taumata Rau. There is no separate application: eligible students who hold a conditional or unconditional programme offer by 20 October 2026 are invited by the Scholarships Office on 21 October 2026 to complete a supplementary application form, which must be submitted by 4 November 2026. Applicants must be international students with an Admissions GPE of at least 7.0 and must complete at least two consecutive semesters of study or repay the value. The award is made on the recommendation of a selection committee and granted by the Vice-Chancellor.

official_details.deadline_central_display: Supplementary application forms must be submitted online by 4 November 2026 to be considered
official_details.deadline_note: No open application exists at the time of verification: invitations are issued on 21 October 2026 only to students who already hold a conditional or unconditional programme offer by 20 October 2026. The scholarship is offered twice a year; the Semester One / Quarter Two 2027 round is the next applicable cycle.
official_details.status_note: Cycle not yet open on 2026-10-04. Invitations go out 21 October 2026 and the supplementary application window closes 4 November 2026. Successful applicants are notified from 30 November 2026 and waitlisted applicants from 14 December 2026.
official_details.funding_duration: One year of full-time enrolment (one year of FTE)
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Partial tuition coverage only: the regulations state the scholarship comprises "A tuition fees credit of up to 25% of the recipients tuition fees for the first two semesters of their masters degree." Living costs, fees and travel are not covered.
official_details.funding_label: Tuition fee credit of up to 25% of one year of tuition fees; not a full tuition waiver and no living-cost stipend

official_details.description: The University of Auckland International Student Excellence Scholarship provides a tuition fees credit of up to 25% of one year of tuition fees to new international master's students at Waipapa Taumata Rau. Applicants do not apply directly: those holding a conditional or unconditional programme offer for Semester One or Quarter Two 2027 by 20 October 2026 are invited on 21 October 2026 to complete a supplementary application form, due 4 November 2026. Eligibility requires an Admissions GPE of at least 7.0 and exclusion of prior study at the University, prior tertiary study in New Zealand (other than exchange), distance enrolment, and most Graduate School of Management programmes. Selection is by a committee recommendation to the Vice-Chancellor on academic merit and personal statement, and recipients must complete at least two consecutive semesters or repay the value.

records.deadline: The scheme runs four awarding rounds each year. In the 2027 dates table the next applicable round is "Apply by 1 November 2026"; the record page also lists the closing dates as 1 February, 1 May, 1 August and 1 November.

There is no separate scholarship application: the candidate indicates in the doctoral programme application that they wish to be considered for the scholarship, and must not enrol in the programme before scholarship consideration has concluded and the outcome has been advised.

Not enrol in the doctoral programme before the University has considered you for the scholarship and advised you of the outcome

Compulsory tuition fees and Student Services Fee for prescribed study in the doctoral programme, up to 42 months FTE

Guaranteed scholarships exist for Māori and Pacific applicants with a New Zealand university qualifying programme GPA of 7.0 or above who are offered a place in a doctoral programme.

records.description: The University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship is a competitive scheme run in four awarding rounds each year for high-achieving candidates applying for admission to an approved doctoral programme at Waipapa Taumata Rau. In 2026 it provides a tax-free stipend of $35,468 per annum with an annual CPI adjustment for up to 42 months full-time equivalent, compulsory tuition fees and the Student Services Fee for the same period, and the single student health insurance charge where applicable. No separate scholarship application is needed — the candidate confirms in the doctoral programme application that they wish to be considered, and must not enrol before the outcome is advised. records.duration: One year
records.funding_period: one-year tenure, paid as a single tuition fee credit
records.deadline: Opening date 1 May in year prior to study for offshore students, 1 July for onshore students. Closing dates 10 December for semester 1 (February) start, 30 April for semester 2 (July) start for offshore students, 15 August for onshore students.
records.application_period: Applications open 1 May in the year prior to study for offshore students (1 July for onshore students) and close 10 December for a Semester 1 (February) start, or 30 April for a Semester 2 (July) start for offshore students.
records.eligibility_summary: New international students from nominated countries who hold a passport from Bangladesh, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam and are commencing full-time undergraduate degree-level study at the University of Otago from 100 level through to degree. Applicants must be studying on campus throughout their studies and cannot be sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand government.

records.description: The University of Otago Global Scholarships provide NZD $15,000 towards tuition fees to new international Bachelor degree students who hold a passport from one of twelve nominated countries — Bangladesh, China, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Macau, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are automatically assessed during the admission process and must tick the agreement to be considered for international scholarships in their eVision application for study. The scholarship is paid only as a credit towards tuition fees with a one-year tenure, is not deferrable, and becomes invalid if study does not commence by the enrolment date in the Offer of Place. Applicants must study on campus, and students sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand government are not eligible.

records.description: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program), previously the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents, is the postgraduate scholarship of the Alliance of National and International Science Organizations for the Belt and Road Regions (ANSO), sponsored by the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and administered at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) for master's and PhD study. The 2026 call opened for application on 15 October 2025 and closed for applicants and referees on 31 January 2026 Beijing Time; results were announced in June 2026 and the 2027 call was not yet published on 2026-10-04. The 2026 coverage table published on the call page lists tuition waiver, a monthly stipend of CNY 6,000 or 7,000 for PhD candidates and CNY 3,000 for master's candidates, health insurance, application fee waiver, one international travel allowance and a one-time visa/residence permit allowance. A sub-category, the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship, selects up to 40 PhD students from developing countries each year, with 10 scholarships prioritised for recipients engaged in climate-related research.
records.duration: PhD: monthly stipend for up to 48 months. Master's: monthly stipend for up to 36 months. The official page states the scholarship duration explicitly in the Admission Notice.
records.deadline: Deadline for Applicants and Referees: 31st January 2026 (Beijing Time) for the 2026 cycle, which has now closed. The 2027 call was not published on the UCAS site on 2026-10-04.
records.application_period: 15 October 2025 to 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time) for the 2026 cycle. The 2027 window was not published on 2026-10-04.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must not hold Chinese citizenship, must hold a valid foreign passport, must be proficient in English or Chinese, and must meet the UCAS admission criteria for international students. Master's applicants must be born after 1 January 1996 (inclusive) and PhD applicants after 1 January 1991 (inclusive). Applicants currently pursuing a master's or doctoral degree at any institution in China are barred from the corresponding level of this scholarship, and applying through both USTC and UCAS simultaneously leads to disqualification.

official_details.description: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (Degree Program), launched in 2019 as the ANSO Scholarship for Young Talents, trains young scientists from all over the world through postgraduate study. CAS is the major sponsor; the degree program supports 100 to 200 master's students and 300 PhD students every year at USTC, UCAS and CAS institutes. UCAS is responsible for the enrolment and management of the master's and doctoral candidates it admits. The 2026 coverage table published by UCAS itemises tuition waiver, a degree-level-dependent monthly stipend, health insurance, application fee waiver, one international travel allowance and a one-time visa/residence permit allowance.

official_details.coverage: Tuition waiver, monthly stipend, health insurance, application fee waiver, international travel allowance, one-time visa/residence permit allowance

records.program_type: Government scholarship administered by the China Scholarship Council, Type B (university nomination), awarded through Peking University
records.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship for Advanced Graduate Program is a merit-based award from the China Scholarship Council for international students with outstanding academic backgrounds, awarded through Peking University under Type B. Peking University's 2026 notice states the scope as 'Full or partial tuition waiver, living stipend, housing, and medical insurance' for a duration of 2 to 3 years at master's level and 4 to 5 years at doctoral level. Applicants must first secure admission to a self-funded full-time international graduate programme and then apply twice: once in the Peking University International Student Service System and once in the China Scholarship Council system. The 2026 cycle closed at 9:00 a.m. Beijing Time on 9 March 2026 for the PKU form and 24:00 Beijing Time on 17 March 2026 for the CSC form, and the 2027 notice had not been published on 2026-10-04.
records.duration: Master's degree: 2 - 3 years. Doctoral degree: 4 - 5 years. Renewable on an annual basis provided the holder passes the annual scholarship review.
records.deadline: For the 2026 cycle the Peking University online scholarship application was 'open now until Beijing Time at 9:00 a.m. on March 9' and the China Scholarship Council application 'open now until Beijing Time at 24:00 on March 17'. Both dates have passed; the 2027 notice was not published on 2026-10-04.
records.application_period: The standing programme page states 'Application Time: Generally in January and March each year'. The 2026 cycle ran from the notice date of 12 January 2026 to 9 March 2026 (PKU) and 17 March 2026 (CSC).
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must meet the admission requirements for international students of Peking University, must have successfully submitted an application for the current year's full-time self-funded graduate programme as an international student, must not have received any other scholarship from the Chinese government or Peking University (except one-time non-renewable merit awards), and must not be a candidate in a joint training programme.

records.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) funds international students who will study at Japanese national universities as undergraduates. MEXT publishes the terms in the FY2027 Application Guidelines and the application is made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general, or through a university recommendation. The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition at the accepting university and provides round-trip airfare. Under embassy recommendation the scholarship runs for five years including one year of Japanese language training.

official_details.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) is one of seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship programme, awarded by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology of Japan to international students admitted to Japanese national universities. Applicants are selected either by embassy recommendation or by university recommendation. Under embassy recommendation the award covers a monthly scholarship, tuition and round-trip airfare for five years including one year of Japanese language training.
official_details.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme
official_details.coverage: Monthly scholarship of JPY 117,000, tuition exemption at the accepting national university, and round-trip airfare under embassy recommendation

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your age band: applicants must in principle have been born on or after 2 April 2002
Confirm you hold the nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan and that you are not a Japanese national
Ask your Japanese embassy or consulate general for its own application deadline and examination dates - they are not published centrally
Prepare two identical packets (originals and copies) with document numbers 1 to 9 written on each first page
Obtain a medical certificate completed and signed by a physician
Decide your field of study, course and up to three majors from the official table
If you want direct placement, plan to contact universities for a letter of provisional acceptance using the MEXT-specified format only
common_rejection_risks: Missing the embassy deadline, which is set locally and differs by country
Submitting only one packet instead of an original set plus a copy set
Untranslated documents, or documents not in Japanese or English
Choosing a field, course or major combination that does not exist in the official table
Failing the written academic examination or interview
Not declaring a previous MEXT scholarship award, which makes the applicant ineligible

official_details.description: The NL Scholarship, previously called the Holland Scholarship, is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area who want to do a bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. Study in NL, the official website of Nuffic, states that it "is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences". The award is EUR 5,000 received in the first year of study, and the official page warns that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Applications are made through a participating Dutch institution, which publishes its own deadlines and eligible fields of study.

records.description: The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is the University's main doctoral award, funding PhD and professional doctorate (DClinDent, DMA, DBA, EDd) candidates at the University of Otago in Dunedin, New Zealand. It pays a NZ$34,128 per annum stipend plus a tuition fee waiver for 36 months at the domestic rate, and excludes student services fee and insurance. Up to 153 awards are offered annually to both domestic and international applicants who are seeking their first doctoral qualification. Applications can be submitted at any time and are considered at quarterly rounds in March, June, September and November.

official_details.description: The General Anders Scholarship Programme supports young people of the Polish diaspora in studying full-time first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle Master's degrees in Poland at higher education institutions supervised by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education, the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Culture and Cultural Heritage. Candidates must hold a Pole's Card or have dual Polish and other citizenship and must have completed secondary education outside Poland. Study must be in Polish, excluding double degree, applied linguistics and foreign languages other than Polish philology, and a preparatory Polish-language course may precede the studies. Calls for proposals are published annually by the Director of NAWA, with separate 2026 calls for first-cycle and second-cycle studies.

official_details.description: The Bekker NAWA Programme is run by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange to support the international mobility of PhD students, scientists and academic teachers from Polish scientific units. It funds research fellowships of 3 to 24 months in recognised research centres worldwide, open to all scientific disciplines and to artistic disciplines, with no restriction on the host country. The funding covers the scholarship holder's living expenses during the stay plus a mobility allowance, and can be increased where the grantee has a spouse or underage children, or where the grantee has a severe or moderate disability. For young scientists it can take the form of a postdoctoral fellowship, and for PhD students part of their doctoral education. Applications are submitted in English through NAWA's ICT system; the 2026 call closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time for projects starting between 1 March and 1 October 2027.

records.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme funds international mobility for researchers in medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences connected with Polish institutions, letting them carry out research and work alongside leading specialists in the best medical centres worldwide. Participants choose a teaching, research or clinical track for a stay of one to six months. Eligible applicants are PhD students and doctoral-school participants, doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. The support, described by NAWA as covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel expenses, amounts to up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay, with a one-off PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path whose stay exceeds three months. NAWA's call page still shows the December 2024 edition as the most recent announcement.

records.description: Lund University runs the ARUA Scholarship as part of its global scholarship programme for high-achieving African students who have demonstrated academic excellence at an ARUA member university. Applicants must first apply for an international degree programme at Lund University with Lund as first choice, then apply through a separate Lund scholarship portal that opens by email invitation in early February each year.

official_details.description: The ARUA Scholarship is part of Lund University's global scholarship programme and provides financial support to prospective students who have demonstrated academic excellence at an ARUA member university in Africa. It is selective and merit-based, aimed at African students committed to Lund University. The award covers a percentage of tuition fees up to a maximum of 90%, with the exact percentage dependent on the budget of the relevant programme or faculty, and it does not cover living costs. Applicants must apply for an international degree programme with Lund as first choice and then apply through a separate scholarship portal that opens by email in early February each year, including a one-minute motivation video.
